papers.title: Prevention and management of hormonal crisis in neuroendocrine tumors undergoing PRRT (peptide receptor radionuclide therapy): a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) is an established treatment of advanced well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) expressing somatostatin receptors. Although generally well tolerated, PRRT may precipitate or exacerbate pre-existing hormonal syndromes in patients with functioning NETs, leading to acute endocrine decompensation requiring urgent management. Current recommendations from the most important NET societies for prevention and treatment remain inconsistent, and available evidence is still fragmented. To address this gap, we conducted a comprehensive systematic review of the literature in PubMed, Scopus, and Embase up to May 2025, with the aim of identifying, organizing, and critically appraising the existing evidence on prevention and therapeutic strategies for managing hormonal crises in patients undergoing PRRT. Twenty-eight studies were included, comprising 18 case reports/series, 7 retrospective studies, and 3 prospective studies. Reported events included carcinoid crisis, insulinoma-related hypoglycemia, VIPoma-related secretory crisis, ectopic Cushing syndrome exacerbation, and catecholaminergic crisis in pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma. Carcinoid crisis was the most frequently reported endocrine emergency, with available cohort studies suggesting an incidence ∼1% during PRRT, although definitions and reporting remain heterogeneous. Hypoglycemic crises occurred mainly during the first PRRT cycle in patients with insulinoma, supporting the role of inpatient monitoring and preventive glucose-stabilizing strategies. Evidence for rarer syndromes was limited to small series and case reports but consistently emphasized pretreatment endocrine optimization, syndrome-specific prophylaxis, early recognition, and multidisciplinary management. Overall, available data remain insufficient to support firm recommendations but suggest that structured risk assessment, periprocedural monitoring, and harmonized management algorithms are essential to improve PRRT safety in functioning NETs.

papers.title: Sertoli-Leydig Cell Tumour With Heterologous Elements Presenting as Hyperandrogenaemia and Markedly Elevated Alpha-Fetoprotein: A Challenging Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumours (SLCTs) are rare ovarian sex cord-stromal tumours that classically present with features of virilisation due to androgen excess and are frequently misdiagnosed as polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS). We report a case of a 33-year-old woman with a three-year history of progressive hirsutism, weight gain, and secondary amenorrhoea, initially attributed to PCOS. An incidental pelvic ultrasound arranged in the context of an endocrinology review revealed a large complex solid-cystic mass measuring 21.2 × 13.8 × 23.4 cm. Tumour markers demonstrated a markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) of 8,147 KU/L, raising initial suspicion of a yolk sac (germ cell) tumour. CT imaging confirmed a 23 cm predominantly cystic pelvic mass with no evidence of metastatic disease. Following multi-disciplinary team discussion and referral to a specialist germ cell tumour MDT, the patient underwent laparotomy and left salpingo-oophorectomy. Initial histology reported an immature teratoma; however, following expert second-opinion review by Professor McCluggage, the final diagnosis was revised to a moderately to poorly differentiated SLCT with heterologous intestinal-type mucinous elements and a small carcinoid component. Ascitic fluid cytology demonstrated no malignant cells. This case highlights the risk of anchoring bias in attributing hyperandrogenaemia to PCOS, the capacity of SLCT with heterologous mucinous elements to mimic germ cell tumours biochemically and histologically, and the indispensable role of expert pathological review in rare ovarian tumours.

papers.title: Spatial epigenomics reveals stromal niche-associated regulatory programs across pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor grades.
papers.abstract: Non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (NF-PanNETs) account for the majority of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms and exhibit substantial clinical and biological heterogeneity, yet their epigenetic regulation and spatial architecture remain poorly understood. Here, we present an integrative analysis of NF-PanNETs across multiple tumor grades using single-nucleus advent of transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (snATAC-seq) and spatial ATAC-seq. snATAC-seq identified grade-associated chromatin accessibility programs characterized by distinct transcription factor activities, including HNF1A and FOXA2 in low-grade tumors, ETS family factors in intermediate-grade tumors, SNAI-associated regulatory programs in high-grade tumors, and CEBPB- and TOX-associated immune states. Spatial ATAC-seq revealed spatially coordinated tumor-stroma interactions, with stroma-proximal regions enriched for MYC/FOX-associated proliferative programs and distal regions exhibiting SNAI-enriched invasive programs. Together, our study provides a spatially resolved epigenomic atlas of NF-PanNETs across tumor grades, offering a resource for understanding epigenetic heterogeneity and generating hypotheses regarding regulatory programs and tumor-stroma interactions for future functional and clinical investigation.

papers.title: Retroviral Transduction of Human T Cells with a Chimeric Antigen Receptor Targeting PD-1 Ligands for Melanoma Immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: T cells are able to target melanoma-associated antigens in an MHC-independent manner through the expression of chimeric antigen receptors. Using retroviral transduction, these receptor constructs can be efficiently delivered into human CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells. In this protocol, we describe the production of retroviral supernatants along with the activation, transduction, expansion, and selection of human T cells engineered to express a chimeric PD-1 receptor. This method can be readily adapted for any human chimeric antigen receptor construct.

papers.title: Generation of Murine Chimeric Antigen Receptor T Cells for Adoptive T Cell Therapy for Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Expression of chimeric antigen receptors enables T cells to be redirected toward melanoma-associated antigens in an MHC-independent manner. Retroviral transduction can be used to introduce these receptor constructs into murine CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells. Here, we outline the generation of retroviral supernatants and the activation, transduction, expansion, and selection of murine T cells expressing the chimeric-PD1 receptor. This protocol can be adapted for any murine chimeric antigen receptor construct.

papers.title: Assessing the Antitumor Immune Effects of Gut Microbiota in a Preclinical Melanoma Model.
papers.abstract: Antitumor immune responses are regulated by a multitude of factors, including the gut microbiota. Specific bacterial taxa and metabolites have been correlated with improved responses to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy in melanoma patients. Gut microbiota and microbiota-derived metabolites can modulate antitumor immune responses by increasing antigen presentation capabilities and enhancing cytotoxic T-cell effector functions. To assess the effects of gut microbiota on antitumor immune responses, we optimized the following protocols focused on immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy in a preclinical melanoma model. Analysis of tumor-infiltrating and circulating lymphocytes, bacterial translocation and growth, and immune cell activation provides a foundation for microbiota/cancer immunology research.

papers.title: Lipoplex Nanoparticle-Based RNA Delivery to 3D Melanoma Spheroids.
papers.abstract: Lipoplex nanoparticle-based vaccination technologies have shown tremendous efficiency for in vivo transfection during the COVID-19 pandemic and also hold promise for treating melanoma. While pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics need careful in vivo and clinical testing, other parameters of drug performance can be assessed with in vitro systems as well. Spheroids composed of more than one cell type can serve to assess drug penetration, cell-type specificity, and transfection efficiency at an early stage of drug development.

papers.title: In Vivo Reversible Electroporation for Melanoma Therapy.
papers.abstract: Reversible Electroporation (rEP) has been a venerable in vitro lab technique for the transfection of cells. Recent in vivo applications of rEP for manipulating tumors and forcing tumor cell expression of proteins of interest are being explored in clinical trials. The ability to perform in vivo rEP in the lab can create translational opportunities and study mechanisms for optimal outcomes in patients. A general protocol is described and may serve as a template for melanoma researchers.

papers.title: Characterization of an Anti-Tryptophan 2,3-Dioxygenase Monoclonal Antibody and Use in a Melanoma Model.
papers.abstract: Monoclonal antibodies have served as research tools to characterize specific proteins and biomolecules to understand their role in biological processes and disease. However, because of nonspecific reactivity with other components in samples, specific reactivity can be difficult to interpret. Using web-based tools, standard hybridoma technology, and standard immunostaining methods, we describe the development of a tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase 2 (TDO2)-targeted antibody with high specificity. In addition to providing a unique reagent needed as a research tool to investigate the role of TDO2 in preclinical models and human tissue samples, herein we provide methods to characterize TDO2 expression in human tissue samples and murine disease models. We note also that the general protocol described in this chapter will be useful to investigators interested in developing monoclonal antibodies against other targets of interest as well.

papers.title: High-Throughput Identification of miRNA-Target Interactions in Melanoma Using miR-CATCHv2.0.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) have the potential to regulate the expression of nearly every transcript in the cell, making the identification of miRNA-mRNA target interactions crucial for understanding their role in diverse biological processes. However, the identification of the miRNAs that regulate a given mRNA remains a challenge. Here, we describe miR-CATCHv2.0, an innovative method for the high-throughput identification of the miRNAs physically interacting with an mRNA of interest. We further highlight how miR-CATCHv2.0 overcomes key limitations of both current computational predictions and existing experimental strategies, enabling a more accurate and comprehensive characterization of physiologically relevant miRNA-mRNA interactions.

papers.title: Assessment of Cell-Free MicroRNA by NGS Whole Transcriptome Analysis in Cutaneous Melanoma Patients' Blood.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRs) are small RNA molecules (18-22 nucleotides) that regulate the transcriptome at a post-transcriptional level by affecting the expression of specific genes. This regulatory mechanism is critical to maintain cell homeostasis and specific functions. Aberrant expression of miRs has been associated with pathobiological processes, including cancer. There are few technologies available that are able to profile whole-genome miR expression using minimal amounts of blood samples and without the need for time-consuming extraction steps. Here, we describe the HTG EdgeSeq miR Whole Transcriptome Assay (WTA) in serum and plasma samples. To identify specific cell-free miR (cfmiR) patterns, we have first focused on the analysis of normal donor samples and have then compared these to patients with cutaneous melanoma. The identification of specific cfmiR for melanoma patients will allow for better patient surveillance during targeted and/or checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy (CII) treatment.

papers.title: Unbiased Microbiome and Metabolomic Profiling of Fecal Samples from Patients with Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiota influence and modulate host immune responses. In preclinical cancer models, mice lacking gut microbiota have a markedly diminished response to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. Further, in melanoma patients, specific commensal gut microbiota have been associated with a positive clinical response to immunotherapy. In order to study the gut microbiome and metabolome, we have developed methods for fecal sample collection and processing, microbiome and metabolome profiling, and bioinformatic analysis. This protocol will be a useful tool for interrogating the taxonomic composition and functional output of a melanoma patient's gut microbiome.

papers.title: Discovery of Salivary Metabolomic Biomarkers for Canine Oral Melanoma and Squamous Cell Carcinoma via CIL LC-MS Analysis.
papers.abstract: In this case-control cross-sectional study, we examined the diagnostic potential of salivary metabolomics to differentiate canine oral melanoma (OM) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) from benign oral tumors (BN). Using high-performance chemical isotope labeling liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (CIL LC-MS) targeting at the amine/phenol submetabolome, we analyzed saliva from 65 dogs across malignant, benign, and healthy groups. Our results revealed distinct metabolic clustering among the groups, identifying 154 significantly altered metabolites in OM and 66 in OSCC compared to BN (Padj < 0.05). Notable biomarkers included elevated tryptophyl-threonine and decreased 1,2-dihydroxynaphthalene-6-sulfonic acid in OM, while OSCC was characterized by reduced seryl-arginine and sarcosine. These findings, and the protocol described herein that was used to obtain them, demonstrate the broad coverage of the salivary submetabolome and emphasize the potential of noninvasive metabolic profiling as a practical, high-throughput approach for accurate diagnosis of canine oral cancers in clinical settings.

papers.title: Serum Peptidomic Profiling for Biomarker Discovery in Canine Oral Melanoma and Squamous Cell Carcinoma via MALDI-TOF and LC-MS/MS.
papers.abstract: Canine oral malignancies, particularly oral melanoma (OM) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), present significant diagnostic hurdles due to their aggressive metastasis and the difficulty of early-stage detection. This study establishes a robust methodological workflow for identifying systemic biomarkers by analyzing the serum peptidome, a minimally invasive alternative to traditional tissue biopsies. Using a high-throughput approach that combines matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) for rapid screening with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) for precise peptide identification, we successfully differentiated early and late-stage malignancies from benign and healthy controls. Principal component analysis confirmed distinct peptidomic clusters, leading to the identification of four key proteins: FKBP4, ESRRA, IGSF10, and ABCB5. Notably, FKBP4, ESRRA, and ABCB5 were overexpressed in both late-stage OM and late-stage OSCC, while IGSF10 showed specificity for late-stage OSCC. These markers are integral to metastatic pathways and correlate with chemotherapeutic sensitivity, providing a foundation for precision diagnostic and prognostic protocols in veterinary oncology.

papers.title: Integrated Functional and Metabolomic Profiling of Melanoma Cells Treated with Redox-Active Compounds.
papers.abstract: Metabolic plasticity is a hallmark of melanoma progression and therapy resistance. This chapter describes a reproducible protocol for comprehensive metabolic profiling of melanoma cells exposed to redox-active compounds such as emodin and aloe-emodin. The method integrates cell proliferation assays, mitochondrial functional analysis using Seahorse extracellular flux measurements, reactive oxygen species (ROS) quantification, LC-MS-based metabolomics, stable-isotope tracing, and 13C metabolic flux analysis (13C-MFA). The workflow enables quantitative characterization of treatment-induced alterations in energy metabolism, redox balance, and central carbon fluxes in melanoma cell lines with distinct metabolic phenotypes. The procedures are presented in a step-by-step format suitable for researchers unfamiliar with the individual techniques and can be adapted to other cancer models or metabolic perturbations.

papers.title: Methods for Analyzing Immune Infiltrates and Spatial Organization Within the Melanoma Microenvironment Using Multiplex Immunofluorescence.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapies improve survival in patients with melanoma by enhancing the immune system's ability to recognize and eliminate tumor cells. Understanding the immunological effects of these therapies requires evaluation of both changes in lymphocyte composition and activation within the tumor microenvironment (TME) as well as the spatial organization of these cells. Increased lymphocyte infiltration and distinct patterns of immune cell distribution within the TME have been associated with improved survival and enhanced response to immunotherapy in melanoma. However, relatively few methodologies currently enable detailed characterization of both the structural organization and immunological features of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes. In this chapter, we describe multiplex immunofluorescence staining approaches for the identification, characterization, and quantification of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in melanoma.

papers.title: A Method for Quantifying Immune Infiltrates and Tertiary Lymphoid Structures in Murine Melanoma Tumors by Multiplex Immunofluorescence.
papers.abstract: The presence of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and elevated levels of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes have been linked to improved survival outcomes in several solid cancers, including melanoma. Despite this association, the precise function and immunological impact of TLS remain incompletely understood, as do factors that drive their formation and which might potentially be leveraged to enhance patient outcomes. Functional studies using murine models may help clarify the biological roles of TLS; however, relatively few methodologies currently exist that allow for detailed assessment of the structural organization and functional characteristics of TLS within solid tumors. To advance understanding of the biology underlying TLS, this chapter describes multiplex immunohistochemistry panels designed for the identification, characterization, and quantification of TLS and intratumoral immune infiltrates in melanoma. Although these methods are presented in the context of melanoma, they are broadly applicable and can be used to investigate TLS across a wide range of human cancers.

papers.title: Preparation of Melanoma Tissue for Multiplex Immunofluorescence Histology Analysis of Immune Infiltration and Spatial Organization.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapies extend survival in melanoma patients by increasing the immune system's capacity to detect tumors and mediate tumor cell death. Understanding mechanisms of antitumor immunity requires evaluating changes in immune infiltrate composition, activation, and spatial distribution within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Despite this need, relatively few methods allow for detailed analysis of both the structural organization and immunological characteristics of tumor-infiltrating immune cells in preclinical cancer models. In this chapter, we present a multiplex immunofluorescence staining approach for identifying, characterizing, and quantifying tumor-infiltrating immune cells in murine melanoma, allowing evaluation of how therapies influence immune infiltration in preclinical models.

papers.title: PET Imaging of Melanoma Using a Melanocortin 1 Receptor-Targeted Probe.
papers.abstract: The melanocortin-1 receptor (MC1R) is overexpressed in more than 80% of melanoma cells but is expressed at low levels in normal tissues, making it an important target for melanoma imaging and therapy. Recently, MC1R has attracted the interest of numerous researchers as a target for melanoma. Radiolabeled alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) peptides bind specifically to MC1R and internalize into tumor cells, enabling melanoma diagnosis and therapy. Several radiolabeled α-MSH peptides have been developed. Among those, a cyclized α-MSH peptide produced via an alternative click chemistry cyclization strategy offers faster and more specific bindings to MC1R. It could be labeled with ²0³Pb/²¹²Pb (VMT01) for melanoma single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) imaging and therapy and also could be labeled with 68Ga (VMT02) for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. Preliminary clinical imaging showed highly sensitive and specific melanoma detection. This chapter describes the synthesis of VMT02 and PET/CT imaging procedures in both mouse models and patients.

papers.title: SPECT Imaging of Melanoma Using a 99mTc-Labeled Melanin-Targeted Probe.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is a highly aggressive cutaneous malignancy characterized by a poor clinical prognosis, making early and accurate detection paramount for patient survival. Melanin, abundantly expressed in most melanoma lesions, serves as an ideal and highly specific biomarker for targeted molecular imaging. While various imaging modalities exist, single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) provides a highly accessible and cost-effective strategy for widespread clinical translation. From our recent studies, 99mTc-SMIC-4006 emerged as the optimal 99mTc-labeled radiotracer, demonstrating exceptional radiochemical purity, highly specific melanin binding, and superior tumor-to-blood contrast in B16F10 melanoma xenografts. Herein, we describe the detailed radiosynthesis protocol for 99mTc-SMIC-4006, alongside comprehensive procedures for its in vitro property evaluation and in vivo SPECT/CT imaging in preclinical melanoma models.

papers.title: PET Imaging of Melanoma Using a Melanin-Targeted Probe.
papers.abstract: Melanin exists in most melanoma lesions. Melanin plays an important role in melanoma progression, metastasis, therapy response, and the overall survival of patients. Therefore, melanin is a critical target for melanoma diagnosis and therapy. Many melanin-targeting probes, such as radioisotope-labeled benzamide analogs, have been developed for melanoma diagnosis using positron emission tomography (PET). The N-(2-(diethylamino)-ethyl)-18F-5-fluoropicolinamide (18F-P3BZA) probe is one of the benzamide analogs and has been preliminarily tested for clinical diagnosis of melanoma in our recent studies. It has shown high specificity and favorable in vivo performance for PET imaging of melanoma. Herein, we describe the detailed synthesis protocol of 18F-P3BZA and the PET/CT imaging procedure for animal models and patients.

papers.title: Radiopharmaceuticals for Melanoma Theranostics.
papers.abstract: Malignant melanoma (MM) remains a formidable clinical challenge due to its high metastatic potential and the eventual emergence of resistance to current BRAF/MEK and immune checkpoint inhibitors. To address these limitations, the theranostic strategy integrating diagnostic imaging with targeted radionuclide therapy to enable personalized treatment has gained significant traction. Current research primarily exploits the overexpression of the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R), very late antigen-4 (VLA-4), and melanin as primary molecular targets for radiopharmaceutical development. For MC1R, α-MSH peptide analogs have been engineered with β-emitters such as 177Lu and 90Y for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT), as well as α-emitters like 225Ac and 212Pb (β- decay to 212Bi and then emit α particles) for targeted alpha therapy (TAT), showing high specificity and rapid clearance. Concurrently, VLA-4-targeted platforms utilizing high-affinity LLP2A ligands have been optimized through PEGylation and albumin-binding strategies to enhance bioavailability and tumor retention. Beyond these primary receptors, this review evaluates alternative strategies, including copper transporter (CTR1) targeting with 64CuCl2 and the use of gold nanocages for multimodal applications. Together, these advancements represent a critical shift toward image-guided, dosimetry-driven radionuclide therapies that may work synergistically with existing immunotherapies to improve survival in metastatic melanoma.

papers.title: Multi-Analyte Responsive Fluorescent Sensing of Pathological Cellular States in Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Melanoma progression involves multiple biomarkers and signaling pathways, and relying on a single marker can lead to incomplete or inaccurate diagnoses. Multi-analyte sensors allow simultaneous monitoring of several biomarkers, providing a more comprehensive picture of the tumor microenvironment, identifying distinct cellular states, and improving diagnostic accuracy. This chapter presents protocols that can be used for fluorescence sensing of the melanoma marker enzyme tyrosinase in conjunction with different In Vitro microenvironmental signals, including hypoxia and reactive oxygen species.

papers.title: Design Strategies for Melanoma-Targeting Fluorescent Probes.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is responsible for most skin cancer-related mortalities, and clinical urgency drives the development of novel diagnostic tools. Precision diagnostics relying on fluorescence output provide many advantages, including easy and noninvasive readout and a high signal-to-noise ratio that is enabled through a change in the intensity or the wavelength of fluorescence in response to disease-associated parameters. This chapter explores the chemical design strategies for fluorescent probes, focusing on the exploitation of melanogenic enzymes, protein biomarkers, and the targeting of the dysregulated tumor microenvironment to achieve unprecedented diagnostic precision.

papers.title: Imaging and Isolation of Extravasation-Participating Endothelial and Melanoma Cells During Angiopellosis.
papers.abstract: Cancer mortality is driven largely by metastatic progression rather than by primary tumor burden. The ability of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) to exit the vasculature and invade surrounding tissues-known as extravasation-is a critical and rate-limiting step in metastasis. Recent advances in high-resolution intravital microscopy have made it possible to directly visualize this process in vivo, enabling real-time imaging of individual CTCs as they interact with, transmigrate through, and recruit components of the endothelium. In this chapter, we describe intravital microscopy approaches that allow for both visualization and isolation of extravasating CTCs, as well as the endothelial cells that actively participate in their transendothelial migration. These methods provide a powerful platform for dissecting the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying metastatic spread. Beyond mechanistic insights, the approach can also serve as a functional screening system for evaluating anticancer therapeutics that target CTC behavior, endothelial interactions, or early metastatic niche formation.

papers.title: Detection of Biomarkers for EMT-Associated Phenotype Switching in Melanoma-Derived Extracellular Vesicles.
papers.abstract: Melanoma cells exhibit epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-like phenotype switching during targeted therapy, which contributes to the development of drug resistance. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by melanoma cells carry surface proteins reflective of this EMT-associated transition, providing an accessible window to track therapeutic response. This chapter presents a step-by-step protocol for profiling EMT-related melanoma EV protein signatures directly from unpurified sera using a microfluidic surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) biosensing platform. The method integrates melanoma-specific EV capture, alternating current-electrohydrodynamic nanomixing-enhanced binding, and multiplex SERS nanotag labeling to enable sensitive quantification of EMT surface markers in a streamlined assay. Detailed instructions for reagent preparation, SERS nanotag synthesis, biosensor fabrication and operation, spectral acquisition, and data processing are provided to support implementation in melanoma translational research laboratories. This protocol enables reproducible monitoring of EMT-like phenotypic evolution in melanoma models and patient samples and may assist future studies aiming to predict or mechanistically dissect resistance to targeted therapy.

papers.title: Imaging and Analysis of Melanoma-Secreted Extracellular Vesicles in Tumor-Draining Lymph Nodes.
papers.abstract: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) are key mediators of intercellular communication and play important roles in both physiological and pathological processes. In cancer, sEVs mediate communication between the tumor and its microenvironment but also contribute to metastatic organotropism and the formation of pre-metastatic niches in regional and distant organs. Lymph nodes (LNs) are central regulators of immune responses and primary sites of early metastasis, and, as such, they are critical targets for understanding cancer progression and improving immunotherapy. sEVs contribute to the conditioning of lymph nodes during pre-metastatic niche formation by altering lymphatic endothelial cell function and modulating immune cell populations, thereby promoting tumor progression. Because these interactions are complex and dynamic, their study requires in vivo models and specifically tailored sEVs-based techniques. In this chapter, we describe several approaches for studying sEVs in the LN context, including biodistribution analysis in the lymphatic system, imaging by immunofluorescence, and uptake measurement by flow cytometry.

papers.title: Post-Lymphadenectomy Analysis of Small Extracellular Vesicles from Lymphatic Drainage/Exudative Seroma of Melanoma Patients.
papers.abstract: Circulating extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as a promising source of disease biomarkers in biofluids. Although multiple isolation methods are available, differential ultracentrifugation remains a gold standard for small EV purification. Small EVs purified using this approach retain functional activity both in vitro and in vivo and are suitable for downstream applications, including proteomics, electron microscopy, mass spectrometry, and nucleic acid analysis. An additional purification step, either by density gradient centrifugation or size-exclusion chromatography, allows for the isolation of highly pure EV fractions for subsequent biomarker analysis. Here, we describe a protocol based on differential ultracentrifugation followed by a density gradient centrifugation or size exclusion chromatography step for the recovery of highly pure small extracellular vesicles (EVs) from lymphatic exudate (seroma) collected following lymphadenectomy, with the aim of supporting biomarker discovery and liquid biopsy applications.

papers.title: A Rapid Exosome Isolation Using Ultrafiltration and Size Exclusion Chromatography (REIUS) Method for Exosome Isolation from Melanoma Cell Lines.
papers.abstract: Cells release extracellular vesicles (EVs) that can be detected both in vivo and in cell culture medium. Among EVs, exosomes are 50-150 nm vesicles that are systematically packaged into multivesicular bodies for release into the external environment. In cancer, these intentionally packaged exosomes carry a payload of molecules such as protein, RNA, and surface receptors that facilitate the reprogramming of proximal cells to assemble a pro-tumor microenvironment. Exosomes have been implicated as an important intermediary extracellular communication pathway between cells, including in melanoma. Human melanoma-derived exosomes (HMEX) have been demonstrated to modulate the extracellular environment and inhibit immune cell activation. There are many methods to isolate and enrich for exosomes, and the method applied can impact yield and purity of the isolates. In this chapter, we describe the REIUS (Rapid Exosome Isolation Using Size exclusion chromatography) method to isolate HMEX from melanoma cell cultures and then demonstrate their enrichment using molecular and microscopic approaches.

papers.title: Capture and Isolation of Circulating Melanoma Cells Using Photoacoustic Flowmetry.
papers.abstract: Early detection of cancer has been a goal of cancer research in general and melanoma research in particular. Early detection of metastasis has been targeted as pivotal to increasing survival rates. Melanoma, though curable in its early stages, has a dramatic decrease in survival rates once metastasis has occurred. The transition to metastasis is not well understood and is an area of increasing interest. Metastasis is always premeditated by the shedding of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from the primary tumor. The ability to isolate rare CTCs from the bloodstream has led to a host of new targets and therapies for cancer. Detection of CTCs also allows for disease progression to be tracked in real time while eliminating the need to wait for additional tumors to grow. Using a photoacoustic flow cytometer, in which we induce ultrasonic responses from circulating melanoma cells (CMCs), we identify and quantify these cells in order to track disease progression. Additionally, these CMCs are captured and isolated, allowing for future analysis such as RNA-Seq or microarray analysis. Finally, anticipating the need to streamline clinical workflow, a method for testing in whole blood is offered.

papers.title: Modeling Proliferative Versus Migratory Melanoma Cell Phenotypes Using Biofabricated Matrices.
papers.abstract: Biofabrication enables the controlled generation of three-dimensional cell cultures that can be highly useful to study different cellular phenotypes. As melanoma cells reveal high plasticity, and the "phenotype switching model" defining the cells as either proliferative or migratory active has been described, we recently developed a 3D bioprinted model mimicking these phenotypes. Here, we describe the generation of these bioprinted models based on either Matrigel or Cellink Bioink, which can be used with various cell lines and which allows for the analysis of cell response on microscopic and molecular levels. This model system offers novel opportunities for fundamental research and drug testing on heterogeneous tumors like melanoma.

papers.title: Skin Organ Constructs for In Vitro Modeling of Melanoma Invasion.
papers.abstract: Melanoma progression from an in situ lesion to an invasive dermal tumor is strongly associated with poor patient prognosis, with depth of invasion serving as a predictor of survival. Increasing evidence indicates that remodeling of the extracellular matrix (ECM) plays a central role in this transition by altering both mechanical and biochemical cues within the tumor microenvironment. To facilitate mechanistic studies of ECM-mediated melanoma invasion, we developed a reproducible in vitro skin organ construct (SOC) model that recapitulates key structural and cellular features of human skin. The SOC system is assembled using a two-layer collagen-based dermal equivalent containing primary human dermal fibroblasts, overlaid with normal human epidermal keratinocytes to generate a stratified epidermis. Melanoma cells are subsequently seeded onto the reconstructed epidermal surface and cultured under defined conditions, including staged modulation of epidermal growth factor and exposure to an air-liquid interface to promote keratinization. The model permits incorporation of defined ECM components or genetically modified melanoma cells to evaluate their impact on tumor invasion. Melanoma progression is assessed by measuring radial growth and quantifying invasion depth and patterns in paraffin-embedded sections using histological and immunohistochemical analyses. This SOC platform provides a physiologically relevant and customizable system to investigate ECM-driven mechanisms of melanoma invasion and to evaluate candidate therapeutic targets that modulate tumor-microenvironment interactions.

papers.title: Evaluating Melanoma Cell Migration/Invasion in Transwell Assays by Flow Cytometry.
papers.abstract: Cell migration and invasion are vital aspects of melanoma biology that are critical to the progression of this aggressive cancer. Numerous in vitro assays are available to study these hallmark properties of cancer, including two-dimensional wound healing ("scratch") and transwell (Boyden chamber) assays, as well as three-dimensional microfluidic-based video microscopy assays and matrix/skin organ construct-based assays. Though each of these assays has unique advantages depending on the experimental question at hand, transwell assays are highly adaptable and thus particularly well-suited for investigating the role of specific stimulators/inhibitors of cancer cell migration and invasion. Traditionally, quantification of migrating/invading cells that are capable of transiting the Boyden chamber utilized in these assays is achieved by manual counting of cells that have reached the bottom chamber or by colorimetric/fluorometric detection of transited cells that were preloaded with specific dyes prior to assay initiation. These approaches, while commonly used, have inherent limitations in their design, including the introduction of quantification artifacts that arise from human error during direct cell counting or uneven/inconsistent cell labeling within/across experiments. To overcome these limitations, we have optimized a non-fluorescent flow cytometry-based assay for quantifying melanoma transwell migration and invasion, and we present herein an application of this assay to assess the role of the FOXC2 transcription factor in these processes.

papers.title: Wound Healing Assay for Melanoma Cell Migration.
papers.abstract: Cell migration is a critical process involved in morphogenesis, inflammation, and cancer metastasis. The wound healing assay is a simple, nonexpensive, and highly reproducible method to study cancer cell migration in vitro. It is based on the observation that cells growing in a monolayer migrate to re-establish cell contacts after the development of an artificial wound. The assay involves creation of a wound in a monolayer, image acquisition during wound closure, and comparison of migrated area at initial and final time points.

papers.title: A Flow Cytometric Assay for Investigating Melanoma Cell Adhesion to Lymphatic Endothelial Cells.
papers.abstract: Lymph node invasion by tumor cells is an important process in the progression of melanoma and is a poor prognostic factor for patients with this cancer. Before they are able to spread to regional lymph nodes, though, melanoma cells must first adhere to lymphatic endothelium and transmigrate into the lymphatic vasculature. In order to study melanoma cell adhesion to lymphatic endothelial cells and the factors that regulate this process, we have developed an in vitro flow cytometry-based assay to measure melanoma cell attachment to lymphatic endothelial cells. This assay will be a useful tool for investigating the interactions that take place between melanoma cells and lymphatic endothelial cells during the adhesion process.

papers.title: Indirect Coculture of Melanoma Cells with Stromal Cells Present in Their Microenvironment as a Method for Evaluation of Their Mutual Interactions.
papers.abstract: A tumor tissue consists not only of cancer cells but also of stromal cells, which often support cancer cell progression. Therefore, oncology research utilizes models that enable the study of cancer cell characteristics in the presence of noncancereous cells that, in vivo, also form the tumor. The following protocol describes the culturing of cancer cells with stromal cells (such as keratinocytes, fibroblasts, and adipocytes) in an indirect coculture model, in which both cell types exchange secretory factors in the culture medium but do not interact directly. This system allows for the assessment of the influence of one cell type on the other without the need to separate them through sorting to conduct further experiments based on only one selected cell type.

papers.title: A Fluorescence-Based Assay for Measuring Glucose Uptake in Living Melanoma Cells.
papers.abstract: Melanoma cells have high glycolytic capacity. Glucose uptake is a key rate-limiting step in glucose utilization. Here we describe a simple protocol for measuring direct glucose uptake in living melanoma cells by flow cytometry.

papers.title: Establishment and Characterization of Model Antigen-Expressing Melanoma Cell Lines.
papers.abstract: Significant advances in our understanding of antitumor immunity over the last two decades have ushered in an exciting era of cancer immunotherapy. During this time, several strategies have been developed to elicit robust antitumor immune responses by CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes. Despite the documented benefits of various approaches aimed at targeting these cells, however, there remains a substantial number of patients who either fail to respond to these regimens or who relapse after an initial response. Therefore, to gain insight into mechanisms of innate and acquired resistance to immune-based therapies for cancer, we must improve our understanding of factors that regulate the induction and maintenance of T cell responses against cancer antigens. In this regard, experimental systems that enable the study of cancer antigen-specific T cells are useful tools for investigating the activation and suppression of antitumor T lymphocytes. To this end, we describe herein a method for generating and characterizing model antigen-expressing melanoma cell lines, and we specifically validate this method using two variants of B16 murine melanoma that we engineered to express the OVA257 epitope of chicken ovalbumin, a model neoantigen against which both natural and T cell receptor (TCR) transgenic OT-I CD8+ T cell responses can be monitored.

papers.title: Generation of Functional Gene Knockout Melanoma Cell Lines by CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in the treatment of metastatic melanoma have emerged only from advances in our understanding of melanoma development and progression at the cellular and molecular level. Despite the impact that such advances have made on the clinical management of this cancer over the last decade, additional insights into factors that promote melanoma progression and therapeutic resistance are needed to combat this disease. CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing technology is a powerful tool for studying gene function in a timely and cost-effective manner, enabling the manipulation of specific DNA sequences via a targeted approach. Herein, we describe a protocol for generating functional gene knockouts in melanoma cell lines by CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, and we present an example application of this protocol for the successful knockout of the Foxc2 transcription factor-encoding gene in the B16-F1 murine melanoma cell line.

papers.title: Model Systems for the Study of Malignant Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Since the first resection of melanoma by Hunter in 1787, efforts to treat patients with this deadly malignancy have been ongoing. Initial work to understand melanoma biology for therapeutics development began with the employment of isolated cancer cells grown in culture. However, these models lack in vivo interactions with the tumor microenvironment. Melanoma cell line transplantation into suitable animals, such as mice, has been informative and useful for testing therapeutics as a pre-clinical model. Injection of freshly isolated patient melanomas into immunodeficient animals has shown the capacity to retain the genetic heterogeneity of the tumors, which is lost during long-term culture of melanoma cells. Upon the advancement of technology, genetically engineered animals have been generated to study the spontaneous development of melanomas in light of newly discovered genetic aberrations associated with melanoma formation. Culturing melanoma cells in a matrix generates tumor spheroids, providing an in vitro environment that promotes the heterogeneity commonplace with human melanoma and displaces the need for animal care facilities. Advanced 3D cultures have been created simulating the structure and cellularity of human skin to permit in vitro testing of therapeutics on melanomas expressing the same phenotype as demonstrated in vivo. This review discusses these models and their relevance to the study of melanomagenesis, growth, metastasis, and therapy.

papers.title: Normal variants, pitfalls, and interpretation challenges of somatostatin receptor PET.
papers.abstract: Somatostatin receptor (SSTR) PET has become a central imaging tool in neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), with established roles in detection, staging, restaging, and selection of patients for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT). Despite its high sensitivity and target specificity, interpretation is not always straightforward. Physiological SSTR expression, focal variants of normal biodistribution, technical and administration-related artifacts, inflammatory conditions, and benign or malignant non-neuroendocrine lesions may all generate uptake that mimics NET involvement. Conversely, small lesion size, partial-volume effects, high physiological background, and genuinely low or absent receptor expression may reduce lesion conspicuity and lead to false-negative or underestimated disease. Interpretive challenges have also become more relevant as SSTR PET is increasingly used for quantitative, longitudinal, and theranostic assessment. Somatostatin analogue treatment can modify normal-organ biodistribution and lesion-to-background contrast, while liver and spleen uptake may vary substantially across serial examinations and should not necessarily be considered stable reference tissues. In addition, inter-lesional differences in receptor expression may have practical implications when SSTR PET is used to assess suitability for PRRT, because intense uptake in part of the disease does not necessarily imply adequate target expression across all clinically relevant lesions. This review summarizes the principal physiological variants and false-positive and false-negative findings encountered on SSTR PET and discusses contemporary pitfalls related to biodistribution, receptor heterogeneity, quantitative interpretation, and theranostic decision-making. Accurate interpretation requires integration of molecular, anatomical, and clinical information rather than reliance on isolated uptake intensity or a binary positive/negative classification.

papers.title: Preoperative normetanephrine levels, but not doxazosin dose, predict intraoperative hemodynamic instability in pheochromocytoma surgery.
papers.abstract: Preoperative α-adrenergic blockade is routinely recommended before adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma to reduce intraoperative hemodynamic instability. However, the need, intensity, and duration of preoperative blockade remain uncertain. This single-center, retrospective study included adult patients who underwent adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma at Karolinska University Hospital between 2014 and 2023. The association between preoperative doxazosin treatment, plasma metanephrine and normetanephrine concentrations, and intraoperative hemodynamic instability was evaluated. Correlation analysis and multivariable linear regression were performed. Thirty-three patients were included (49% female; median age 59 years). Neither preoperative doxazosin dose nor treatment duration was associated with intraoperative systolic blood pressure reduction or intraoperative adenosine requirements. In contrast, higher preoperative metanephrine and normetanephrine concentrations were significantly associated with greater intraoperative vasoactive support requirements and a greater systolic blood pressure reduction after adrenal vein ligation. Tumor size showed a significant positive correlation with normetanephrine concentrations but was not independently associated with intraoperative hemodynamic instability. In multivariate analysis, preoperative normetanephrine concentration remained the only independent predictor of intraoperative reduction in systolic blood pressure after adrenal vein ligation. Preoperative normetanephrine concentration is associated with intraoperative hemodynamic instability in pheochromocytoma surgery, whereas doxazosin dose and treatment duration were not. These findings suggest that biochemical tumor activity may be more clinically relevant than the intensity of preoperative α-blockade when assessing perioperative cardiovascular risk.

papers.title: Germline Pathogenic Variants in Succinate Dehydrogenase Genes: Implications from a Single Institution Study.
papers.abstract: Germline pathogenic variants (PVs) in the succinate dehydrogenase (SDHx) genes are associated with inherited pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma (PPGL). Because of the high incidence of germline PVs, genetic testing is recommended for all cases of PPGL; relatives may thus be found through cascade testing. PPGL-associated genes are also included on cancer genetics panels, which may lead to variant identification related to other tumors. After PV detection, screening recommendations entail biochemical/radiologic testing and frequent surveillance. To assess the consequences and impact of these approaches in a cohort of individuals with germline PVs in the SDHx genes. Natural history study. Single academic medical centerPatients or Other Participants: 156 patients with SDHx PVs collected over 10 years. None. We report distribution of PVs; rationale for genetic screening; tumor incidence, and second genetic variants. Of 156 patients with variants in the SDHx genes, PVs in SDHB were the most common. In probands tested for non-PPGL tumors, SDHA PVs were the most common, whereas SDHD cases were never detected in this manner. We also identified individuals with variants in a second cancer-associated gene. For individuals not found to have a tumor at initial presentation, the rate of tumor development was <5%. SDHx PVs may be more common than expected and there are gene-specific patterns of ascertainment. Future research is needed to evaluate the role of modifier variants on tumor risk. Reconsideration of surveillance guidelines may be appropriate given the low frequency of new lesions in tumor-free carriers.

papers.title: Fertility Treatment and Risk of Melanoma: A Certainty-Rated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of 3,733,499 Women.
papers.abstract: Cancer safety after fertility treatment is well studied for breast and gynaecological tumours, but melanoma risk remains poorly characterized. We synthesized internally controlled evidence on this association. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov (2000-2025) were searched for comparative observational studies of melanoma incidence. The primary outcome was incident melanoma; treatment-pathway/SIR analyses were secondary. Hazard ratios and case-cohort relative risks (rare-disease approximation) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis (REML, Hartung-Knapp) in R; SIRs were synthesized separately. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-E and certainty graded using GRADE. Twelve observational studies (3,733,499 women; 219,357 exposed) were included. ROBINS-E rated no study overall low risk of bias (83% some concerns, 17% high risk), reflecting incomplete ultraviolet-exposure adjustment. Melanoma risk was modestly elevated (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.02-1.50; I2 = 0%; prediction interval 0.97-1.58); drug-only ovulation induction showed a stronger association (HR 1.39, 95% CI 1.01-1.92), while ART/IVF was near-null (HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.81-1.48). Corresponding absolute increases were approximately 3-8, 5-13, and 1-3 per 10,000 women over 10 years (baseline 13.3-33.1/100,000/year). Certainty was very low for any fertility treatment and drug-only treatment, and low for ART/IVF. SIR-based analyses were non-significant and highly heterogeneous (SIR 1.25, 95% CI 0.66-2.38; I2 = 80%). Observed associations are small and of very low to low certainty, reflecting incomplete ultraviolet-exposure and risk-factor adjustment; causality cannot be established. Current evidence does not justify changes in fertility-treatment practice. Future studies require cycle-level exposure data and rigorous ultraviolet-exposure control.

papers.title: Pheochromocytomas with Aggressive Histopathological Features Have Reduced Apelin and Increased VEGF Expression: Diagnostic and Prognostic Implications.
papers.abstract: Background: Pheochromocytoma is a highly vascular neuroendocrine tumor with variable biological behavior. Reliable biomarkers reflecting tumor aggressiveness remain limited. This study evaluated apelin and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression in pheochromocytoma and their associations with histopathological prognostic parameters. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 20 pheochromocytoma patients and 18 normal adrenal medulla controls. Apelin and VEGF expression were evaluated immunohistochemically using the immunoreactivity score (IRS). Associations between IRS values and Pheochromocytoma of the Adrenal Gland Scaled Score (PASS), Grading System for Adrenal Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma (GAPP) score, Ki-67 index, tumor size, clinicopathological characteristics, and individual PASS components were analyzed. Results: Apelin IRS was significantly lower in pheochromocytoma than in normal adrenal medulla (median 0 vs. 4, p = 0.001), whereas VEGF IRS was significantly higher (median 6 vs. 2, p < 0.001). Tumors with PASS ≥ 4 had significantly lower apelin IRS than those with PASS < 4 (p = 0.001). Apelin IRS was inversely correlated with PASS (r = -0.874, p < 0.001), GAPP score (r = -0.618, p = 0.004), and Ki-67 (r = -0.560, p = 0.010). Lower apelin expression was also associated with diffuse growth pattern, central/confluent necrosis, and tumor cell spindling. VEGF IRS showed no significant association with PASS, GAPP score, Ki-67, tumor size, or individual PASS components. Conclusions: Reduced apelin immunoreactivity was associated with unfavorable histopathological features in pheochromocytoma, whereas increased VEGF immunoreactivity was not associated with the evaluated histopathological risk parameters. These exploratory findings suggest that apelin may be a candidate tissue marker; however, its clinical and prognostic relevance requires further investigation in larger multicenter studies.
papers.journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology

papers.title: First case report of ectopic Cushing's syndrome secondary to synchronous mediastinal neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: Ectopic Cushing's syndrome (ECS) is a rare cause of hypercortisolism resulting from non-pituitary adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) secretion, most associated with neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) of pulmonary or gastrointestinal origin. Mediastinal NETs are an extremely rare source. We report the case of a 23-year-old male with no relevant medical history, presenting with progressive muscle weakness, hyperpigmentation, weight gain, and signs of severe hypercortisolism, including moon facies, ecchymosis, hypertension, hyperglycemia, and hypokalemia. Hormonal tests confirmed ECS with markedly elevated ACTH and cortisol levels. Imaging revealed two anterior mediastinal masses. Histopathological analysis of the surgical specimens confirmed ACTH-producing atypical NETs. This case highlights the importance of considering ectopic ACTH secretion from mediastinal neuroendocrine tumors in the differential diagnosis of severe, rapidly progressive hypercortisolism. Early recognition and timely surgical management can prevent life-threatening complications and improve patient outcomes, even in rare and aggressive presentations.

papers.title: Multikilohertz optical microelastography for viscoelastic characterization of soft biomaterials demonstrated on melanoma spheroids.
papers.abstract: The stiffness and viscosity of biological tissue determine how mechanical forces are transmitted and dissipated within it, and both are increasingly used to study tumor growth and treatment response. Measuring these properties within small three-dimensional samples is challenging: it requires shear waves at kilohertz frequencies, which attenuate over short distances, while conventional excitation methods introduce additional signal loss that is difficult to separate from the intrinsic dissipation of the tissue. To enable sub-millimeter viscoelastic characterization of three-dimensional biological constructs in the multikilohertz frequency range using quasi-planar wave excitation and optical detection. We developed an optical microelastography platform that combines quasi-planar shear-wave excitation using a piezoelectric actuator, high-speed imaging (up to 210,000 fps), and k -space dispersion analysis to estimate frequency-dependent viscoelastic parameters through a Kelvin-Voigt model. The system was validated using polyacrylamide phantoms with tunable viscoelastic properties at five concentrations (15% to 26% v/v). Validation across polyacrylamide concentrations yielded effective shear moduli of 0.70 to 19.31 kPa, with a minimum resolvable shear wavelength of ∼ 110 μ m in the polyacrylamide phantoms. Experimental phase-velocity dispersion showed good agreement with finite-element predictions ( RMSE < 0.16 m / s , mean relative error < 3 % , R 2 > 0.96 ). Measurements on four melanoma spheroids (237 to 823 µm diameter) produced effective viscoelastic parameters of μ = 0.45 to 0.71 kPa and η = 0.033 to 0.097 Pa · s ( R 2 ≥ 0.96 ), obtained within specimen-specific analysis bands and consistent with values reported for three-dimensional tumor spheroid models. This platform demonstrates kilohertz-range viscoelastic characterization of three-dimensional biological constructs at sub-millimeter scales, validated in polyacrylamide phantoms and demonstrated in proof-of-concept measurements on four melanoma tumor spheroids of different sizes. The quasi-planar excitation approach reduces geometric spreading artifacts associated with conventional excitation methods and provides a noninvasive optical tool for studying frequency-dependent mechanical behavior in mechanobiology and tissue engineering.

papers.title: Stereotactic Radiosurgery for an Unresectable Jugulotympanic Paraganglioma: Clinical Response and Acute Toxicity in a 70-Year-Old Patient.
papers.abstract: Jugulotympanic paragangliomas (JTPs) are rare, highly vascular neuroendocrine tumors characterized by slow but locally aggressive growth at the skull base. Their management in elderly patients is particularly challenging because of their close proximity to critical neurovascular structures. We report the case of a 70-year-old woman with a 20-year history of pulsatile tinnitus and a 13-year history of chronic vertigo. Her symptoms progressively worsened, with the recent onset of otic bleeding, occipital headache, and dysphonia, prompting referral to the Radiation Oncology Department. Physical examination revealed a pulsatile reddish mass in the left middle ear, along with ipsilateral lower cranial nerve deficits. Given the unresectable nature of the lesion and the patient's comorbidities, definitive stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) was recommended. Treatment was delivered in a single fraction of 14 Gy with the aim of achieving local tumor control and symptom stabilization. Following treatment, the patient experienced significant improvement in pulsatile tinnitus and complete resolution of occipital pain. At the three-month follow-up evaluation, she developed local complications including tympanic membrane ulceration and middle ear mucosal necrosis, which were managed conservatively with antibiotic therapy and close clinical surveillance. At eight months after treatment, the patient maintained clinical improvement and neurological stability, with persistent local tumor control on follow-up MRI and no evidence of locoregional progression. SRS represents an effective treatment option for unresectable JTPs, offering symptom control and functional preservation with acceptable toxicity. Nevertheless, careful post-treatment monitoring is essential for the early identification and management of radiation-related complications, particularly in tumors with extensive local invasion.

papers.title: Selpercatinib in Treatment of Advanced Medullary Thyroid Cancer: Effectiveness and Side Effects - A Case Report of 2 Patients during 60 Months of Therapy.
papers.abstract: Medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) is a rare, but aggressive tumor that accounts for 4% of thyroid carcinomas. A mutation in the proto-oncogene RET has been shown to occur in ca. 70% of those neoplasia. Selpercatinib is a newly approved drug that specifically targets the RET-kinase and demonstrated a very high efficacy in reducing the tumor activity and in progression-free survival in patients with an advanced metastatic disease [1]. In accordance with the approval of the FDA, we started a treatment with selpercatinib on 2 patients with advanced metastatic MTC with an established RET mutation. They received selpercatinib 160 mg bidaily, and we observed the patients for 60 months. We observed a very good metabolic and serological response to the treatment with a decrease in the tumor marker of 99.8% and 98.5% and stable imaging. Hypertension grade II, hypotension grade I, proteinuria grade I, hyperphosphatemia grade I, and hypocalcemia grade II were the low-grade side effects that we observed during these 60 months of therapy. Selpercatinib proved to be a good antineoplastic drug for patients with RET-mutated, advanced, and inoperable MTC.

papers.title: A Case Report of a Grade G2 Rectal Neuroendocrine Neoplasm with Perineural Invasion and Lymph Node Metastasis.
papers.abstract: Rectal neuroendocrine tumors (R-NETs) are a common type of gastrointestinal neuroendocrine tumor, with an incidence that has increased due to advancements in endoscopic technology. Most are small, low-grade, and have a favorable prognosis, but their clinical presentation is nonspecific and easily confused with benign lesions, posing challenges in differential diagnosis, especially for medium-sized lesions. This article reports a case of a 50-year-old male patient who presented with nonspecific lower abdominal pain. Postoperative pathology confirmed a G2-grade, pT2N1 stage R-NET with perineural invasion, lymph node metastasis, and tumor nodule formation. The uniqueness of this case lies in its aggressive biological behavior. Preoperative biopsy indicated G2 grade, while postoperative pathology revealed more extensive infiltration and metastasis. Additionally, the tumor coexisted with tubular adenoma, increasing diagnostic complexity. The patient underwent laparoscopic radical surgery combined with postoperative systemic therapy using octreotide and surufatinib. The significance of this case highlights the need for clinical vigilance regarding the potential aggressiveness of G2-grade R-NETs, emphasizing the critical role of multidisciplinary collaboration, comprehensive pathological evaluation, and individualized stage-based treatment in optimizing diagnosis and prognosis.

papers.title: Refractory Acute Myeloid Leukemia following Extended Peptide Receptor Radionuclide Therapy for Well-Differentiated GEP-NETs: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) using 177Lu-DOTATATE is an established treatment for somatostatin receptor-positive gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. However, the incidence and risk profile of therapy-related myeloid neoplasms following extended 177Lu-DOTATATE exposure particularly beyond the standard four-cycle regimen remain poorly defined. We report a 49-year-old woman with a well-differentiated jejunal neuroendocrine tumor with hepatic and peritoneal metastases who underwent bowel resection and limited hepatic metastatectomy, followed by long-acting somatostatin analog therapy and subsequent enrollment in a provincial PRRT clinical trial. She received 12 cycles of 177Lu-DOTATATE over 5 years (4 induction, 8 maintenance), without prior cytotoxic chemotherapy or external-beam radiotherapy, achieving durable biochemical and radiologic disease stability with minimal early toxicity. In late 2023, she developed progressive pancytopenia. Bone marrow examination in September 2024 revealed high-risk therapy-related acute myeloid leukemia (AML) characterized by inv(3)(q21q26.2), monosomy 7, complex cytogenetics, and a KRAS mutation. Her leukemia was refractory to intensive induction and subsequent lower-intensity therapy. She died on January 13, 2025, from progressive refractory AML with multiorgan dysfunction and central nervous system involvement. This case highlights a rare but life-threatening late hematologic toxicity associated with extended 177Lu-DOTATATE exposure and underscores the importance of long-term hematologic surveillance and critical evaluation of PRRT maintenance strategies beyond the standard four-cycle protocol.

papers.title: SDHB-Related Carney-Stratakis Syndrome Presenting with a Gastric Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor and a Clinically Suspected Paraganglioma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
papers.abstract: Carney-Stratakis syndrome (CSS) is a rare autosomal dominant hereditary tumor-predisposition syndrome characterized by succinate dehydrogenase (SDH)-deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) and paragangliomas. These tumors typically arise in younger patients, may occur synchronously or metachronously, and often show limited sensitivity to conventional tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Given the potential for multifocal disease, recurrence, and familial involvement, accurate clinicopathological assessment, genetic evaluation, and long-term surveillance are essential. A 36-year-old woman presented with a 7-month history of visual disturbance. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a hypervascular tumor extending from the left jugular foramen to the carotid sheath, raising clinical suspicion of a paraganglioma and prompting biochemical and functional imaging evaluation. Plasma noradrenaline and dopamine levels were elevated, whereas 123I-metaiodobenzylguanidine scintigraphy showed no abnormal uptake. Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography incidentally identified a gastric submucosal tumor. Because placement of a lumboperitoneal shunt for intracranial hypertension was expected to increase the risk of infection and complicate subsequent abdominal surgery, gastric resection was prioritized. Laparoscopic-endoscopic cooperative surgery (LECS) was selected to facilitate local resection of the tumor near the esophagogastric junction while preserving the cardia; an intraoperative perforation necessitated conversion to classical LECS, and complete macroscopic resection was achieved. Histopathological examination demonstrated a multinodular epithelioid GIST positive for KIT and DOG1, with loss of SDHB expression, indicating an SDH-deficient GIST. Germline testing identified a pathogenic SDHB variant, supporting the diagnosis of CSS in the context of the clinically suspected paraganglioma. The jugular foramen lesion, for which no histological diagnosis was obtained, was managed conservatively, and delayed shunt placement improved the visual symptoms. This case highlights the importance of considering an SDH-related hereditary syndrome in a young patient with an SDH-deficient gastric GIST and a synchronous lesion clinically suggestive of paraganglioma. It also illustrates the value of genetic evaluation, explicit recognition of diagnostic uncertainty, and multidisciplinary treatment sequencing.

papers.title: Endoscopic resection of a periampullary duodenal paraganglioma.
papers.abstract: Periampullary subepithelial lesions are generally removed by surgery. We demonstrate a video of endoscopic resection of a periampullary duodenal paraganglioma. A combination of ERCP and endoscopic submucosal dissection skills was used to facilitate separation of the subepithelial lesion from the ampulla and lesion resection. En bloc resection with negative margins was achieved. Pathology confirmed a gangliocytic paraganglioma. Endoscopic resection is a feasible and less-invasive alternative to pancreaticoduodenectomy for selected periampullary subepithelial lesions.
papers.journal: VideoGIE : an official video journal of the American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy

papers.title: Severe insulin-requiring diabetes in a noradrenergic giant pheochromocytoma: a secretory-metabolic phenotype paradox.
papers.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a rare catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor associated with hypertension and dysglycemia in 20% to 40% of cases. Insulin-requiring diabetes has been reported in tumors with an adrenergic profile, owing to epinephrine-mediated inhibition of β-cell secretion. A 37-year-old man with a normal body mass index and an 18-year history of insulin-requiring diabetes and hypertension was found to have a right adrenal mass measuring 10.1 × 8.0 × 6.7 cm. Biochemical evaluation showed a noradrenergic profile, with urinary normetanephrine greater than 5000 μg/24 hours (SI: >26 400 nmol/day; reference range, 70-538 μg/24 hours [SI: 370-2841 nmol/day]) and normal urinary metanephrine. Right adrenalectomy and histopathology confirmed an intra-adrenal pheochromocytoma. After surgery, insulin was discontinued, and glycated hemoglobin remained below 6.1% (SI: 41-43 mmol/mol) without therapy. A preoperative insulin requirement of 0.83 units/kg/day, normal C-peptide, and negative glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies supported a mixed and reversible mechanism involving catecholamine-induced insulin resistance and β-cell suppression. Severe postoperative hypoglycemia was attributed to reversal of catecholamine excess. This case challenges the association of severe diabetes with adrenergic pheochromocytomas and suggests that catecholamine burden and exposure duration may be more important determinants of metabolic severity than secretory profile alone, after prolonged exposure to high catecholamine concentrations.

papers.title: Carcinoid Heart Disease Associated with a Primary Ovarian Stromal Carcinoid Tumor: A Case Report and a Review of the Literature.
papers.abstract: Carcinoid heart disease (CHD) is a rare cardiac manifestation of neuroendocrine tumors, typically associated with hepatic metastases. Primary ovarian carcinoid tumors represent an uncommon source of CHD and may lead to cardiac involvement in the absence of metastatic disease. A 51-year-old Iranian woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea, bilateral lower extremity edema, and episodes of facial flushing. She had undergone total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for a primary ovarian stromal carcinoid tumor 3 months prior. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe tricuspid regurgitation with thickened, retracted valve leaflets and impaired coaptation, while the pulmonary valve was spared. Laboratory findings were within normal limits except for a markedly elevated 24-h urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) level (128 mg/24 h). Cross-sectional imaging, including chest CT and abdominal-pelvic MRI, showed no evidence of hepatic or pulmonary metastases. A diagnosis of isolated CHD secondary to a primary ovarian carcinoid tumor was established. The patient declined surgical intervention and was discharged against medical advice. This case highlights a rare presentation of CHD originating from a primary ovarian carcinoid tumor without metastatic involvement. Clinicians should consider this diagnosis in patients with unexplained right-sided valvular disease and features of carcinoid syndrome, even in the absence of liver metastases.

papers.title: Porta Hepatis Paraganglioma: A Rare Case Report With Diagnostic Pitfalls.
papers.abstract: Paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine tumors that infrequently localize to the porta hepatis, where they create significant diagnostic challenges by mimicking hepatocellular carcinoma or distinct mesenchymal neoplasms. We report the case of a 64-year-old woman presenting with vague abdominal pain and an enhancing porta hepatis mass compressing the inferior vena cava. An initial core needle biopsy, which suggested a benign mesenchymal tumor, underscores the potential for misdiagnosis in such atypical presentations. During surgery, the patient developed paroxysmal hypertension suggestive of occult catecholamine release. Subsequent histopathological examination revealed a classic zellballen pattern, with immunohistochemical positivity for Chromogranin A, Synaptophysin, and S100 definitively confirming a paraganglioma. The patient remains disease-free at a 2-year follow-up. This case highlights the importance of considering paraganglioma in the differential diagnosis of porta hepatis masses and emphasizes the value of histopathology and immunohistochemistry for accurate diagnosis, particularly in patients who lack preoperative adrenergic symptoms.

papers.title: Bidirectional ventricular tachycardia unmasked by beta-blockade in pheochromocytoma presenting as hypertensive optic neuropathy: a case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor that can produce life-threatening cardiovascular complications. Bidirectional ventricular tachycardia (BVT) is a rare arrhythmia with a narrow differential diagnosis, classically associated with digitalis toxicity and catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, and only exceptionally reported as the presenting feature of pheochromocytoma. A 51-year-old woman presented with acute visual impairment secondary to hypertensive optic neuropathy; her blood pressure was 220/138 mmHg. Within 24 h of initiating sodium nitroprusside and metoprolol, she developed bidirectional ventricular tachycardia followed by torsades de pointes. Marked blood-pressure lability, dramatically elevated plasma free metanephrines and catecholamines, and a left adrenal mass on computed tomography established the diagnosis of pheochromocytoma. After alpha-adrenergic blockade with phenoxybenzamine, laparoscopic adrenalectomy was performed, and histopathology confirmed the diagnosis. No ventricular arrhythmia recurred, and blood pressure normalized without antihypertensive medication. Bidirectional ventricular tachycardia may be the initial manifestation of pheochromocytoma and may be unmasked by beta-blockade administered before alpha-blockade. Unexplained BVT accompanied by blood-pressure fluctuations should prompt biochemical screening and adrenal imaging. Etiologic treatment is curative, whereas antiarrhythmic therapy alone is insufficient. We review the previously published cases to contextualize this rare phenotype.

papers.title: Three Cases of Primary Hepatic Neuroendocrine Tumor Treated with Surgical Resection: A Case Series and Literature Review.
papers.abstract: Primary hepatic neuroendocrine tumors (PHNETs) are extremely rare, accounting for approximately 0.3% of all neuroendocrine tumors (NETs). Because the liver is the most common metastatic site of NETs, distinguishing PHNET from metastatic disease is often challenging. Optimal treatment strategies and follow-up protocols for PHNET have not been well established. We report 3 cases of PHNET treated with surgical resection. Case 1 involved a 42-year-old woman with a liver tumor detected during a routine medical examination. Laparoscopic partial hepatectomy was performed under the preoperative diagnosis of hepatic adenoma or hemangioma. Histopathological examination revealed a NET, grade 2. The patient developed intrahepatic recurrence 5 years and 8 months after the initial surgery and underwent repeat hepatectomy. Case 2 involved a 72-year-old woman diagnosed with PHNET (grade 2) by liver biopsy. Laparoscopic extended posterior sectionectomy was performed. Intrahepatic recurrence occurred 3 years and 9 months later, and repeat hepatectomy was performed. Case 3 involved a 50-year-old man diagnosed with NET (grade 1) by endoscopic US-guided fine-needle aspiration. Extended left hepatectomy with partial resection of segment 8 was performed. He remains recurrence-free. In all cases, comprehensive examinations, including endoscopy, somatostatin receptor imaging (SRI), and PET, revealed no evidence of extrahepatic primary lesions, leading to the diagnosis of PHNET. PHNET is a rare tumor that may recur several years after curative resection. Careful long-term follow-up is therefore required, and repeat surgical resection may be an effective treatment option for selected patients with recurrent disease.

papers.title: Metachronous and Sporadic Bilateral Carotid Body Paraganglioma.
papers.abstract: The Authors' goal is to highlight the importance of early diagnosis and management of metachronous carotid body paraganglioma (CBP), analysing and discussing the main features of this rare tumor. This study review the literature on a very particular topic, reporting the case of a patient with the rare evidence of a metachronous CBP in the left side of the neck, which onset and was surgically treated 26 years after the first contralateral presentation. After excision, the diagnosis of CBP was confirmed by histological and immunohistochemical examination of the surgical specimen. Transient dysphonia and dysphagia were observed after surgery, both recovered after 1 years. No cardiac anomalies were detected. Paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms with an incidence of 2-8 X 1,000,000. Paragangliomas of the head and neck (HNP) originate mainly from the carotid body (60%) and in a few cases from the jugular bulb, the medial promontory of the middle ear (30%), the vagal nerve and the nodose ganglion (5-10 %). Bilateral CBP represents an extremely rare entity, accounting for approximately 5% of patients with CBP. Diagnostic imaging of CBP includes ultrasound, Computed Tomography (CT), Magnetic Resonance Images (MRI) and Angiography. The treatment of choice for CBP is its complete surgical removal. Early detection of symptoms referable to a new CBP is very important, because of the possibility, even after many years, of contralateral presentation of the same tumor. This, if operated at an early stage, decrease the risk of neurovascular complications.

papers.title: Randomized controlled trials of radiation therapy for cutaneous malignancies: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: In cutaneous oncology, radiotherapy use is largely based on retrospective studies, institutional experience, and expert consensus, with limited high-level evidence to guide practice. We summarize randomized controlled trials in cutaneous radiation oncology and identify gaps in contemporary treatment warranting additional study. We searched Ovid MEDLINE ALL, Embase.com, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials for randomized controlled trials of radiotherapy for cutaneous malignancies: basal cell carcinoma (BCC), squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), melanoma, and Merkel cell carcinoma. Outcomes of interest included recurrence, survival, toxicity and cosmesis. Study inclusion required approval by three authors, with discrepancies resolved by an additional author.
