Thirteen trials entailing fewer than 2500 patients were identified, with only four studies published in the last decade. Three BCC studies compared radiotherapy with other treatments, while two additional BCC studies and one mixed BCC/SCC study compared dose-fractionation regimens. One SCC study evaluated adjuvant radiotherapy versus chemoradiotherapy. Among five melanoma trials, four evaluated adjuvant radiotherapy, including one for the primary tumor site and three for the regional nodal basin, and one compared definitive radiotherapy with topical imiquimod for unresectable melanoma in situ. One Merkel cell carcinoma trial evaluated lymph node basin radiotherapy. Randomized trials of radiotherapy for cutaneous malignancies are limited, small and heterogeneous, relative to the frequency of these diseases and clinical trials of other therapeutic interventions. Modern randomized trials are needed to bridge these gaps.

papers.title: Postpartum diagnosis of pheochromocytoma presenting as atypical hypertensive disorder of pregnancy: A case report.
papers.abstract: Pheochromocytoma, a catecholamine-secreting adrenal tumour, is a rare but important cause of hypertension in pregnancy. Its symptoms may mimic more common disorders of pregnancy, making diagnosis challenging. We present a postpartum pheochromocytoma diagnosis with favourable maternal and neonatal outcomes. A 29-year-old woman in her first pregnancy developed proteinuria at 34 weeks and new-onset hypertension at 36 weeks, managed as pre-eclampsia. Worsening hypertension, gestational diabetes and breech presentation led to caesarean section at 36 weeks and 4 days of gestation. Postpartum, she experienced severe headaches, labile blood pressure, tachycardia and sweating. Imaging identified a 4 cm right adrenal mass. Markedly elevated plasma and urinary normetanephrines confirmed pheochromocytoma. Right adrenalectomy was performed seven weeks post-partum, with complete excision. Symptoms resolved postoperatively. Subsequent surveillance imaging showed no recurrence. She later had a second uncomplicated pregnancy. This case highlights how pheochromocytoma in pregnancy can be differentiated from more common conditions. Prompt diagnosis and multidisciplinary management can optimise patient outcomes.

papers.title: Mutations in Chromatin Regulator Genes Associate With TMB and Immunotherapy Response in Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is a high-tumor-mutational-burden (TMB) cancer, largely driven by ultraviolet-induced DNA damage. Although TMB predicts response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), the genomic factors underlying its variability remain unclear. In addition to canonical DNA-repair defects such as mismatch repair (MMR) and POLE/POLD1 mutations, alterations in chromatin regulators (CRs) may influence genome stability and mutational load. We analyzed melanoma cohorts from the MSK-ICI, TCGA, MSK-Met, DFCI, and UCLA datasets. TMB was compared between CR-mutant and CR-wild-type tumors and overall cohorts, along with gene-level analyses of individual CRs. Associations between the number of CR mutations and TMB were assessed. Overall survival (OS) in ICI-treated patients was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox models, with TCGA as a non-ICI-treated comparator. Across datasets, CR-mutant melanomas consistently exhibited significantly higher TMB than CR-wild-type tumors. Several CRs were linked to elevated TMB, comparable to MMR- or POLE/POLD1-mutant tumors. Multiple CR alterations showed a positive linear relationship with TMB. In ICI-treated cohorts, CR-mutant tumors had significantly longer OS, while this link was not observed in non-ICI-treated cases. These findings suggest that CR mutations define a subset of melanomas with high TMB and improved response to ICIs, warranting prospective validation as predictive biomarkers.

papers.title: Calcium-stimulated calcitonin and procalcitonin in borderline hypercalcitoninemia: histopathologic and nodal correlates in a thyroidectomy cohort.
papers.abstract: Mild basal calcitonin elevation represents a diagnostic gray zone in patients undergoing thyroid surgery for non-medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) indications. We evaluated calcium-stimulated calcitonin and procalcitonin kinetics according to final histopathology and nodal status in this setting. This retrospective study included 37 adults with reproducible borderline basal calcitonin elevation (< 50 pg/mL) selected from 577 patients who underwent total thyroidectomy for non-MTC indications between 2021 and 2024. All patients underwent calcium stimulation testing with measurement of calcitonin and procalcitonin at baseline and after stimulation. Biochemical responses were compared with final histopathology. Median basal calcitonin was 13.1 [11.0-16.8] pg/mL and median peak stimulated calcitonin (psCT) was 480 [320-790] pg/mL. Final histopathology showed MTC in seven patients (18.9%), all microcarcinomas, C-cell hyperplasia (CCH) without MTC in nine, and no C-cell pathology in 21. Median psCT was highest in MTC, intermediate in CCH without MTC, and lower in patients without C-cell pathology (820 [640-1040], 460 [310-670], and 360 [270-540] pg/mL, respectively; nominal p = 0.047 for MTC vs CCH). psCT values ≥ 500 pg/mL were observed in 6 of 7 MTC cases compared with 1 of 9 CCH cases without MTC. Central lymph-node metastasis was documented in 3 of 7 MTC patients and was accompanied by numerically higher psCT and fold-rise values. wf45g6 Procalcitonin increment and fold-rise were greater in MTC than in CCH without MTC, but no stable procalcitonin-based threshold or combined rule was identified. Occult micro-MTC may show marked calcium-stimulated calcitonin responses despite mild basal hypercalcitoninemia. These findings are exploratory and do not validate diagnostic or surgical thresholds.

papers.title: OTUD4 stabilizes CYLD and counteracts BCL3 K63-linked polyubiquitination to suppress melanoma progression.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is a highly aggressive malignancy in which dysregulated ubiquitin-dependent signaling contributes to tumor progression. OTUD4 is frequently downregulated in melanoma, but the functional significance of this alteration remains unclear. Here, we identify OTUD4 as a dual-mode deubiquitinase that suppresses melanoma progression by coordinating K48- and K63-linked polyubiquitination. OTUD4 directly binds and stabilizes CYLD by counteracting K48-linked polyubiquitination, whereas it independently binds BCL3 and counteracts BCL3 K63-linked polyubiquitination. OTUD4 depletion promotes BCL3 ubiquitination and nuclear translocation in melanoma cells, leading to increased melanoma cell proliferation and tumor growth in clonogenic and xenograft assays. Clinically, expression of OTUD4 and CYLD progressively decreases from normal skin through benign nevi to melanoma, with a further reduction in highly metastatic tumors. Reduced expression of OTUD4 and CYLD is associated with poor prognosis in patients with melanoma. Together, these results reveal an OTUD4-CYLD-BCL3 regulatory axis in melanoma, in which OTUD4 stabilizes CYLD and inhibits BCL3 activity.

papers.title: Catecholamine-induced metabolic dysfunction and its reversal postsurgery in pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma patients: Insights from the "PheoMet" study.
papers.abstract: Catecholamine excess in pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma is believed to result in numerous metabolic implications leading to insulin resistance and glucose intolerance. PheoMet was a prospective cohort study including 40 pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma patients and 20 age- and sex-matched controls with nonfunctioning adrenal tumors. Patients with comorbidities affecting metabolism were excluded. Metabolic evaluation comprised oral glucose tolerance testing with serial glucose, insulin, and C-peptide measurements preoperatively, early postoperatively (1-2 weeks), and at 6-month follow-up. Derived indices included homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance, homeostatic model assessment of β-cell function, insulinogenic index, and disposition index. Lipid profile and hemoglobin A1c were also analyzed. Patients and controls were age and sex matched. Study group patients had higher baseline systolic blood pressure and 24-hour urinary metanephrines and normetanephrines compared with controls; these normalized following surgery. Pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma patients demonstrated higher fasting glucose and postprandial glucose at 30, 60, 90, and 120 minutes, which declined significantly postsurgery across all postoperative time points (P = .001). Hemoglobin A1c showed a progressive decline from 6.18% ± 0.89 preoperatively to 5.51% ± 0.51 at 6 months. Insulin and C-peptide levels did not change significantly over time. Homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance did not show any significant changes, whereas disposition index increased significantly from 0.57 (0.20-1.44) to 0.86 (0.56-1.67) (P = .02). Lipid profile did not exhibit any statistically significant longitudinal changes. Pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma causes reversible catecholamine-mediated metabolic dysfunction. Curative surgery results in early and sustained improvement in glucose homeostasis. These results suggest the utility of comprehensive metabolic assessment in pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma patients.

papers.title: Clinicopathologic and Molecular Characteristics of Gastric Cancer With a Neuroendocrine Carcinoma Component.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancers containing a neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) component show aggressive clinical behavior, but the clinicopathological significance of NEC components and the mechanisms associated with neuroendocrine differentiation (NED) remain incompletely understood. This study evaluated the prognostic, metastatic, molecular, and immune features of gastric cancers with NEC components. This retrospective cohort study included patients with resectable gastric adenocarcinoma (GAC) and gastric adeno-neuroendocrine carcinoma (G-ANEC) treated at Peking University Third Hospital from 2011 to 2022. Clinicopathological characteristics, recurrence patterns, lymph node metastatic components, and survival outcomes were analyzed. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed at a 1:3 ratio to reduce baseline imbalance. Component-level immunohistochemistry was used to compare adenocarcinoma (ADC) and NEC components. Transcriptomic data from TCGA-STAD were analyzed to explore pathways associated with ASCL1 expression and STAT3 pathway activity. ASCL1-overexpressing AGS gastric cancer cells were established, and invasive capacity was assessed using Transwell invasion assays. Among 666 patients, including 639 with GAC and 27 with G-ANEC, G-ANEC showed more aggressive clinicopathological features than conventional GAC. After PSM, G-ANEC was associated with worse overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS). Recurrence and liver metastasis rates were significantly higher in G-ANEC than in GAC. Component-level analysis showed that lymph node metastases in G-MANEC were predominantly composed of NEC components, indicating NEC enrichment in metastatic deposits. ASCL1 and p-STAT3 expression were significantly higher in NEC components than in paired ADC components (P = 0.041 and P = 0.016, respectively). TCGA-STAD analyses showed that high ASCL1 expression and increased STAT3 pathway activity were associated with neuroendocrine-related pathway enrichment, reduced immune-related pathway activity, and poorer survival. CD8+ T-cell infiltration was lower in NEC components than in ADC components (P < 0.001) and inversely correlated with ASCL1 expression (rpb = -0.645, P = 0.006). In vitro, ASCL1-overexpressing AGS cells showed enhanced invasive capacity. Gastric cancers containing NEC components are associated with aggressive clinicopathological behavior, increased recurrence, and worse prognosis. ASCL1 and STAT3 are associated with NED and immune suppression, and ASCL1 overexpression enhances gastric cancer cell invasion in vitro. These findings suggest that NEC component-associated molecular and immune features may contribute to the aggressive phenotype of G-ANEC and support distinct therapeutic considerations beyond conventional GAC.

papers.title: Structural and Quantitative Surface N-Glycomic Profiling of Cisplatin-Treated Melanoma Cells with Distinct Metastatic Potential.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is a highly aggressive skin cancer with strong metastatic potential and frequent chemoresistance. Aberrant N-glycosylation plays a critical role in tumor progression and drug resistance; however, cisplatin-induced alterations in melanoma surface N-glycans remain poorly understood. Thus, this study aimed to perform comprehensive structural and quantitative profiling of surface N-glycans in G-361 (low metastatic potential), A375P (moderate), and SK-MEL-28 (high) melanoma cells following cisplatin treatment using LC-MS/MS. A total of 25, 39, and 28 surface N-glycans were identified in untreated G-361, A375P, and SK-MEL-28 cells, respectively, whereas 40, 37, and 40 N-glycans were detected after cisplatin treatment. Absolute quantification revealed a marked increase in total N-glycan abundance in G-361 (3.2 to 8.4 pmol) and A375P (5.7 to 10.9 pmol), whereas SK-MEL-28 maintained homeostasis (3.9 to 4.0 pmol). Surface N-glycans were predominantly high-mannose and complex-type glycans with extensive sialylation and fucosylation. Cisplatin induced distinct cell line-specific remodeling: G-361 accumulated high-mannose glycans with reduced Neu5Gc-containing sialylation; A375P showed increased glycan branching and Neu5Ac-containing sialylation; and SK-MEL-28 maintained a stable glycan distribution but exhibited increased Neu5Gc-containing sialylation. These results demonstrate adaptive N-glycosylation responses to cisplatin in melanoma cells with distinct metastatic potentials and provide a glycomic framework for understanding cisplatin-associated glycan alterations.

papers.title: Developments of Quinoline-Engineered Radioligands for Melanin-Targeted PET Imaging.
papers.abstract: A quinoline-based platform was developed to generate melanin-targeted radiotracers suitable for 68Ga-labeling. Four quinoline derivatives integrating a melanin-binding moiety and a radiometal chelator were synthesized and evaluated. All tracers exhibited high hydrophilicity (Log P -2.86 to -2.50) and good radiochemical stability. Among them, [68Ga]Ga-D-6-2-DMA showed the most favorable in vivo performance, with high tumor uptake in B16F10 melanoma (3.00 ± 0.25% ID/g at 0.5 h; 2.75 ± 0.25% ID/g at 2 h) and results consistent with biodistribution. Blocking studies confirmed melanin-specific targeting, and negligible uptake was observed in non-melanoma A375 xenografts. In melanoma lung metastasis models, [68Ga]Ga-D-6-2-DMA clearly visualized metastatic lesions, which correlated with bioluminescence imaging and autoradiography. These findings identify [68Ga]Ga-D-6-2-DMA as a promising lead radiotracer for further development.

papers.title: Rationally Designed Ru(II) Complex with Dual Type I/II ROS Generation for Hypoxia-Tolerant Photodynamic Therapy in Melanoma.
papers.abstract: The hypoxic tumor microenvironment of melanoma imposes a critical limitation on conventional type II photodynamic therapy (PDT), relying on oxygen for the generation of cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS). To overcome this challenge, a donor-π-acceptor (D-π-A) bis-terpyridine ruthenium(II) complex, Ru(tpy)2TT, was rationally designed and synthesized to enable dual type I/II ROS generation. The ROS production efficiency was quantitatively evaluated in B16 murine melanoma cells, and the antitumor efficacy was assessed in a syngeneic C57BL/6N mouse melanoma model. Upon photoactivation at 500 nm, Ru(tpy)2TT efficiently generated both superoxide anion (type I ROS) and singlet oxygen (type II ROS). Intratumoral administration followed by localized irradiation resulted in an 80% reduction in tumor volume after 10 days, with no observed systemic toxicity or off-target effects. These findings demonstrate that Ru(tpy)2TT circumvents hypoxia-induced PDT resistance in melanoma via hypoxia-tolerant and oxygen-dependent ROS pathways, establishing its potential as a targeted precision antitumor agent. Furthermore, this work provides a generalizable molecular design strategy for developing hypoxia-tolerant PDT agents for refractory melanoma.

papers.title: Current state and future potential of radiopharmaceutical therapy in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Radiopharmaceutical therapy has been adopted with success in malignancies such as prostate cancer and neuroendocrine tumors. This approach often combines a diagnostic agent to measure and assess target availability prior to administering a parenteral radiotherapeutic agent against the same target. Emerging evidence and ongoing research suggest that this approach could have a beneficial impact in breast cancer treatment, with a number of different breast cancer-specific or tumor microenvironment targets. There are several agents under investigation, with the majority in early-phase trials. This narrative review will provide a brief introduction to radiopharmaceutical imaging and therapy for breast cancer, discuss emerging therapeutic targets under investigation in breast cancer, and discuss challenges with the implementation of radiopharmaceuticals in breast cancer.

papers.title: Robotic-assisted transduodenal ampullectomy for a neuroendocrine tumour: A step-by-step surgical video.
papers.abstract: When endoscopic resection of ampullary neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) is not feasible due to tumour size or location, transduodenal ampullectomy can offer a parenchymal-sparing alternative to a formal pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure) [1,2]. We present a robotic-assisted transduodenal ampullectomy (RATA) in a 71-year-old male with an incidental 14 mm ampullary NET found during routine screening. Preoperative 68Ga-DOTATATE PET-CT demonstrated intense somatostatin-receptor avidity (SUVmax 66.8) and absent FDG uptake. The MDT recommended surgical excision due to size and Ki-67 4%. Following right colonic flexure mobilisation and a Kocher maneuver, the cystic duct was isolated and cannulated with a 4 Fr catheter to guide biliary identification. After a longitudinal duodenotomy, the ampullary lesion was visualized. Submucosal saline-adrenaline was injected in the submucosal plane. Diathermy scissors were used to perform a circumferential mucosal and muscularis dissection. Biliary and pancreatic ducts were sharply divided and reconstructed using interrupted 5/0 polydioxanone sutures between the pancreatobiliary ducts and the duodenal mucosa after positioning a 6 Fr catheter in the pancreatic duct. The duodenotomy was closed in two layers using a 4/0 absorbable barbed suture, and a methylene blue leak test through the nasogastric tube confirmed duodenal integrity. The procedure was completed successfully with no intraoperative complications. A postoperative contrast-enhanced CT on day 5 demonstrated no collections and no oral contrast extravasation. Oral feeding was gradually reintroduced, the abdominal drain was removed, and the patient was discharged on day 7. Following a brief readmission on day 13 for a pulmonary microembolism successfully treated with medical therapy, the patient recovered fully and remains disease-free 7 months after surgery. RATA can represent a safe, feasible, and pancreas-preserving alternative to formal pancreaticoduodenectomy for well-differentiated ampullary NETs in selected patients. The robotic platform enhances three-dimensional visualization and wrist articulation, optimizing the delicate micro-reconstruction of the pancreaticobiliary junction.

papers.title: [18F]DOPA PET Reveals Metabolically Active Transcriptomic States Associated with Clinical Outcome in Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors.
papers.abstract: [18F]fluorodihydroxyphenylalanine ([18F]DOPA) uptake is dependent on amino acid transport and decarboxylation pathways, including large neutral amino acid transporter 1, encoded by SLC7A5, which are linked to tumor aggressiveness. This study evaluated whether in vivo uptake of [18F]DOPA can serve as an imaging biomarker for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (panNETs), reflecting a tumor's transcriptional status and a patient's clinical course. Methods: This retrospective single-center study was based on a transcriptomic cohort of 74 primary panNETs. A subset of 22 panNETs from patients who underwent preoperative [18F]DOPA PET/CT constituted the discovery radiotranscriptomic cohort. [18F]DOPA tumor uptake was quantified using SUVmax and integrated with matched RNA-sequencing data. Unsupervised clustering, differential expression analysis, gene set enrichment, and tumor microenvironment deconvolution were performed to identify transcriptional programs associated with [18F]DOPA uptake. The prognostic value of SLC7A5 was evaluated in the discovery cohort, the full transcriptomic cohort (n = 74), and an independent external cohort (n = 33). Results: Unsupervised clustering of gene expression profiles identified 2 robust molecular subtypes: cluster 1 and cluster 2. Cluster 1 showed higher [18F]DOPA uptake than did cluster 2, with a median SUVmax of 24.3 versus 5.9, respectively (P = 0.030), and was associated with more advanced clinicopathologic features and shorter event-free survival. This subtype was also characterized by enrichment in extracellular matrix, stromal, vascular, and immune-related components, along with upregulation of amino acid transport and amine metabolism genes, including SLC7A5 As a mechanistic link between tracer uptake and tumor metabolism, SLC7A5 expression significantly stratified event-free survival in the discovery cohort and remained prognostic in the full cohort. Conclusion: [18F]DOPA PET uptake was associated with amino acid-driven metabolic programs in panNETs, including SLC7A5 expression, and adverse clinical features. These findings suggest that [18F]DOPA uptake may provide a noninvasive readout of tumor metabolic activity, although its value as an imaging biomarker requires independent validation.

papers.title: Method optimization and verification of homovanillic acid (HVA), vanillylmandelic acid (VMA) and 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) on liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS).
papers.abstract: Homovanillic acid (HVA) and vanillylmandelic acid (VMA) are used in diagnosis of neuroblastoma. 5-hydroxyindolacetic acid (5-HIAA) is used in diagnosis of intestinal carcinoid syndrome. The aim of this study is to optimize and verify the Chromsystems kit for these cancer biomarkers on our Waters Xevo TQ-S Cronos LC-MS/MS. The method was optimized and verified for our LC-MS/MS. The verification included simple (SP) and complex precision (CP), lower limit of detection (LLD) and quantification (LLQ), linearity, carryover, bias through measuring external quality assessment (EQA) samples, and patient comparison with another laboratory that already validated the LC-MS/MS method. For two levels of HVA quality control: SP was 1.3% and 1.8%, CP 4.9% and 3.0%; VMA: SP was 1.5% and 1.3%, CP was 3.5% and 1.6%; and 5-HIAA: SP was 0.7% and 0.9%, CP was 5.4% and 3.8%. The LLD and LLQ were 0.587 μmol/L and 1.20 μmol/L, 0.138 μmol/L and 0.65 μmol/L, and 0.0464 μmol/L and 5.03 μmol/L for HVA, VMA and 5-HIAA, respectively. The linearity was 1.20 - 290.4 μmol/L (HVA), 0.64 - 910.7 μmol/L (VMA) and 5.03 - 1103.4 μmol/L (5-HIAA), without carryover for three analytes. The LC-MS/MS method had no significant bias when compared to the EQA assigned values. The patient comparison had Passing-Bablok regression equations for HVA: y = -0.4801 + 1.153x; VMA: y = -0.3784 + 1.139x; and 5-HIAA: y = 0.0749 +1.140x. The new reference intervals were adjusted for our method using the method comparison. We successfully optimized and verified the combination of a Chromsystems kit and laboratory developed method for measuring urinary HVA, VMA and 5-HIAA on our Waters LC-MS/MS.

papers.title: Lung neuroendocrine cancer induces immunosuppressive macrophages via serotonin to drive resistance to the T cell engager tarlatamab.
papers.abstract: Tarlatamab, a delta-like protein 3 (DLL3) × CD3-directed T cell engager (TCE), provides clinical efficacy against small cell lung cancers (SCLCs), although its efficacy remains limited, indicating the importance of clarifying the resistance mechanisms. We show that serotonin (5-HT) produced by DLL3high neuroendocrine cancers (NECs) induces immunosuppressive tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), resulting in impaired CD8+ T cell function and TCE resistance. Using SCLC and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma cohorts, we find that DLL3high SCLCs induce immunosuppressive TAMs in the tumor microenvironment and become resistant to tarlatamab. DLL3high NECs increase 5-HT production via TPH1 upregulation. NEC-derived 5-HT augments the immunosuppressive activity of 5-HT receptor 7 (HTR7)-expressing TAMs. Genetic ablation of HTR7 in TAMs or TPH1 in NECs restores CD8+ T cell function and improves the efficacy of TCEs and programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade. We propose that NEC-derived 5-HT-HTR7 axis drives immunosuppressive TAM activation and TCE resistance, making it a key target to increase TCE efficacy.

papers.title: Liver transplantation as a treatment option for neuroendocrine liver metastases: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: The aim was to carry out a systematic review of published articles on liver transplantation outcomes in patients with (LM-NET). We performed a systematic review according to the PRISMA guideline guidelines, using the MEDLINE (PubMed) and Scopus databases to identify published studies. We included 2471 articles after the search, finally selecting 25. We collected data from 1005 patients, with a mean age of 47.9 years, most of them male. The most frequent locations of the primary tumor were the pancreas, followed by the small intestine. The disease-free survival was 25.3 months (14-31) and overall survival 38.5 months (32.5-57.1). Liver transplantation appears to provide a survival benefit in patients with diffuse LM-NET without extrahepatic disease in selected cases.

papers.title: Near real-time intraoperative assessment of pituitary neuroendocrine tumors using stimulated Raman histology during endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery: comparison with conventional histopathology.
papers.abstract: Accurate intraoperative identification of adenomatous versus normal pituitary tissue remains challenging during surgery for pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs), as both can appear similar macroscopically. Stimulated Raman histology (SRH) is a label-free optical imaging technique that provides high-resolution digital histological images of unprocessed tissue within minutes. This study evaluated the feasibility, diagnostic accuracy, and histopathological concordance of SRH compared with conventional hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining in PitNETs. Adult patients (≥ 18 years) who underwent surgery for suspected PitNET were included. Fresh tissue samples from the tumor core and, when feasible, from peritumoral regions were analyzed intraoperatively using SRH followed by standard histopathological processing. A board-certified neuropathologist, blinded to clinical data, independently compared SRH and H&E images regarding diagnostic accuracy, tissue classification (adenomatous vs nonadenomatous), and histopathological features using a semiquantitative scoring system. A total of 28 patients were included, yielding 66 tissue samples for final comparative analysis. SRH imaging was feasible in all cases. SRH demonstrated excellent comparability with conventional H&E in 37 samples (56.1%), good comparability in 20 (30.3%), and low comparability in 9 (13.6%). No significant difference in comparability was observed between tumor core and peritumoral tissue samples (p = 0.409). SRH accurately depicted key histopathological features, including the loss of the lobular glandular structure in adenomatous tissue and connective tissue organization in surrounding structures. Characteristic subtype features-such as Crooke cells in corticotroph PitNET or perivascular tumor cell arrangements in gonadotroph PitNET-were also identifiable. SRH showed high feasibility for intraoperative assessment of PitNETs, generating near H&E-quality digital images within minutes. It reliably enabled distinguishing tumor from normal gland tissue and detected tumor infiltration into adjacent structures. These findings support SRH as a useful aid to intraoperative decision-making in pituitary surgery, with future AI integration likely to further improve diagnostic speed and accuracy.

papers.title: ILC2-derived IL-9 promotes eosinophil-mediated antitumor activity.
papers.abstract: Innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) regulate tissue immunity, yet their roles in tumor control remain incompletely understood. Here, we combined analyses of human sequencing datasets with genetic ablation mouse models and adoptive transfer experiments to identify that glucocorticoid-induced tumor necrosis factor receptor (GITR) engagement on tumor-infiltrating group 2 ILCs (ILC2s) induced activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3) and robust interleukin-9 (IL-9) production, exceeding the modest coinduction of IL-5 and IL-13. ILC2-derived IL-9 promoted intratumoral eosinophil accumulation by enhancing survival, tissue retention, and cytotoxicity through tumor-induced IL-9 receptor expression. Eosinophil ablation abolished GITR-mediated tumor control, whereas adoptive eosinophil transfer restored it. This IL-9-eosinophil pathway suppressed tumor growth in the absence of adaptive lymphocytes. In human datasets, IL-9 and eosinophil signatures were associated with favorable prognosis in melanoma and lung adenocarcinoma. These findings define an innate pathway linking ILC2s to eosinophil-mediated tumor immunity and support GITR agonism as a therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Expression and Clinical Significance of Somatostatin Receptor 2 in Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Somatostatin receptor 2 (SSTR2) has important diagnostic and therapeutic implications in neuroendocrine tumors, but studies on its expression and clinical significance in medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) remain limited with inconsistent findings. SSTR2 expression was evaluated in 75 MTC patients using two scoring methods: the percentage of positive tumor cells and the H-score. Its associations with clinicopathological features were then analyzed. These results were derived from both manual assessment by pathologists and validated using an automated digital analysis platform. Of 75 cases, 61.3% (46) were SSTR2-positive (>5% positive cells), with a median manual H-score of 0.15 (range 0-2.7). A higher manual H-score was associated with octreotide scintigraphy positivity (P = 0.019). Within SSTR2-positive cases, lymph node metastasis decreased from low to high expression (80.0% vs. 73.3% vs. 27.3%, P = 0.015), and the median manual H-score was lower in high-grade than in low-grade tumors (0.00 vs. 0.25, P = 0.010). In univariate analysis, patients with non-high SSTR2 expression (≤50% positive cells) had higher odds of elevated calcitonin at final follow-up (OR 4.17, P = 0.047). Digital and manual assessments showed directionally consistent clinicopathological associations, and the digital H-score correlated strongly with the manual H-score (Spearman ρ = 0.778, P < 0.001). SSTR2 expression in MTC varies widely between patients. High SSTR2 expression appears associated with reduced tumor aggressiveness and a higher likelihood of biochemical cure.

papers.title: Unusual Gastric Metastases in the Setting of Recurrence of Pancreatic NET: Dual Tracer PET/CT and Theranostic Approach.
papers.abstract: Gastric metastases from neuroendocrine tumors (NET) are infrequently encountered. Commonly, locally advanced pancreatic NET can involve stomach resulting in inoperable presentation. We herein present a case of gastric wall metastatic disease in postoperative pancreatic NET, which was identified on [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE-PET/CT as recurrence of disease after prolong progression-free period. [18F]F-FDG avidity of the lesions on [18F]F-FDG-PET/CT indicated requirement of chemotherapy alone, or in combination with [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT). Hence, dual-tracer PET/CT imaging proved important in identifying unusual metastatic disease site and deciding therapeutic strategies in GEP-NET after a long follow-up period following surgical removal of primary disease.

papers.title: Mast cell phenotypic remodeling toward a PD-1-positive, Chymase-negative phenotype is associated with metastatic melanoma and poor survival.
papers.abstract: Mast cells (MCs) display phenotypic heterogeneity across tissues and disease contexts, yet their relevance in melanoma remains unclear. Here, we investigated MC phenotypic programs associated with melanoma progression using high-dimensional phenotyping of MCs co-cultured with melanoma spheroids, trajectory inference, and transcriptomic analyzes. Human melanoma tissues showed differences in MC phenotypic composition despite comparable abundance between outcome groups, with metastatic melanomas enriched for Tryptase⁺ Chymase- MCs. Melanoma exposure induced MC phenotypic remodeling, characterized by loss of lineage- and effector-associated features and increased PD-1 expression, with more pronounced changes following metastatic melanoma co-culture. Trajectory analysis was consistent with a continuum toward a PD-1⁺ Chymase- phenotype, which was detected in melanoma tissues and enriched within intratumoral regions of metastatic melanomas. Experimentally defined protein changes were used to derive two MC-associated transcriptomic signatures with opposing clinical associations, reflecting lineage- and effector-enriched versus melanoma-remodeled programs. The MC-LE signature was associated with favorable survival and interferon-responsive pathways, whereas the MC-MR signature was associated with poorer survival and tumor-associated pathways. These transcriptomic associations extended beyond melanoma across multiple TCGA cancer cohorts, and independent analysis of MCs from healthy skin, basal cell carcinoma, and melanoma showed corresponding differences in MC-LE-related features. Together, these findings support distinct mast cell phenotypic programs associated with melanoma progression and identify a PD-1⁺ Chymase- MC phenotype enriched in metastatic disease and linked to transcriptomic features of poor survival.

papers.title: Gastric Mixed Neuroendocrine-Non-neuroendocrine Neoplasms Develop from POU2F3+ Multipotent Progenitors.
papers.abstract: Gastric mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs) are aggressive malignancies that exhibit complex cellular heterogeneity driven by the dual lineages. The dismal patient survival rates highlight the need to elucidate the cellular origin of gastric MiNENs and the key regulatory mechanisms to develop improved treatment strategies. Here, we identified a gastric POU2F3+epithelial population as a potential cell of origin for gastric MiNENs. Lineage tracing and single-cell RNA sequencing further identified that POU2F3+ cells include three distinct subpopulations with divergent differentiation trajectories: progenitor cells (SOX2+SOX9+), tuft cells (POU2F3+DCLK1+), and neuroendocrine cells (SYP+CHGA+). Combined Rb1/Trp53 deletion and MYC overexpression in POU2F3+ epithelial cells (Pou2f3-CreERT; Rb1fl/fl; Trp53fl/fl; LSL-MycT58A) led to the rapid development of gastric MiNENs containing both neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine lesions, recapitulating human gastric MiNENs pathology. Transcription factor activity analysis and spatial transcriptomics revealed SOX2 and SOX9 as critical regulators driving subpopulation specification, with SOX2 and SOX9 being enriched in dysplasia and adenocarcinoma, respectively. Bulk RNA sequencing further showed increased expression of CXCL5 in gastric MiNENs, and inhibition of CXCL5 reduced the growth of tumor organoids and xenografts in mouse models. Together these findings offer a physiologically relevant model for studying gastric MiNENs and identify CXCL5 as a potential therapeutic target for this heterogeneous cancer.

papers.title: Discovery and Synthesis of Selective Casein Kinase 1δ Degraders for Suppressing Oncogenic NRAS-Mutant Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Activating NRAS mutations occur in approximately 20% of melanomas but remain largely undruggable due to the lack of effective targeted therapies. We previously identified casein kinase 1δ (CK1δ) as a critical upstream regulator that stabilizes oncogenic NRAS mutants. However, no selective CK1δ inhibitors have advanced to clinical evaluation. Here, we report the discovery of 8u, a selective CK1δ degrader derived from PF-670462. Compound 8u potently degrades CK1δ in NRASQ61R melanoma cells (DC50 = 1.25 μM, Dmax = 74%) via the ubiquitin-proteasome system, sparing against the closely related isoform CK1α and CK1ε. CK1δ degradation induced by 8u leads to destabilization of NRASQ61R and attenuation of downstream signaling pathways. Furthermore, 8u elicited significant tumor regression (TGI = 58.9%) in an NRASQ61R xenograft model in vivo at 30 mg/kg. The studies establish targeted degradation of CK1δ as a promising therapeutic strategy for NRAS-mutant melanoma.

papers.title: Imaging features of pituitary Crooke cell adenoma: a 13-case series.
papers.abstract: Crooke cell adenoma (CCA) is a rare and aggressive subtype of pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET). This study aimed to characterize the imaging features of CCA. Preoperative and postoperative follow-up MR images of 13 patients with CCA were retrospectively reviewed to characterize their imaging features in conjunction with clinical and pathological findings. Among the 13 CCAs, 8 (61.5%) were macroadenomas and 5 (38.5%) were microadenomas. On T1-weighted imaging, 12 tumors (92.3%) were isointense. On T2-weighted imaging, 6 (46.2%) were hyperintense, 4 (30.8%) were hypointense, and 3 (23.1%) were isointense. Macroadenomas were predominantly hyperintense (5/8) or isointense (3/8), whereas microadenomas were predominantly hypointense (4/5). Multiple microcystic changes were observed in 2 macroadenomas (15.4%). Mild contrast enhancement was observed in 10 tumors (76.9%). Knosp grade 1 was the most common pattern of parasellar extension (8/13, 61.5%). During postoperative follow-up of 2-39 months, tumor progression occurred in 4 patients (30.8%), all of whom had undergone subtotal resection. Retrospective review of their preoperative contrast-enhanced MRI showed reduced enhancement of the tumor-adjacent internal carotid artery wall (ICAW) in all four cases. CCA exhibits several imaging characteristics, particularly mild contrast enhancement and a tumor size-related T2-weighted signal pattern. Knosp grade 1 was the most frequent parasellar extension pattern. Reduced enhancement of the tumor-adjacent ICAW was observed in four cases with postoperative tumor progression; however, the clinical significance of this finding requires validation in larger cohorts with longer-term follow-up.

papers.title: Special AT-rich sequence-binding protein 2-positive primary small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the urinary bladder: A diagnostic pitfall.
papers.abstract: Special AT-rich sequence-binding protein 2 (SATB2) expression in conjunction with CK20 expression has been established as a specific marker for the detection of colorectal adenocarcinomas. Recently, its expression in foregut, midgut, and hindgut neuroendocrine neoplasms has been documented. SATB2 expression has been documented in neuroendocrine neoplasms from various primary sites; however, its expression in the urinary bladder has not been reported. A case of primary small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the urinary bladder (SmCCB) is presented, where strong SATB2 expression led to the suspicion of metastatic neuroendocrine carcinomatous deposits from the lower gastrointestinal tract. However, on positron emission tomography-computed tomography scan, no fluorodeoxyglucose-avid lesion elsewhere in the body was found, which established the diagnosis of primary SmCCB with SATB2 expression.
papers.journal: Indian journal of urology : IJU : journal of the Urological Society of India

papers.title: Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Microtumors: Etiology, Diagnostic Criteria, and Differential Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic neuroendocrine microtumors represent small, well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms (<5 mm) that are widely regarded as early lesions within the spectrum of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumorigenesis; however, their biological behavior remains a matter of an ongoing debate. Although frequently associated with hereditary tumor syndromes such as multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 and von Hippel-Lindau disease, pancreatic neuroendocrine microtumors also occur sporadically and are increasingly detected incidentally. In this review, we summarize their histopathological features, including key differential diagnoses, outline current insights into their molecular pathogenesis, and highlight unresolved issues in their clinical and diagnostic management. Pancreatic neuroendocrine microtumors are small, low-proliferative neoplastic lesions arising in the islets of Langerhans and are considered precursor lesions of fully developed pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. Increased proliferative activity and lymph node metastases are exceedingly rare. In contrast to non-neoplastic, hyperplastic islets, they show an altered distribution of islet cell hormones, which represents a key feature distinguishing them from their principal differential diagnosis.

papers.title: Resolution of hypertension following adrenalectomy in patients with pheochromocytoma and Conn's syndrome: A comparative cohort study.
papers.abstract: There is limited literature comparing the resolution of hypertension after adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma and Conn's syndrome endocrine hypertension. We assessed the rate of hypertension remission and factors predicting it among patients undergoing adrenalectomy. As part of an institutional review board-approved study, we retrieved data of patients who underwent adrenalectomy for localized pheochromocytoma or Conn's syndrome between 2020 and 2024 at our institution. Patients were contacted telephonically to assess the status of their hypertension. Out of 61 eligible patients, 31 with pheochromocytoma and 16 with Conn's syndrome were included in this study. Patients with pheochromocytoma were younger (mean age: 30.8 years vs. 42.8 years), had a lower body mass index (20.7 kg/m2 vs. 28.4 kg/m2), had a lower preoperative duration of hypertension (median- 12 vs. 84 months), and had fewer antihypertensive medicines (median 2 vs. 4) than patients with Conn's syndrome. At discharge, 82.6% (n = 19/23) of pheochromocytoma patients achieved complete hypertension remission vs. 31.2% (n = 5/16) of Conn's syndrome patients (P < 0.01). At 1 year after surgery, remission was maintained in 85% (17/20) and 50% (7/14) of patients, respectively (P = 0.05). Older age (odds ratio [OR]: 1.08), worse preoperative disease burden (OR: 2.23), multifocal lesions on histopathology (OR: 12.27), and chronic kidney disease (OR: 15.43) were associated with persistence of hypertension postoperatively. Adrenalectomy achieves quicker and more complete resolution of hypertension in patients with pheochromocytoma than in Conn's syndrome. Persistent hypertension is more likely in older patients with long standing, severe baseline hypertension, and other comorbidities.
papers.journal: Indian journal of urology : IJU : journal of the Urological Society of India

papers.title: When Every Test Fails: Multifocal Grade 1 Ileal Neuroendocrine Tumors Causing Transfusion-Dependent Obscure Overt Gastrointestinal Bleeding.
papers.abstract: Small bowel neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) rarely present as obscure overt gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB), causing significant diagnostic challenges. We report a 56-year-old man who presented with OGIB that required approximately 50 units of packed red blood cells during a 6-week hospitalization. Multimodal evaluation, including computed tomography angiography, tagged red blood cell scan, video capsule endoscopy, computed tomography enterography, provocative mesenteric angiography, balloon enteroscopy, and octreotide scan, failed to identify a source. Exploratory laparotomy identified 3 mid-ileal nodules with histopathology revealing well-differentiated grade 1 neuroendocrine tumors. Bleeding resolved following resection. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic role of surgical exploration in refractory OGIB.

papers.title: UPF1-mediated mRNA decay promotes melanoma tumorigenesis through miR-101-3p-dependent destabilization of NANOS1.
papers.abstract: Numerous studies have reported Up-frameshift protein 1 (UPF1) as a crucial posttranscriptional regulator in nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD), attributing its role to tumorigenesis across various cancers. However, its recently unveiled function in UPF1-mediated mRNA decay (UMD), intricately coordinated with miRNA, remains unexplored in the context of tumorigenesis. Here, we demonstrate that UPF1 contributes to melanoma tumorigenesis by regulating NANOS1 expression in a miR-101-3p-dependent manner. Depletion of UPF1 across three melanoma cell lines significantly impaired cell growth, migration, and invasion by cell cycle arrest and disrupted tumor formation in vivo. Through comprehensive RNA-seq and biochemical analyses, we elucidate that attenuation of UPF1 leads to an increase in NANOS1 expression, consequently suppressing melanoma tumorigenesis. Mechanistically, UPF1 orchestrates the destabilization of NANOS1 via UPF1-mediated mRNA decay (UMD) facilitated by miR-101-3p. Intriguingly, UPF1 depletion and NANOS1 upregulation were associated with reduced ERK and ELK1 phosphorylation, suggesting that attenuation of MAPK/ERK/ELK1 signaling may contribute, at least in part, to the observed melanoma-suppressive phenotypes. Importantly, the biological relevance of UPF1 and NANOS1 in melanoma cell lines was further supported in drug-resistant melanoma cells and in xenograft mouse models. Collectively, these findings expand our understanding of UMD in melanoma and identify the UPF1/NANOS1 regulatory relationship as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in both parental and drug-resistant melanoma cells.

papers.title: Neuronal intermediate filament neurologic autoimmunity in a patient with Merkel cell carcinoma receiving pembrolizumab.
papers.abstract: Neuronal intermediate filament (NIF) autoimmunity is an uncommon paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome that has increasingly been recognized in association with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Merkel cell carcinoma is among the malignancies most frequently associated with NIF antibodies, although reported cases remain limited. A 55-year-old female with stage IIIA Merkel cell carcinoma developed vertigo, gait instability, dysarthria, and persistent right hemifacial and cervical spasms after receiving second dose of pembrolizumab for recurrent disease. Brain MRI was unremarkable, while continuous electroencephalography demonstrated encephalopathy without a definitive electrocerebral correlate, raising suspicion for subcortical myoclonus. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein. CSF and positive NIF antibodies using cell-based assay. Pembrolizumab was discontinued, and the patient was treated with high-dose corticosteroids followed by monthly intravenous immunoglobulin, resulting in near complete resolution of her neurologic symptoms after 6 months. This case expands the growing spectrum of ICI-associated NIF paraneoplastic neurologic autoimmunity complicating Merkel cell carcinoma. To our knowledge, persistent hemifacial and cervical spasm has rarely been reported in this clinical setting. Early recognition of this syndrome, prompt antibody testing, discontinuation of ICI therapy, and initiation of therapy may improve neurological outcomes while informing further oncologic management.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology

papers.title: Unusual metastatic recurrence of pulmonary adenocarcinoma with a focal neuroendocrine component presenting with bilateral renal metastases and an accompanying pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor-like lesion: a case report.
papers.abstract: A 72-year-old woman with a history of resected lung adenocarcinoma presented with a pancreatic mass and multiple bilateral renal masses. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition of the pancreatic lesion showed neuroendocrine morphology, synaptophysin positivity, focal chromogranin A positivity, and a Ki-67 labeling index of 2%, leading to an initial diagnosis of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor grade 1. Renal biopsy also demonstrated neuroendocrine differentiation with a Ki-67 labeling index of 17%. However, the pancreatic lesion was hypovascular and poorly defined, and the multifocal bilateral renal involvement was atypical for a low-grade pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. Re-evaluation of the resected lung specimen revealed a focal neuroendocrine component showing large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma-like features, although the strict diagnostic criteria for such a diagnosis were not fully met. Genomic analysis identified a KRAS G12V mutation shared by the renal and lung tumors, supporting the interpretation that the renal lesions represented metastatic recurrence of the previously resected lung tumor. Direct molecular confirmation was unavailable for the pancreatic lesion because of insufficient residual endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition material; therefore, its origin remained diagnostically uncertain. Nevertheless, based on the overall clinicopathological context, the pancreatic lesion was interpreted as an accompanying neuroendocrine tumor-like lesion most consistent with metastatic recurrence. This case highlights the importance of integrating clinical history, imaging features, disease distribution, archival pathology, and molecular findings when evaluating neuroendocrine tumor-like lesions in patients with a prior malignancy.

papers.title: A rare collision tumor of paraganglioma and intravascular large B-cell lymphoma: a case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma (IVLBCL) is a rare and aggressive subtype of extranodal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. It is characterized by the selective proliferation of lymphoma cells within the lumina of small blood vessels. Collision tumors involving IVLBCL are exceedingly rare, and no cases involving paraganglioma as a collision component have been reported to date. We report the case of an 80-year-old man who presented with nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms and intermittent fever. Imaging studies suggested biliary and intra-abdominal malignancies. Surgical resection revealed a mesenteric mass. Histopathological examination demonstrated features consistent with paraganglioma. Notably, numerous atypical lymphoid cells were identified within the lumina of small vessels in the tumor. Immunohistochemical analysis showed positivity for CD20, CD19, PAX5, MUM1, and BCL2, supporting a diagnosis of IVLBCL. Epstein-Barr virus-encoded RNA (EBER) in situ hybridization was negative. Systemic involvement was excluded based on clinical evaluation and imaging findings. The final diagnosis was IVLBCL in collision with paraganglioma. Given the patient's advanced age and poor performance status, intensive chemotherapy was considered unsuitable, and targeted therapy with 'Surufatinib' was initiated. During follow-up, no recurrence of the primary tumor was observed. However, the patient subsequently developed duodenal adenocarcinoma and received appropriate treatment. The patient died approximately two years after the initial diagnosis. To the best of our knowledge, based on a systematic literature search in PubMed up to April 2026, this is the first reported case of a collision tumor composed of paraganglioma and IVLBCL. This case underscores the diagnostic challenges of IVLBCL due to its nonspecific presentation and its potential to be overlooked when coexisting with other tumors. Careful histopathological evaluation, particularly of intravascular components, is essential for accurate diagnosis. Increased awareness may facilitate early detection and improve patient outcomes.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomic and Proteomic Analysis Identifies Novel Immune-Associated Biomarkers of Anti-PD1 Response in Metastatic Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Resistance to anti-PD1 therapy remains a major challenge in metastatic melanoma, despite long-term benefit in some patients. Since a functional dendritic cell (DC)-CD8+ T cell axis is essential for anti-PD1 response, biomarkers associated with this axis may help characterize underexplored immune states linked to resistance. Here, we further characterized poor survival predictor (PSP) biomarkers previously negatively correlated with DC-CD8+ T cell axis in melanoma, evaluating their associations with anti-PD1 response, immune infiltration, and transcriptional and proteomic signatures. Pre-treatment transcriptomic data were analysed using CIBERSORTx and Reactome, while NanoString GeoMx spatial transcriptomic and proteomic data were used to resolve biomarker-associated features across tumour and immune compartments. We identified 28 PSP biomarkers significantly increased in non-responsive patients with strong correlations with one another, suggesting coordinated transcriptional patterns within a tumour microenvironment unfavourable to therapeutic response and survival. These biomarkers were associated with immunosuppressive cell types, decreased cytotoxicity, and pathways related to transcription, translation, epigenetic regulation, and signal transduction. Spatially, PSP biomarkers were expressed in both tumour and immune compartments, but survival associations were compartment- and site-specific. Among them, FAM57A, GSTA4 and KCTD1 were associated with poor survival when highly expressed in the CD45+ immune compartment of lymph node metastases. Their expression was associated with transcriptomic signatures of reduced immune activation, altered antigen presentation, and epigenetic regulation, and increased proteomic PI3K-AKT-mTORC1/MAPK signalling, especially upon co-expression. Together, these results identify FAM57A, GSTA4 and KCTD1 as emerging immune-associated biomarkers linked to established resistance-associated immune states and poor prognosis in metastatic melanoma.

papers.title: Effectiveness, safety, and retreatment outcomes in GEP-NET patients undergoing 177Lu-based PRRT: a ten-year real-world experience.
papers.abstract: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) using 177Lu-labeled somatostatin analogues is an established and increasingly applied treatment for advanced gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs). We report results focusing on effectiveness, short-term safety, and retreatment outcomes, based on ten years of clinical experience from an Austrian center of expertise, including patients referred for retreatment after prior therapy elsewhere. This retrospective study included 49 patients treated with 177Lu-DOTATATE or 177Lu-DOTATOC between 2014 and 2023. Subgroups included patients receiving their first PRRT course at our center (n = 45). Of this initial-treatment cohort, 9 patients subsequently underwent PRRT retreatment at our center. Additionally, 4 external patients previously treated with 90Y-PRRT at another institution were referred for 177Lu-based retreatment, resulting in a total retreatment subgroup of 13 patients. Overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and selected laboratory toxicity parameters were evaluated according to CTCAE v5.0. In the GEP-NET group, the median number of PRRT cycles was 4 with a median cumulative activity of 27.9 GBq. Median OS was 54.2 months (95% CI: 33.2-upper bound not reached), and median PFS was 24.1 months (95% CI: 11.8-36.1). PET-CT-based response assessment was available in 36 of 45 patients. Using evaluable patients as denominator, the exploratory visual SSTR-PET-CT-based objective response rate was 30.6%. Considering the entire initial-treatment cohort and assuming patients without follow-up imaging were non-responders, the ORR was 24.4%. Grade 3 or higher hematologic toxicity occurred in 4.4% of patients with one case each of grade 3 anemia and grade 4 leukopenia while no grade 3 or higher renal toxicity was observed. One patient (2%) developed myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), followed by acute myeloid leukemia (AML). In the retreatment group (median 4 additional cycles), the median PFS was 18.1 months (95% CI: 8.6-24.6) and the ORR was 30.8% (n = 13). No grade ≥3 toxicities or hematologic malignancies were observed. PRRT at our institution showed clinical outcomes and a favorable short-term safety profile broadly consistent with previously published PRRT studies. These findings support the role of PRRT in routine clinical practice. Retreatment outcomes appeared encouraging in selected patients but should be interpreted as exploratory given the limited cohort size, retrospective design, and absence of formal comparative analysis.

papers.title: [Workout with consequences].
papers.abstract: A 61-year-old female patient with a short history of recurrent episodes of exercise-induced dizziness and syncope presented to our internal medicine department for further examination after an initial tonic-clonic seizure. Following an extensive diagnostic evaluation, the cause was found to be an insulinoma, which was successfully treated.

papers.title: p38α orchestrates BRAFV600E-melanoma progression and immunotherapy response via tumor fitness and immune microenvironment modulation.
papers.abstract: Understanding how tumor cells shape the tumor microenvironment (TME) and evade the host immune response is critical for developing novel therapeutic combinations. In this study, we identify tumor cell p38α as a therapeutic target that restricts antitumor immunity and contributes to resistance against immune-checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Genetic analyses of mouse and human melanomas reveal alterations in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK)-stress pathway, including upregulation of MAPK14. We demonstrate a dual role for p38α in ultraviolet-B (UVB)-induced Braf V600E melanoma, acting as a tumor suppressor during melanocyte transformation but promoting melanoma growth and progression. Mechanistically, p38α impairs cytotoxic immune responses, modulates immunosuppressive myeloid cells, and regulates inflammatory mediators that shape the TME. Loss or inhibition of p38α enhances and restores sensitivity to PD-1 blockade, resulting in tumor regression and improved overall survival. Moreover, a p38α-associated gene signature correlates with favorable immunotherapy outcomes in patients with melanoma, underscoring its translational relevance.

papers.title: Specialized cancer care for medullary thyroid cancer: A Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-Medicare study of Traditional Fee-For-Service and Medicare Advantage beneficiaries.
papers.abstract: Medullary thyroid cancer is rare and requires specialized knowledge. Medicare Advantage is associated with reduced access to top-rated cancer hospitals and worse outcomes for complex cancer surgery than Traditional Fee-for-Service Medicare. Whether this applies to medullary thyroid cancer is unknown. We described access to accredited cancer centers and compared outcomes between Traditional Fee-for-Service Medicare and Medicare Advantage beneficiaries with medullary thyroid cancer. This retrospective cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries who underwent surgery for a new diagnosis of medullary thyroid cancer in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-Medicare database (2018-2021) examined the association between Medicare type (Traditional Fee-for-Service Medicare or Medicare Advantage) and utilization of a Commission on Cancer-accredited center, with stratification by state. Logistic regression models evaluated risk-adjusted Commission on Cancer hospital utilization. We identified 381 patients, of whom 231 (60.6%) were enrolled in Traditional Fee-for-Service Medicare and 150 (39.4%) in Medicare Advantage. In the overall analysis, there were no significant differences in accredited cancer center utilization by Medicare type (Traditional Fee-for-Service Medicare: 83.6% versus Medicare Advantage: 78.0%; P = .22). When stratified by state, Medicare Advantage beneficiaries were less often treated at accredited cancer centers in California and New York. Postoperative complications, delayed reoperation, and disease-specific survival did not differ significantly by Medicare type. Medicare type is associated with state-level variation in the utilization of accredited cancer centers for medullary thyroid cancer surgical care. Patients with medullary thyroid cancer should consider access issues in their local context when selecting Medicare plan types. Outcome studies of health care utilization by Medicare plan type must consider the geographic setting as a component of their analysis to responsibly report results.

papers.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Cancer Risk in Obesity Treatment.
papers.abstract: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for numerous cancers, with body habitus, especially central adiposity, contributing to increased cancer incidence and worse prognosis. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), initially developed to treat Type 2 diabetes, have rapidly gained prominence as powerful anti-obesity agents due to their ability to induce significant weight loss and potential to improve metabolic health. These medications act by reducing appetite, enhancing insulin sensitivity, lowering systemic inflammation, and preferentially targeting fat mass for reduction. This review explores the growing body of evidence linking GLP-1 RA therapy to potential changes in cancer risk among individuals with obesity. To date, data suggest that GLP-1 RAs do not increase overall cancer risk and may reduce the risk of certain obesity-related cancers, likely by interrupting obesity-driven metabolic dysregulation. Still, questions remain about the beneficial effects of weight loss and the sustainability of health benefits if weight is regained after stopping treatment. We examine how GLP-1 RAs' anti-inflammatory and metabolic effects might mediate reductions in cancer risk, review emerging data regarding both protective signals and specific safety concerns (e.g., increased risk of medullary thyroid carcinoma), and emphasize the critical role of combining pharmacotherapy with lifestyle interventions to maintain muscle mass and long-term weight loss. Ultimately, given the strong link between obesity and cancer, GLP-1 RAs represent a promising new class of agents that may not only help to manage obesity but also serve as effective chemopreventive tools against obesity-associated cancers.
papers.journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity

papers.title: Carcinoids of the lung caused by exogenous noxious agents: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Approximately 2% of lung tumours are pulmonary carcinoids (PCs), divided into typical (90%) and atypical (AC) (10%). The link with external exposure to carcinogens remains controversial. To investigate the association between occupational exposure to carcinogens and PC tumours. A PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review was performed. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed and Embase (January 2025). Studies were reviewed, data extracted, analysed and summarised narratively. 1302 studies were reviewed. 27 original studies and seven conference papers on topics including exposure to cigarette smoke (n=23) and asbestos (n=6), or mechanistic information, were included. Following the collapse of the World Trade Center in 2001, carcinoids accounted for 6% of lung cancer cases in people exposed to the resulting dust (9% in women, 3% in men). The proportion of ACs among carcinoids rose from 9.3% (controls) to 16.3% (smokers) and from ∼25% to 45% (probable versus definite asbestos exposure). Basic research has identified biological pathways linking harmful exposures (such as asbestos and cigarette smoke) to neuroendocrine cell proliferation and the potential progression of PCs to higher-grade lung tumours. The significance these of findings is limited due to 1) the limited number of studies, 2) the small number of tumours within those studies and 3) the lack of rigid diagnostic (morphological and molecular) criteria for PCs in most studies. Nevertheless, a consistent finding is a higher proportion of AC among carcinoids, particularly following asbestos exposure. Based on these findings, a link between carcinogenic substances (especially asbestos and cigarette smoke) and carcinoids seems plausible. More stringent analyses in epidemiological surveys are needed to further clarify the pathogenesis of PCs.
papers.journal: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society

papers.title: Adrenal Collision Tumors: A Practical Application of the Existing Evidence.
papers.abstract: Adrenal collision tumors (ACTs) are rare lesions in which two histologically distinct tumors coexist within the same adrenal gland. They are almost always incidental findings, and although their heterogeneous, dual-component appearance can raise concern for malignancy, they seldom represent a distinct clinical problem. The principal pitfall they create is radiologic rather than biochemical: the mixed composition of an ACT renders the adrenal CT washout protocol unreliable and can mimic a neoplasm. The established adrenal incidentaloma pathway (biochemical exclusion of pheochromocytoma and adrenocortical carcinoma, imaging phenotyping, and size- and growth-based surveillance) reliably identifies both a functional and a malignant component of a collision tumor . Drawing on institutional experience and the published case literature, this narrative review describes the entity and its imaging caveats, and shows how the standard pathway can be applied to risk-stratify low-risk lesions and avoid unnecessary surgery while selecting appropriate first-line imaging.
papers.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists

papers.title: Prognostic Performance of AJCC Version 9 versus Other Staging Systems for Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors.
papers.abstract: Several anatomical staging systems are used for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNETs), but their comparative prognostic performance in a common surgical cohort remains uncertain. We compared AJCC Version 9, European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society (ENETS), modified ENETS (mENETS), and modified AJCC (mAJCC) staging. This retrospective multicenter cohort included 891 patients who underwent pNET resection between 2000 and 2023 and had assignable stage under all four systems. Performance was assessed using homogeneity, monotonicity, Harrell concordance index (C-index), Akaike information criterion (AIC), and integrated time-dependent area under the curve (iAUC). C-index uncertainty and optimism were evaluated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Overall survival (OS) was the primary outcome. All four systems stratified OS (all log-rank p < 0.001). In the final common comparable cohort, the estimated 3-, 5-, and 10-year OS rates were 91.8%, 87.7%, and 67.5%, respectively. ENETS had the highest likelihood-ratio chi-square (26.90), mENETS the highest linear-trend chi-square (22.10), and mAJCC the highest apparent C-index (0.681; bootstrap 95% CI, 0.616-0.742). AJCC Version 9 had the lowest AIC (1126.65) and highest iAUC (0.652). Bootstrap-corrected C-indices were 0.666 for AJCC Version 9, 0.654 for ENETS, 0.647 for mENETS, and 0.661 for mAJCC; confidence intervals overlapped. The equal-weight composite ranked AJCC Version 9 first as a descriptive summary. All four systems provided prognostic stratification, and no system dominated every evaluation domain. AJCC Version 9 had the most balanced descriptive profile, but the small differences do not establish clinical superiority or independently direct treatment or surveillance decisions.
papers.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal surgery : official journal of the Society for Surgery of the Alimentary Tract

papers.title: Imaging response to neoadjuvant checkpoint inhibitor therapy in Merkel cell carcinoma: Association with pathologic response.
papers.abstract: Radiographic biomarkers of response are needed to identify patients with Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) who respond to neoadjuvant immunotherapy. We evaluated FDG-PET/CT characteristics associated with pathologic response. Patients with stage III MCC treated with neoadjuvant immunotherapy and surgery (2021-2025) were retrospectively evaluated. Imaging response markers including standardized uptake value (SUVmax), total lesion glycolysis (TLG, g), and PET/CT tumor volume (cm3) were compared to pathologic response. Of 13 patients, 3 (23%) achieved pathologic complete response (no viable tumor), 4 (31%) achieved major response (<10% viable tumor), and 6 (46%) achieved partial/no response (>10% viable tumor). Among patients with pre- and post-neoadjuvant immunotherapy imaging (n = 7), greater reductions in SUVmax and PET/CT tumor volume were observed in complete responders; none achieved statistical significance. These preliminary findings highlight the need for larger prospective studies evaluating radiographic biomarkers of treatment response in MCC.

papers.title: Patterns of Care, Resource Disparities, and Professional Perceptions in Neuroendocrine Tumors in Mexico: A Nationwide Survey of Medical Oncologists.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) require accurate pathology, functional imaging, targeted therapies, and multidisciplinary care. We described NET care patterns and resource availability among Mexican medical oncologists in public and private settings. We conducted a nationwide survey of Mexican medical oncologists. The questionnaire assessed NET caseload, perception of pathology report completeness, use of biomarkers and echocardiography, access to multidisciplinary teams (MDTs) and interventional radiology (IR), availability of nuclear medicine studies and systemic therapies, and management in key clinical scenarios. For oncologists working in both sectors, responses were reshaped into a long format, yielding 142 practice-specific observations (71 public, 71 private). One hundred oncologists responded, and 54% reported seeing fewer than five NET patients per year. Nearly 80% perceived that NET pathology reports were incomplete or incongruent, only 9.9% reported frequent MDT meetings, and IR was available in 19.7% of practices. NET-specific somatostatin receptor (SSTR) positron emission tomography was concentrated in private practice (60.6% v 19.7% public), and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy was available in 20.4% (similar for both practices). Somatostatin analogs were the most widely available systemic therapy (73.2% overall; 84.5% private v 62.0% public). Active surveillance, chemotherapy use, and post-somatostatin analogues sequencing were heterogeneous, with sector differences in first-line treatment for SSTR-positive grade 3 NETs. This first nationwide survey of Mexican oncologists highlights substantial public-private inequities in NET diagnostics, therapies, and multidisciplinary support, alongside concerns about pathology quality and low NET caseloads. Strengthening pathology practice, imaging, treatment access, MDTs, and education may help close NET care gaps in Mexico and other middle-income settings.

papers.title: Curcuminoids and Dimethoxycurcumin as Therapeutic Agents in Melanoma: Focus on Metastasis and Primary Care Integration.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is a type of skin cancer associated with the uncontrolled growth of melanocytes, the pigment-producing cells. This type of skin cancer continues to be a major concern owing to its strong tendency to spread. Melanoma progression is influenced by the activation of various signalling pathways, such as PI3K/AKT/mTOR, MAPK/ERK, and Wnt/β-catenin pathways. Curcuminoids, derived from turmeric, are known for their anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties and influence the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway by acting on key molecules, such as mTORC1, PI3K, and AKT. Curcuminoids have demonstrated reduced ERK phosphorylation, which lowers MAPK pathway activity. Additionally, curcuminoids have been shown to block the cell cycle at the G2/M phase and consequently inhibit Wnt/β-catenin pathway signalling. This review aims to explore the potential use of curcumin, bisdemethoxycurcumin, demethoxycurcumin, and a synthetic analogue of curcumin, dimethoxycurcumin, in combating melanoma. This review stands out by comparing natural and synthetic curcuminoids against the signalling pathways that drive melanoma. The abovementioned curcuminoids and synthetic analogue have shown anti-cancer potential by targeting key molecular targets implicated in the PI3K/AKT/mTOR, MAPK/ERK pathways, paving the way for potential novel treatment approaches. Additionally, this review addresses the sustainable development goals and the role of curcuminoids in primary health care.

papers.title: Attitudes of cancer patients toward ctDNA-based liquid biopsy for follow-up.
papers.abstract: Circulating tumor DNA-based liquid biopsy is increasingly integrated into cancer care, particularly for detecting minimal residual disease, yet patient perspectives remain poorly understood. This single-center, cross-sectional, mixed-methods study assessed recall, knowledge, and attitudes toward liquid biopsy and circulating tumor DNA among 195 patients (median age 65 years; 63% female) undergoing cancer treatment or follow-up, supplemented by focus groups. Although 65% reported prior liquid biopsy, this was confirmed in only 44%, and only 10% had heard of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). Correct recall and knowledge on ctDNA were higher among patients with neuroendocrine neoplasms and those with postgraduate education. In hypothetical scenarios assuming proven clinical validity and utility, 62-80% supported liquid biopsy-guided clinical action, 74% were comfortable with liquid biopsy replacing tissue biopsy, and 79% accepted its use to guide adjuvant treatment. Most patients anticipated reassurance rather than stress, and 85% expected improved quality of life with home- or general practitioner-based blood sampling. Overall, patients showed high acceptance of clinically actionable liquid biopsy use, driven by trust and perceived clinical benefit.

papers.title: Amphicrine Carcinomas of the Pancreas Showing Neuroendocrine and Acinar Cell Differentiation: A Case Report and Literature Review.
papers.abstract: This study clarifies the distinct clinicopathological and molecular features of amphicrine pancreatic carcinoma (AmpCA) through a case analysis and literature review. We present a case of AmpCA in a 73-year-old female, characterized by co-expression of acinar cell markers and neuroendocrine markers within individual tumor cells. Molecular profiling revealed high-risk mutations in KRAS G12V, TP53, and RB1, along with a high Ki-67 index (85%). Literature comparison confirms that AmpCA exhibits a unique bidirectional, single-cell differentiation pattern, fundamentally distinguishing it from the bicellular composition of mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNEN). We conclude that AmpCA is a distinct malignant entity requiring specific diagnostic criteria, and its molecular profile suggests potential for targeted therapies.

papers.title: When an SSTR-negative lesion does not preclude RLT: the role of dual-tracer PET/CT in a neuroendocrine tumor.
Updates in Management of Merkel Cell Carcinoma: A Scoping Review for Surgeons.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare but aggressive carcinoma with rising incidence. This review summarizes key updates in the optimal surgical and medical management of MCC. Surgery remains the cornerstone of treatment for early-stage MCC, and sentinel node biopsy is important for accurate staging. Emerging salvage options represent critical areas of progress. Sensitive surveillance tools enable earlier recurrence detection. Surgeons play a central role in excision, staging, multidisciplinary coordination, and integration of emerging tools.

papers.title: [The institutionalization of vaccination in Spain: from smallpox to the National Vaccination Schedule (1803-1975)].
papers.abstract: Vaccination has played a central role in the historical development of public health in Spain and in the progressive institutionalization of state health intervention. From the late eighteenth century onwards, the fight against smallpox acted as a driving force for increasingly systematic preventive policies, evolving from variolation to jennerian vaccination and its administrative regulation. The Royal Philanthropic Vaccine Expedition (1803-1813) represented the first major milestone in this process, transforming vaccination into an organized, permanent practice under public authority. Throughout the nineteenth century, successive legal provisions consolidated this model, culminating in the creation of the National Vaccine Institute and in the establishment of compulsory vaccination and revaccination as structural public health policies. During the twentieth century, this framework was extended to other infectious diseases with major social impact. In the case of diphtheria, the introduction of antitoxin therapy and the subsequent development of active immunization led to the legal enforcement of compulsory vaccination in 1943. Later, the National Tuberculosis Eradication Plan (PNET), launched in the 1960s, represented the last major mass vaccination effort prior to the implementation of the National Vaccination Schedule, which integrated immunization into routine healthcare practice. This article examines the regulatory, institutional, and technical evolution of vaccination in Spain between 1803 and 1975, highlighting its key role in the consolidation of modern public health.

papers.title: Sequential Barrier Navigation by Yeast β-Glucan-Engineered Liposomal Nanovaccines Potentiates Oral Melanoma Immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Orally delivered protein antigens face gastrointestinal degradation and inefficient transport through mucus, across the intestinal epithelium, and into antigen-presenting cells (APCs). To address these barriers, we developed YGB@OVA/PBA-C-LIPs, an ovalbumin (OVA)-loaded cationic liposomal nanovaccine coated with yeast β-glucan (YGB) and functionalized with phenylboronic acid (PBA). We characterized the physicochemical properties of YGB@OVA/PBA-C-LIPs and evaluated their mucus and epithelial transport, macrophage uptake, OVA cross-presentation, and immune activation in vitro. Laminarin competition was used to assess β-glucan-sensitive uptake. Gastrointestinal residence, immune responses, antitumor activity, and tolerability were examined after oral administration to B16-OVA-bearing mice.
