YGB@OVA/PBA-C-LIPs averaged 127.5 ± 0.8 nm in diameter and had an OVA encapsulation efficiency of 83.17 ± 1.98%, with no marked size increase over 12 days at 4 °C. They improved transport through a simulated mucus layer and across the Caco-2/Raji B model and increased RAW264.7 macrophage uptake; laminarin attenuated this advantage, supporting a β-glucan-sensitive component of uptake. The formulation also increased surface CD80 and H-2Kb-SIINFEKL levels in DC2.4 cells and IFN-γ release in DC2.4-splenocyte co-cultures. After a single oral dose, the Cy7-labeled formulation remained detectable in the abdomen at 72 h. Repeated dosing reduced tumor weight by 75.0% versus untreated tumor-bearing controls (0.36 ± 0.11 versus 1.44 ± 0.23 g) and increased serum OVA-specific IgG reactivity to 3.8 times the control value. Major-organ histology showed no evident abnormalities. The YGB/PBA dual-functionalized formulation combined gastrointestinal protection and mucosal transport with enhanced antigen presentation by APCs, improving immune responses and tumor control in the B16-OVA model. Validation with clinically relevant tumor antigens is needed to establish broader therapeutic relevance.

papers.title: Familial lichen amyloidosis as a presenting sign of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A tumor syndrome.
Towards epigenetically informed and biobank-driven precision immunotherapy in melanoma.
papers.abstract: Cutaneous melanoma (CM) is a highly immunogenic and therapeutically intricate solid tumor, exemplifying the interactions between tumors and the immune system. Despite the significant enhancement in survival rates for patients with advanced melanoma due to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), numerous patients either exhibit resistance to these agents or develop immune evasion mechanisms. This underscores the pressing necessity to identify biological determinants of drug responses. A significant body of research indicates that epigenetic alterations, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling, are essential in modulating melanoma immunogenicity. This encompasses the modulation of antigen presentation, innate immune detection, interferon (IFN) signaling, melanoma plasticity, and the reconfiguration of the immune microenvironment. Furthermore, in contrast to genetic mutations, these mechanisms are reversible, positioning melanoma as a prime example of epigenetically regulated and potentially therapeutically targeted immune resistance. This review examines the novel insight that epigenetic therapies can enhance the immunological activity of "cold" or immune-excluded melanomas, transforming them into inflamed, drug-responsive tumors. This is achievable by restoring antigenicity and reactivating IFN-related pathways, leading to enhanced immune cell infiltration. The paper also addresses the necessity of longitudinal biobanking combined with integrated multi-omics analyses of epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and spatial profiling to investigate dynamic tumor-immune configurations, support the validation of candidate biomarkers, and explore biologically informed patient stratification. In conclusion, we propose an integrative model connecting epigenetic vulnerability, immune reconfiguration, and biobank-driven systems biology. This model is proposed as a research framework for investigating future biomarker informed immunotherapy strategies in melanoma.

papers.title: Merkel Cell Carcinoma Masquerading as Dermatitis.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare, highly aggressive neuroendocrine skin carcinoma that typically presents as a rapidly enlarging, firm, painless nodule on sun-exposed areas in elderly patients. This malignancy is characterized by high rates of local recurrence, regional spread, and distant metastasis. We report a case of a woman in her 80s who presented with an erythematous patch on the left anterior thigh, a non-sun-exposed site, initially diagnosed as inflammatory dermatitis and treated with topical corticosteroids. After two months of failed therapy and interval growth, a punch biopsy was performed. Histopathology revealed a dermal infiltrate of small to medium-sized cells with "salt and pepper" chromatin and numerous mitotic figures. Immunohistochemistry confirmed a diagnosis of MCC. Staging with positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) revealed an incidental pancreatic lesion with benign cytology and subsequent imaging stability but no evidence of metastatic disease. The staging workup was complicated by acute pancreatitis for which she was hospitalized, and during which she developed new-onset atrial fibrillation and congestive heart failure. After discharge, the patient underwent wide local excision; however, sentinel lymph node biopsy was deferred due to the patient's acute comorbidities. In conjunction with the patient, the decision was made for close surveillance rather than adjuvant radiation or systemic therapy. At the most recent follow-up, 16 months after excision, there was no evidence of recurrence. This case highlights an atypical presentation of MCC as a dermatitic-appearing patch in a non-sun-exposed area and underscores the importance of biopsy in atypical lesions that do not respond to treatment, as well as the need to individualize treatment in elderly patients with significant competing comorbidities.

papers.title: Variant-informed multimodal tissue-state modeling reveals an NRF2 stress niche and dependency axis in KEAP1/NFE2L2-altered cancer.
papers.abstract: Cancer genotypes influence transcriptional programs, spatial organization, histopathology, and treatment-response states, yet these molecular and tissue-level features are often analyzed separately in public-data studies. VISTA was developed as a variant-informed, multimodal framework for modeling genotype-linked tissue states and prioritizing validation-ready biological hypotheses. VISTA integrates somatic variants, protein-region and AlphaMissense-informed priors, RNA-state scoring, whole-slide image embeddings, immunotherapy cohorts, spatial and single-cell references, cell-line dependency maps, and pharmacogenomic screens. We evaluated the framework in KEAP1/NFE2L2-altered lung cancer and melanoma, using the NRF2 stress axis as a biologically defined test case. Analyses incorporated project-adjusted modeling, bootstrap confidence intervals, permutation testing, leave-project sensitivity analyses, independent tumor-level validation cohorts, fixed-effect external meta-analysis, model-system analyses using DepMap/CCLE, tissue-context analyses, immunotherapy cohorts, and exploratory whole-slide image analyses. In TCGA LUAD, LUSC, and SKCM pilot cohorts, KEAP1 and NFE2L2 alterations were consistently associated with NRF2 stress activation across project-adjusted models and sensitivity analyses. Independent analyses of CPTAC LUAD, CPTAC LSCC, and non-TCGA LUAD cohorts reproduced higher NRF2-state scores in KEAP1/NFE2L2-altered tumors. Fixed-effect external meta-analysis supported associations with both KEAP1 mutation and combined KEAP1-or-NFE2L2 alteration status. DepMap/CCLE analyses provided complementary model-system evidence: KEAP1/NFE2L2-mutant models had higher NRF2 scores, while NRF2-high or KEAP1/NFE2L2-mutant contexts showed stronger NFE2L2 dependency. Tissue-context analyses positioned NRF2 stress near hypoxic, stromal, myeloid, and immune programs. Immunotherapy cohorts supported the relevance of NRF2-associated states to treatment-response biology, while also indicating limited utility for static pan-cancer prediction. Exploratory whole-slide image analyses using pathology foundation-model embeddings identified morphology associations with myeloid, hypoxic, and CAF/TGF-beta barrier programs. VISTA provides an evidence-layered approach to variant-informed tissue-state modeling. By integrating genomic, transcriptomic, imaging, spatial, cellular, dependency, and pharmacogenomic evidence, it can help prioritize genotype-linked cancer states and validation-ready hypotheses. VISTA is not intended to function as a stand-alone clinical predictor; its claims are bounded by the evidence available in each data layer and by the biological and clinical context of the analyzed cohorts.

papers.title: [Digestive neuroendocrine tumors : the importance of a multidisciplinary approach].
papers.abstract: Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms form a heterogeneous and complex group of tumors with varying degrees of malignant potential. Their incidence has significantly increased in recent decades. Due to their generally indolent nature, they are often discovered incidentally or following extensive investigations for nonspecific symptoms, leading to diagnostic delays. Notable advances have been made in diagnostic and therapeutic options, including radionuclide therapy, endoscopic resection or radiofrequency ablation, somatostatin analogs, and targeted molecular therapies. A multidisciplinary approach is essential for their management, enabling clinicians to diagnose and treat these lesions optimally.

papers.title: Non-small cell lung carcinoma and its mimics on cytology and small biopsy samples: a practical approach aligned with the WHO Reporting System.
papers.abstract: Accurate classification of lung tumors in cytology specimens and small biopsies remains a diagnostic challenge because of limited cellularity, preanalytical variables, and significant morphologic overlap among entities. This review summarizes key cytomorphologic characteristics and practical immunocytochemical strategies, and common diagnostic pitfalls encountered in the evaluation of non-small cell lung carcinoma, small cell lung carcinoma, neuroendocrine tumors, secondary pulmonary neoplasms, and uncommon thoracic entities in endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration and fine-needle aspiration samples. Particular emphasis is placed on the appropriate use of limited immunohistochemical panels to optimize tumor subtyping while preserving material for molecular testing. Diagnostic challenges such as crush artifact, necrosis, reactive mimics, overlapping morphologic patterns, and the risk of misclassification of rare tumors are addressed with practical guidance for differential diagnosis. By integrating morphologic assessment with ancillary testing, cytopathologists can achieve accurate tumor subtyping, distinguish mimics, and provide precise diagnoses that guide clinical management and selection of targeted therapies.

papers.title: Danish translation and linguistic validation of the Melanoma Concerns Questionnaire.
papers.abstract: Increased focus on monitoring health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in melanoma patients has highlighted the need for validated instruments such as patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). Rather than developing new measures, it is generally recommended to translate and linguistically validate a suitable existing PROM. The Melanoma Concerns Questionnaire (MCQ-28) was adapted from English to Danish following the guidelines by the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research (ISPOR). A forward-and-backwards translation was conducted, followed by cognitive debriefing interviews based on the Consensus-based Standards for the Selection of Health Measurement Instruments (COSMIN), focusing on comprehensiveness, comprehensibility and relevance. The Danish MCQ-28 was tested on 21 patients, including seven in each risk group. Overall responses were positive, though several patients - especially those at a low risk or further in follow-up process - struggled with the timeframe of certain items. The interviews also revealed that some items were interpreted differently depending on individual patient perspectives. By following the ISPOR guideline, a culturally relevant, linguistically validated Danish version of the MCQ-28 was developed. It is a candidate for implementation in Danish melanoma follow-up and for use in international HRQoL research on melanoma patients; however, psychometric validation in a Danish context is necessary. The Herlev and Gentofte Hospital Research Fund. Not relevant.

papers.title: Recurrence Risk After Resection of Typical and Atypical Pulmonary Carcinoids: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary carcinoids generally have favorable outcomes after surgery, but postoperative recurrence differs substantially by histological subtype. Existing guidance recognizes atypical histology and nodal involvement as adverse features, yet a focused quantitative synthesis of the magnitude and consistency of this association remains limited. MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from inception to July 12, 2026 for surgical cohorts reporting postoperative recurrence. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts and assessed full-text eligibility, with disagreements resolved by consensus. The primary meta-analysis emphasized the risk ratio (RR) of observed recurrence in atypical versus typical carcinoids using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp intervals; odds ratios (ORs) and risk differences were complementary measures. Time-defined recurrence, adjusted prognostic factors, and anatomical patterns were synthesized separately because of incompatible outcome definitions and effect measures. Eighteen reports were included in the review, 11 contributed structured quantitative evidence, and 7 independent comparative cohorts entered the primary meta-analysis. Among 1074 resected tumors, recurrence occurred in 24 of 816 typical carcinoids and 51 of 258 atypical carcinoids. The pooled RR of observed recurrence was 6.57 (95% CI, 3.65-11.84), with a complementary OR of 8.08 (95% CI, 4.20-15.53). No statistical heterogeneity was detected (I2 = 0%), but this result was interpreted cautiously because only seven studies were available and clinically important differences in follow-up, staging, pathological review, and surveillance remained. Leave-one-out RR estimates ranged from 5.77 to 7.48. Time-defined evidence suggested recurrence of approximately 18%-25% by 5 years and 29%-32% by 10 years in atypical tumors, whereas node-negative typical tumors generally remained below 5% at 10 years, although late events occurred. Nodal involvement, advanced pT category, and larger tumor size were adverse prognostic features. Observed recurrence after resection was substantially more frequent in atypical than in typical pulmonary carcinoids. Histology and nodal status provide a clinically useful basis for postoperative risk stratification, but the available evidence does not establish the optimal surveillance modality, interval, or duration.

papers.title: Merkel cell polyomavirus DNA in CSF of paediatric patients with suspected meningitis or encephalitis.
papers.abstract: The clinical significance of Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV) in pediatric central nervous system (CNS) infections remains uncertain, particularly in immunocompromised children. To determine the frequency of MCPyV DNA in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from children with suspected viral meningitis or encephalitis and evaluate its association with HIV infection, CSF findings, and clinical outcomes. CSF samples from 46 pediatric patients with suspected viral CNS infection were analyzed using TaqMan probe-based quantitative PCR targeting the large T-antigen gene. Positive specimens were confirmed by amplification of an independent VP1 target and bidirectional Sanger sequencing following conventional PCR re-amplification. Clinical, laboratory, and outcome data were compared using appropriate statistical tests. MCPyV DNA was detected in 6/46 patients (13.0%), all of whom were HIV-positive (p = 0.001; sensitivity analysis excluding patients with unknown HIV status, p = 0.002). Four isolates belonged to genotype I and two to genotype IIc. Compared with MCPyV-negative patients, MCPyV-positive patients had higher CSF lymphocyte percentages (89% vs. 84%; p = 0.048), higher protein concentrations (79 vs. 68 mg/dL; p = 0.022), lower glucose concentrations (51 vs. 55 mg/dL; p = 0.038), and more frequent altered consciousness (83.3% vs. 37.5%; p = 0.039). EBV DNA co-detection was identified in one MCPyV-positive patient. MCPyV DNA was detected exclusively in HIV-positive children and was associated with inflammatory CSF abnormalities. These findings suggest a possible association between MCPyV detection, immunosuppression, and CNS inflammation but do not establish causality. Larger multicenter studies are required.

papers.title: Spontaneous phase separation-driven Janus hydrogel spatiotemporally orchestrates the fibrotic progression for functional tendon regeneration.
papers.abstract: Postoperative tendon regeneration hinges on the precise spatiotemporal orchestration of fibrotic progression, aberrant fibrogenesis instead drives pathological adhesion formation and impairs functional recovery. However, current strategies often target isolated aspects of fibrotic progression and rely on complex fabrication procedures. Here, we engineer a Janus hydrogel (SPS-JH) via spontaneous phase separation-driven stratification and photopolymerization of methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAM) and poly(lactide)-b-poly(propylene glycol)-b-poly(lactide) dimethacrylate (PLD). This innate water/oil demixing yields a Janus architecture in which the outer HAM layer establishes a lubricated anti-adhesion interface, while the inner PLD layer confers durable mechanical reinforcement. Critically, the SPS-JH decodes the temporal hierarchy of tendon repair: the MMP-2-degradable HAM layer releases COX-2 siRNA to silence fibroblast hyperactivation during early inflammation, whereas the PLD matrix sustains niclosamide (NEN) release to polarize macrophages during inflammation and suppress fibrogenesis during proliferation. In rats with Achilles tendon injury, SPS-JH reduces peritendinous adhesions and promotes biomechanically competent, functional tendon regeneration. Transcriptomic analysis reveals coordinated activation of mechanotransduction and tissue remodeling programs accompanied by suppressed fibrogenic signaling. This work establishes a structurally minimalist yet biologically sophisticated paradigm wherein spontaneous phase separation coordinates with the dynamic fibrotic progression to enable functional tendon regeneration.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic and network analysis elucidates the multi-target molecular mechanisms of carboplatin in melanoma.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is an aggressive malignancy with high metastatic potential and frequent resistance to standard therapies, highlighting the need for robust biomarkers and improved mechanistic understanding of effective treatments. This study integrates transcriptomic profiling and network-based analyses to identify key regulatory genes and clarify how clinically used agents may counteract melanoma-specific molecular dysregulation. Comparative evaluation of three independent gene expression datasets yielded 194 overlapping differentially expressed genes (DEGs) enriched in pathways central to tumor progression. A protein-protein interaction network was constructed, and hub genes were prioritized using the Maximal Clique Centrality algorithm, revealing critical nodes involved in melanoma biology. Drug-gene interaction analysis via DGIdb identified carboplatin as a multi-target compound interacting with CDKN1A, BRCA1, PTEN, and AKT1. Although carboplatin, often combined with paclitaxel, is already utilized clinically for advanced or treatment-refractory melanoma, its multi-target molecular effects in relation to melanoma transcriptomic alterations remain insufficiently defined. Experimental validation in B16F0 melanoma cells demonstrated dose- and time-dependent cytotoxicity, with an IC₅₀ of approximately 17 µM at 48 h. RT-qPCR analysis showed increased expression of CDKN1A, BRCA1, and PTEN, alongside reduced AKT1 expression, indicating activation of DNA damage response pathways and reinforcement of tumor-suppressive signaling. Overall, this study identifies key molecular determinants of melanoma progression and provides mechanistic evidence explaining carboplatin's therapeutic activity through modulation of dysregulated transcriptomic hubs. The combined computational and experimental framework offers a valuable strategy for biomarker discovery and mechanistic evaluation of clinically used agents in melanoma research.

papers.title: Pharmacological melatonin induces mitochondrial dysfunction and alters extracellular nucleotide metabolism and CD39/CD73 expression in human melanoma cells.
papers.abstract: Cutaneous melanoma remains an aggressive malignant neoplasm characterized by molecular heterogeneity and therapeutic resistance, highlighting the need to identify alternative pathways involved in tumor progression. Purinergic signaling, particularly the conversion of extracellular ATP to immunosuppressive adenosine mediated by ectonucleotidases CD39 (NTPDase1) and CD73 (ecto-5'-nucleotidase), has emerged as a critical determinant of melanoma biology, but its potential regulation by melatonin remains unexplored.Here, we investigated whether pharmacological melatonin (0.1-5 mM, 24 and 48 h) influences metabolic activity, mitochondrial homeostasis, and extracellular nucleotide metabolism in two human melanoma cell lines with distinct molecular profiles (SK-MEL-28 and A375). Melatonin reduced metabolic activity and induced mitochondrial depolarization in both cell lines, although A375 cells exhibited greater mitochondrial sensitivity than SK-MEL-28 cells. These mitochondrial alterations were accompanied by distinct apoptosis- and inflammation-related transcriptional responses, indicating lineage-dependent cellular response to pharmacological melatonin. In parallel, melatonin differentially altered extracellular nucleotide metabolism and CD39/CD73 gene expression, with distinct responses observed between the two melanoma cell lines. Collectively, these findings indicate that the biological effects of pharmacological melatonin extend beyond mitochondrial dysfunction and involve remodeling of extracellular nucleotide metabolism, providing new evidence for an interaction between melatonergic and purinergic signaling in melanoma.

papers.title: Diagnostic Challenge in Cytology: Fibrosing Thyroiditis Mimicking Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma.
miRNAs bridging the gap between the tumor microenvironment and liquid biopsy in cutaneous melanoma.
papers.abstract: Cutaneous melanoma remains one of the most challenging neoplasms and the deadliest form of skin cancer. miRNAs are a class of non-coding RNA molecules found in both tissues and body fluids that can negatively regulate gene expression in eukaryotic cells, playing key roles in health and disease. Dysregulated miRNA levels have been linked to various aspects of melanocytic tumor biology, including the transition from benign to malignant stages, immunosuppression, dissemination, and therapy resistance. Here, we provide a timely review of the roles of miRNAs within the cutaneous melanoma tumor microenvironment, emphasizing their impact on immune cell phenotypes and functions, angiogenesis, innate and adaptive immunity, and immune checkpoint expression to help refine future biomarkers and therapeutic targets in the field. We will also address their roles in circular and long non-coding RNA sponging interactions and the potential for translating miRNAs into clinical practice, given their simultaneous presence in both cutaneous melanoma tissues and liquid biopsies. The main challenges and limitations associated with such a translational approach will also be addressed.

papers.title: Platform-based manufacturing of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes derived from different solid tumor types.
papers.abstract: In adoptive cell therapy with tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), TILs are isolated and expanded ex vivo from an autologous tumor lesion. TIL therapy, comprising preparative lymphodepleting chemotherapy, TIL infusion, and post-infusion supportive interleukin-2 (IL-2) administration, has demonstrated efficacy in patients with metastatic melanoma. Interest in extending TIL therapy to other solid tumors is growing, and a tumor-agnostic manufacturing platform would allow first-in-human trials to be launched rapidly in these indications. This study investigated whether a manufacturing process and control strategy developed for metastatic melanoma-derived TILs could be adapted into a tumor-agnostic platform for the generation of TILs from different solid tumor types, referred to as NTU101. The feasibility of generating TILs from endometrial carcinoma (ENDC, n=9), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC, n=9), and penile cancer (PENC, n=10) lesions was assessed during process development (PD) runs using predefined quality criteria. Throughout PD runs, flow cytometry was used to characterize cells. When available, autologous tumor digest was used to assess the tumor-reactive potential of TILs. Based on PD experience, adjusted quality criteria were applied to manufacture one full-scale GMP NTU101-drug product (DP) per tumor type. Overall, 89% (n=25/28) of PD NTU101-DPs manufactured met the predefined quality criteria, containing at least 0.5×10^9 and 90% viable CD45+CD3+ cells, less than 1.0% of cellular impurities (viable CD45- and CD19+ cells), and a potency of more than 1.0×10^3 pg/mL IFN-γ secretion upon CD3/CD28-polymer stimulation. Across the tumor types, PD NTU101-DPs had comparable T-cell subset and differentiation state compositions. In vitro tumor-reactive potential was detected in 82% of tested NTU101-DPs (ENDC: 71%, n=5/7; NSCLC: 80%, n= 4/5; and PENC: 100%, n=5/5), although the level of reactivity will need to be confirmed with a more in-depth assay. One GMP NTU101-DP was then manufactured from each tumor type, and all three met NTU101's quality criteria. The NTU101 platform produced comparable NTU101-DPs from three solid tumor types beyond melanoma, with in vitro tumor-reactive potential for some batches. This platform can be applied in TIL therapy clinical trials to generate ENDC-, NSCLC-, and PENC-derived TILs, and possibly other solid tumor types.

papers.title: Commentary: Selpercatinib versus multi-kinase inhibitors for advanced medullary thyroid cancer: a network meta-analysis of RET-targeted therapies.
Precision Thyroid Oncology Using Genetic-Based Therapies: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Most thyroid malignancies harbor a limited set of well-characterized mutations driving tumor initiation and determining phenotype. This relatively direct genotype-phenotype association, bringing insights into molecular mechanisms of progression and drug resistance, makes advanced thyroid cancers suitable for genetic-based therapies. Personalized cancer treatment by targeting actionable tumor mutations represents one of the most innovative frontiers in oncology. The present narrative review focuses on actionable mutations occurring in thyroid cancers and provides a state-of-the-art overview of genetic-based treatments that have received regulatory approval worldwide. These include two selective RET inhibitors (sRET-Is) (selpercatinib and pralsetinib), three NTRK inhibitors (NTRK-Is) (larotrectinib, entrectinib, and repotrectinib), and two dual BRAF/MEK inhibitor regimens (dabrafenib plus trametinib and encorafenib plus binimetinib). The most significant impact has been observed in the management of RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer. Selpercatinib, available in many countries, demonstrated superiority over standard multikinase inhibitors (MKIs) in a head-to-head comparison. It currently represents the best first-line treatment option. In BRAFV600E-positive anaplastic thyroid cancer, both dabrafenib plus trametinib and encorafenib plus binimetinib showed efficacy that appeared to exceed that historically observed with standard approaches. However, their approval is currently limited to a few countries. In radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), sRET-Is and NTRK-Is are effective in molecularly selected patients and are approved in many countries. However, their applicability is limited by the low prevalence of the corresponding actionable alterations. In BRAFV600E-positive radioiodine-refractory DTC, dabrafenib plus trametinib has emerged as a useful option after MKI failure, although a tumor-specific approval has been granted only in Europe. Precision oncology is increasingly being integrated into the management of advanced thyroid cancer. However, its impact varies widely across different tumor settings, and its real-world use is strongly influenced by country-specific drug regulations.

papers.title: Construction of an EMT-Related Prognostic Model for Melanoma and Functional Validation of the EMT-Associated Gene BGN.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is a highly aggressive skin tumour that poses considerable challenges in treatment and prognostic assessment. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a critical process in melanoma progression and contributes to tumour invasion and metastasis. This study aimed to identify EMT-related genes associated with melanoma prognosis and to develop a risk model for patient stratification. Based on previous studies, an EMT-related gene set comprising 200 genes was compiled. Gene expression data from normal skin and skin cutaneous melanoma tissues were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) databases. Differential expression analysis was performed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), using an adjusted p value < 0.05 as the significance threshold. Univariable Cox regression analysis was subsequently conducted to identify survival-related genes among the DEGs (p < 0.05), resulting in the selection of six genes: LAMC2, IL32, MGP, CAP2, ECM1 and BGN. A risk score model was then constructed based on these genes. The model showed prognostic stratification ability in both the TCGA cohort and the external validation cohort GSE65904. Patients were classified into high- and low-risk groups, and overall survival was significantly shorter in the high-risk group than in the low-risk group (p < 0.0001). Analysis of the immune microenvironment showed higher levels of immune cell infiltration in the low-risk group. BGN was significantly overexpressed in melanoma tissues and cell lines. In vitro experiments demonstrated that BGN silencing inhibited the proliferation, migration and invasion of A375 cells and reversed EMT-related changes, whereas BGN overexpression enhanced the malignant phenotype of A2058 cells. In vivo experiments further confirmed that BGN knockdown significantly suppressed xenograft tumour growth and altered the expression of EMT-related markers. These findings establish an EMT-related prognostic model for melanoma risk stratification and provide experimental evidence supporting the potential role of BGN in melanoma progression. This study integrates computational analysis with functional validation; however, further validation in independent prospective cohorts is required before clinical application.

papers.title: Use of plasma chromogranin a epitopes vasostatin and catestatin as biomarkers for catecholamine-producing tumours in dogs.
papers.abstract: Differentiation of catecholamine-producing tumours from other adrenal tumours remains difficult. Chromogranin A (CgA) is a marker for catecholamine secretion in the body. An assay for quantification of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin has been validated for use in dogs but not yet evaluated in dogs with catecholamine-producing tumours. The aims were to evaluate the assays foranalysis of plasma concentrations of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin in dogs with adrenal tumours and to compare concentrations between catecholamine-producing tumours and adrenocortical tumours in dogs that were subjected to adrenalectomy. Twelve dogs with histopathologically confirmed catecholamine-secreting tumours (eleven pheochromocytomas (PCCs), one extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma (PGL)) and twelve with adrenocortical tumours were included in the study. Plasma concentrations of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin were determined byradioimmunoassay (RIA), before adrenalectomy in 23 out of 24 dogs and after adrenalectomy in six of the dogs with catecholamine-secreting tumours (five PCC, one PGL). Tumour diagnosis was made by histopathology in all cases. Overall, median plasma concentration of the CgA epitopevasostatin in dogs with catecholamine-secreting tumours was 0.82 nmol/L (interquartile range (IQR) 0.52 to 1.60 nmol/L), which was significantly higher(Wilcoxon rank sum exact test, P= 0.0374) than the vasostatin concentration in adrenocortical tumours (median 0.50; IQR 0.34 to 0.59 nmol/L). A subsetof dogs (5/12) with catecholamine-secreting tumours had elevated plasma vasostatin concentrations preoperatively. After successful surgery, thepreoperatively elevated plasma vasostatin concentrations decreased numerically, however without reaching statistical significance. Catestatin concentrationdid not differ between tumour types. Elevated plasma concentration of the CgA epitope vasostatin showed potential as a biomarker for asubset of catecholamine-secreting tumours.

papers.title: Occult Hypervascularity of an Endobronchial Carcinoid Demonstrated by Bronchial Angiography.
Expression of Concern: Multifocality as a marker of aggressiveness in medullary thyroid carcinoma: a retrospective cohort analysis of lymph node metastasis and recurrence.
Associations Between Circulating Metabolites and Skin Cancer: A Bidirectional Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization Study.
papers.abstract: Skin cancer is the most common type of cancer worldwide, categorized into melanoma and non-melanoma types. While genetics play a crucial role in the development of skin cancer, recent developments in metabolomics have revealed that circulating metabolites influence genetic risk profiles. In this study, we utilized a bidirectional two-sample Mendelian Randomization (MR) approach, analyzing metabolite datasets from the Canadian Longitudinal Study of Aging (CLSA) and skin cancer datasets from the UK Biobank. Replication analyses were performed with the 10th round of the FinnGen project. Instrumental variables (IVs) were chosen according to established MR criteria and assessed through the Wald ratio, IVW, MR-Egger, and weighted median methods. Various sensitivity analyses were conducted utilizing Cochrane's Q, Egger's intercept, MR-PRESSO, and leave-one-out (LOO) techniques. After meticulous analysis, we identified causal relationships between circulating metabolites and skin cancer risks. Specifically, levels of 1,2-dilinoleoyl-GPE (18:2/18:2), 1-palmitoyl-2-linoleoyl-gpc (16:0/18:2), 1-stearoyl-2-arachidonoyl-gpc (18:0/20:4), 1-stearoyl-2-linoleoyl-gpc (18:0/18:2), and Docosapentaenoate n3 DPA, the ratio of Arachidonate (20:4n6) to oleate to vaccenate (18:1), and Oleoyl-linoleoyl-glycerol (18:1 to 18:2) to linoleoyl-arachidonoyl-glycerol (18:2 to 20:4) were linked to non-melanoma skin cancer, whereas levels of trans-urocanate were causally linked to melanoma of skin, and S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) showed a putative association. It should be noted that docosapentaenoate n3 DPA and SAH were each supported by a single SNP and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than definitive causal evidence. Reverse MR analysis highlighted robust causal relationships with 18 and 10 metabolites and non-melanoma skin cancer and melanoma of skin, respectively. These findings enhance our understanding of skin cancer etiology and risk factors, providing genetic evidence for hypothesis-generating associations that support the development of targeted therapies and aid in the identification of potential biomarkers.

papers.title: Pacak-Zhuang syndrome with EPAS1 p.Pro531Leu somatic variant: one case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: To report a case child of Pacak-Zhuang syndrome with EPAS1 p.Pro531Leu somatic variant in a child and to summarize the clinical characteristics, diagnosis, treatment methods, and prognosis of this syndrome based on a literature review. A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of a child girl with Pacak-Zhuang syndrome admitted to Hebei Children's Hospital in July 2019. Using the search terms 'Pacak-Zhuang syndrome', 'EPAS1', 'HIF-2α', 'HIF-2A', and 'Polycythemia-paraganglioma syndrome', relevant literature was retrieved from PubMed and Web of Science. The clinical manifestations, diagnostic methods, treatment plans, and outcomes of patients with this syndrome were analyzed. A 4-year-old girl had recurrent hypertension, polycythemia and renal hilar masses. Diagnosis was confirmed by imaging, biochemical detection and paraffin tissue genetic testing. She received three operations for paragangliomas; pathology showed CgA(+), Syn(+), NSE(+) and Ki‑67 ≤5%. Follow-up revealed tumor recurrence, but the condition improved with oral temozolomide. Combined with 10 retrieved articles, 18 patients (4 males,14 females, mean age 25 years) were analyzed. Polycythemia was the cardinal manifestation. All patients received surgery, and 10 suffered uncontrolled tumor recurrence. Pacak-Zhuang syndrome is a rare disorder involving the neuroendocrine and hematopoietic systems, often initially presenting with 'polycythemia'. Most cases are sporadic, with no apparent familial inheritance or history of other neuroendocrine tumors. When encountering pediatric patients with unexplained hypertension accompanied by polycythemia symptoms, the possibility of this syndrome should be considered, and further imaging studies and genetic testing are required for definitive diagnosis.

papers.title: Clinicopathological characteristics and outcomes of rectal neuroendocrine tumors according to resection modality.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to compare the effects of different treatment methods on the postoperative results and long-term prognosis of patients with 1-2 cm rectal neuroendocrine tumors (R-NETs), and provide evidence-based guidance for the treatment decision-making of this specific tumor size. The retrospective cohort study of this single-center included 736 patients with pathologically diagnosed R-NETs who were treated from January 2013 to August 2024. According to the treatment received, the patients were divided into endoscopic resection group (ER), local surgery group (LS) and radical surgery group (RS). The primary endpoint was recurrence free survival (RFS). A total of 736 R-NETs patients were enrolled. For the controversial 1-2 cm tumor, there was no significant difference in the long-term RFS between the LS group and the ER group (P = 0.280), and the postoperative hospitalization days of the LS group was relatively short (median 2 days vs. 3 days, P < 0.001). Sensitivity analysis using propensity score matching (PSM) further confirmed these outcomes in postoperative hospitalization days (P < 0.001). For 1-2 cm R-NETs, recurrence events were rare in both treatment groups, and local surgery was associated with a shorter postoperative hospital stay.

papers.title: Oncolytic Vaccinia Virus Armed With CLEC2A Enhances Antitumor Immunity via ROS-Autophagy Feedback Loop and Cytokine Activation.
papers.abstract: Tumors often exhibit immunosuppressive microenvironments (TMEs) and present as immunologically "cold." Oncolytic viruses (OVs), particularly engineered vaccinia viruses (oncoVVs), are an encouraging therapy that directly lyses cancer cells and reprograms the TME. In this study, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of an oncolytic vaccinia virus expressing human C-type lectin domain family 2 member A (oncoVV-CLEC2A) in melanoma and ovarian cancer cells. OncoVV-CLEC2A elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, suppressed Nrf2-mediated antioxidant responses, and triggered autophagy. These changes promoted cytokine production (IL-6, IFN-α/β/γ, TNF-α) via activation of AP-1 and IRF3/7. In a B16-F10 melanoma model, oncoVV-CLEC2A increased serum levels of IFN-γ, accompanied by augmented infiltration of CD8+ T cells and activation of NK cells. Taken together, oncoVV-CLEC2A reshapes the TME by intensifying oxidative stress and autophagic activity, effectively turning "cold" tumors "hot." Notably, the mutual reinforcement between ROS production and autophagy activation not only enhances viral replication but also triggers cytokine-mediated immunity.

papers.title: 177Lu- DOTA-TATE treatment for advanced gastrointestinal neuroendocrine tumor with refractory carcinoid syndrome.
Streptozotocin-based chemotherapy in advanced PanNETs: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Streptozotocin (STZ)-based chemotherapy remains a treatment option for advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (PanNETs), particularly when tumour shrinkage is a therapeutic priority. However, its activity has been reported across heterogeneous treatment schedules, patient populations, and response-assessment eras. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate objective response rate (ORR) and landmark progression-free survival (PFS). We systematically reviewed randomised trials, prospective studies, and retrospective cohorts reporting ORR and/or PFS with STZ-containing regimens. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted in a primary ELIGIBLE dataset restricted to advanced or metastatic pancreatic-only cohorts with standardised outcome assessment, and in a broader ALL dataset for contextual analyses. Comparisons across regimen families were exploratory. Twenty-seven studies including 1,744 patients were included. In the ELIGIBLE dataset, pooled ORR was 36.1% (95% CI 30.6-42.0), with a 95% prediction interval of 23.0-51.0%. Landmark PFS was 59.2% (50.6-67.2) at 12 months and 41.5% (33.4-50.1) at 24 months. Estimates from the ALL dataset were directionally consistent but more heterogeneous. No statistically significant differences were detected between regimen families. Certainty of evidence was very low, mainly because of risk of bias and inconsistency. In cohorts using standardised outcome assessment, STZ-containing regimens were associated with objective responses in approximately one-third of patients, supporting their consideration when tumour shrinkage is a major therapeutic objective. These single-arm pooled estimates do not establish superiority among STZ schedules or relative to other treatments, and the PFS benchmarks require cautious interpretation because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity.

papers.title: Eicosa-11Z,14Z,17Z-Trienoic Acid Suppresses Melanogenesis by Inhibiting Intracellular MITF/Tyrosinase Axis.
papers.abstract: Eicosa-11Z,14Z,17Z-trienoic acid (ETA; 20:3 n-3) is an ω-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid whose role in melanogenesis remains unclear. This study investigated the effects of ETA on melanogenesis using α-MSH-stimulated B16F10 melanoma cells and explored the underlying mechanisms. Structural similarity analysis indicated that ETA is closely related to α-linolenic acid, a lipid known to influence pigmentation. ETA showed minimal direct inhibition of mushroom tyrosinase activity in a cell-free system. In cell-based assays, ETA did not induce significant cytotoxicity within the tested concentration range. Under melanogenic conditions, ETA reduced α-MSH-induced melanin accumulation and intracellular tyrosinase activity. This reduction was accompanied by decreased mRNA expression of Tyr, Tyrp1, and Tyrp2, together with reduced protein expression of MITF, tyrosinase, TYRP1, and TYRP2. ETA also attenuated α-MSH-induced phosphorylation of CREB, ERK, and MITF. Immunofluorescence analysis further showed that ETA reduced α-MSH-induced MITF fluorescence intensity, including signals observed in the nuclear region. Taken together, these findings suggest that ETA modulates melanogenesis-related processes in B16F10 cells, likely through mechanisms involving changes in MITF localization and downstream gene expression rather than direct inhibition of tyrosinase activity. These results suggest that ETA may represent a potential candidate for further investigation in the context of pigmentation regulation.

papers.title: Imaging Manifestations and Clinical Analysis of 12 Cases of Anorectal Malignant Melanoma.
papers.abstract: To investigate the computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features and clinical characteristics of primary anorectal malignant melanoma (ARMM). This retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical, imaging and pathological data of 12 patients with pathologically confirmed ARMM admitted to The First Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine between March 2021 and December 2024, and the relevant literature was reviewed and summarized. All patients underwent CT and MRI examinations. Among the 12 patients, 5 were male and 7 were female; their ages ranged from 37 to 78 years, with a median age of 65 years. The clinical manifestations were diverse, with bloody stool being the most common (58.3%), followed by anal pain (16.7%) and polypoid vegetation prolapsing from the anus (16.7%). Typical anal pigmentation with pruritus was rare (8.3%). Gross pathological examination revealed a polypoid tumor in 7 cases and an ulcerative or infiltrative growth pattern in 5 cases. Immunohistochemical staining results showed that 12 cases were positive for human melanoma black-45 (HMB-45) and Melan-A, and 9 cases were positive for S-100. On imaging, plain CT scan showed that the tumors were predominantly isodense or slightly hyperdense, with a maximum diameter of approximately 2-5 cm. The enhancement patterns varied, but the tumors predominantly demonstrated marked heterogeneous enhancement. On MRI, most lesions were isointense on T1WI (10/12); 11/12 lesions were slightly hyperintense on T2WI, and hyperintense on diffusion-weighted images (DWI). After enhancement, most tumors exhibited marked heterogeneous enhancement. Most of the ARMM lesions in this group demonstrated atypical MRI signal characteristics, making diagnosis challenging. When an anorectal tumor exhibits iso- or hypointensity on T1WI and hyperintensity on T2WI, ARMM should be considered in the differential diagnosis. The CT manifestations lack specificity, and clinical symptoms may mimic those of benign lesions. ARMM may show involvement of the perirectal fat plane on imaging and regional lymph node metastasis and generally shows limited sensitivity to radiotherapy and chemotherapy, contributing to low therapeutic efficacy and poor prognosis. The definitive diagnosis of ARMM depends on histopathological examination, with immunohistochemical staining for S-100, HMB-45 and Melan-A can provide supportive information for the diagnosis of ARMM.

papers.title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Combined With Biopsy for the Preoperative Diagnosis of a Rare Pelvic Schwannoma: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Primary pelvic schwannomas are rare and often misdiagnosed due to non-specific imaging features. Accurate preoperative evaluation remains a challenge. The clinical utility of contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) combined with time-intensity curve (TIC) analysis and targeted biopsy was evaluated for the preoperative diagnosis and management of a pelvic schwannoma. CASE REPORT A 66-year-old man presented with dysuria and lumbago. Imaging revealed a large, mixed cystic-solid pelvic mass. Conventional ultrasound demonstrated a predominantly cystic-solid lesion with limited Doppler flow, whereas CEUS showed progressive dendritic enhancement of the viable solid component from the periphery toward the center, with non-enhancement of cystic or necrotic areas. TIC analysis demonstrated a distinctive "equal-in and slow-out" perfusion pattern, supported by quantitative parameters (rise time, time to peak, fall time, and washout area under the curve). Based on these perfusion characteristics, ultrasound-guided biopsy was directed toward hyperenhanced viable regions while avoiding necrotic zones, thereby improving tissue sampling accuracy. Immunohistochemistry confirmed S-100 and SOX-10 positivity, establishing a definitive diagnosis. Complete surgical resection with bladder defect repair was performed. Postoperatively, urinary function recovered, and no recurrent urinary or pelvic symptoms were reported during outpatient follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Quantitative CEUS-TIC analysis combined with targeted biopsy provides an effective preoperative diagnostic strategy for pelvic schwannomas. The observed CEUS-TIC perfusion pattern may correspond to the heterogeneous microvascular distribution of Antoni A and Antoni B regions; however, this hypothesis requires validation in future imaging-pathology correlation studies.
papers.journal: The American journal of case reports

papers.title: Endothelial exosomes remodel chromatin accessibility and superenhancer in cancer cells to promote liver metastatic colonization.
papers.abstract: Liver-organotropic metastasis occurs in cancers such as uveal melanoma (UM) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and is a leading cause of mortality at the terminal stage. Colonization is a rate-limiting and converging step in the metastatic cascade. The drivers underlying liver colonization have largely remained elusive. In this report, we hypothesized that pioneer transcription factors (TFs) increase chromatin accessibility and superenhancer (SE) remodeling, which subsequently promote colonization-associated cellular features [e.g., proliferation, survival, cancer stem cells (CSCs), motility] by driving the transcription of the respective SE-associated genes. We tested this hypothesis and discovered that the pioneer TF KLF4 promoted chromatin accessibility and SE remodeling by ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq. Chromatin accessibility and SE remodeling significantly increased the transcription of the SE-associated genes MCL1 and RASGRP3, which consequently promoted proliferation, motility, and metastasis. Furthermore, the upregulation of KLF4 expression in UM cells was promoted by RN7SL2-containing exosomes from surrounding endothelial cells. Analysis of clinical datasets revealed that the overexpression of RIG-I, STAT1, KLF4, and RASGRP3 was individually correlated with shorter metastasis-free survival or overall survival in patients with UM and PDAC. In conclusion, the identification of the exoRN7SL2-STAT1-KLF4-SEs-RASGRP3 signaling axis may help elucidate metastatic colonization through interactions between tumor cells and the endothelial niche and may yield novel and viable therapeutic targets.

papers.title: A modular synthetic promoter toolkit for programmable gene control in activated and chronically stimulated T cells.
papers.abstract: Synthetic circuits that couple transgene expression to endogenous transcription factor (TF) activity enable cellular response to changing functional states. In T cells, antigen stimulation results in dynamic changes of transcription factor expression programs. Harnessing these endogenous TF dynamics for programmable gene control remains an important challenge in engineered T cells. Here, we develop a library of synthetic promoters (SPs) responsive to seven TFs identified through transcriptomic analysis of T-cell activation programs. These promoters couple endogenous TF activity to transcriptional output across a broad dynamic range of inducibility and basal expression. We quantitatively profile promoter performance in HEK293 and Jurkat cells, evaluate them for orthogonality, and integrate them into Boolean logic gate architectures and network topologies to minimize basal transcriptional leakiness and improve ON/OFF ratios. We test selected synthetic promoters in primary human CD8⁺ T cells, under endogenous TF regulation, and we further characterize the NR4A2-responsive promoter subset in vitro and in tumor-infiltrating engineered T cells in a melanoma xenograft model, demonstrating dynamic and reversible activation.Together, these results provide a modular SP toolkit of TF-responsive synthetic promoters for programmable transcriptional control in engineered T cells.

papers.title: Emergency Surgery for Brain Tumors: Institutional Experience and Strategic Decision-making in the Era of Structured Work-hour Management.
papers.abstract: Emergency surgery for brain tumors is regarded as a life-saving intervention, but in contemporary neuro-oncological practice it may also serve diagnostic, stabilizing, and treatment-enabling roles. We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients who underwent emergency surgery for brain tumors at a single institution between January 2020 and December 2025. Among 352 brain tumor operations, 59 cases (16.8%) met the study definition of emergency surgery. The frequency of emergency surgery varied by tumor type, being highest in primary central nervous system lymphoma (11/18, 61.1%), followed by brain metastases (25/74, 33.8%), hemangioblastoma (2/7, 28.6%), glioma (15/83, 18.1%), pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (1/15, 6.7%), and meningioma (5/106, 4.7%). Emergency cases were stratified into four operational categories: life-saving surgery, malignant oncological emergency surgery, intentional delayed surgery after stabilization, and semi-urgent surgery. Tumor resection was performed in 42 patients (71.2%) and biopsy was performed in 17 (28.8%); all primary central nervous system lymphoma cases underwent diagnostic biopsy with intraoperative rapid pathology. Regarding operative timing, 34 procedures (57.6%) were completed within the 08:00-17:00 time frame, 17 (28.8%) started within the 08:00-17:00 time frame but extended beyond 17:00, and eight (13.6%) started at or after 17:00. Median preoperative and discharge modified Rankin Scale scores were both 3, with improvement in 21 patients, no change in 29, worsening in 7, and in-hospital death in two. Time to treatment initiation was evaluable in 41 malignant tumor cases requiring subsequent tumor-specific therapy, and differed according to tumor type. Capacity-aware triage may help balance neurological urgency, tumor-specific therapeutic goals, preoperative stabilization, patient safety, and surgical quality under structured work-hour management.

papers.title: Growth hormone-releasing hormone-secreting giant pheochromocytoma causing acromegaly: a case report with a review of the literature.
papers.abstract: The ectopic secretion of growth hormone (GH) or growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) is responsible for fewer than 1% of acromegaly cases. Furthermore, within this small population, GHRH-secreting pheochromocytomas/paragangliomas (PPGLs) are even rarer. A 57-year-old Japanese woman presented to our hospital for treatment of a large left-sided pheochromocytoma (PCC). A physical examination revealed enlargement of the nose and lips as well as macroglossia, thereby raising the suspicion of acromegaly, which was biochemically confirmed by a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a slightly enlarged pituitary gland but no definitive tumor. A left adrenalectomy was performed after careful dose titration of doxazosin and metyrosine. Postoperative biochemical improvement of GH excess and immunohistochemical analysis of the resected tumor confirmed the diagnosis of GHRH-secreting PCC. Given the possibility that PPGLs produce various ectopic hormones and peptides, thorough physical examinations remain fundamental for the accurate diagnosis and optimal management of patients with these tumors.

papers.title: Genetic intratumour heterogeneity in digestive high-grade neuroendocrine neoplasms.
papers.abstract: Digestive high-grade neuroendocrine neoplasms (HG-NEN) are rare and heterogeneous tumours with an aggressive biology and limited treatment efficacy. Genetic intratumour heterogeneity (ITH) is a mechanism of progression and treatment resistance in other cancers, yet unexplored in digestive HG-NEN. Next-generation sequencing with a 360-cancer gene panel was performed on 51 digestive HG-NEN, suitable for multiregional sampling. The mutational status of each sample within a patient was assessed to calculate an ITH-index, defined as the average number of discordant mutations across all pair-wise comparisons between samples. An ITH-index based on primary tumour samples was calculated for chemotherapy-naïve cases: 28 neuroendocrine carcinomas (NEC), 9 mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNEN) and 3 neuroendocrine tumour grade 3 (NET G3). Median ITH-index in NEC/MiNEN was 5, with a wide range (0-98.8). Greater heterogeneity was associated with right-sided colonic primaries (p = .005) and higher tumour mutational burden (r = 0.74, p < .001). Median overall survival was 7 months longer in NEC/MiNEN with median ITH-index above compared to below median (22.5 vs. 15.5 months, p = .077), driven mostly by patients with locoregional disease. Response to first-line chemotherapy was not influenced by median ITH-index. No heterogeneity was found among driver mutations in BRAF and KRAS. NET G3 displayed low heterogeneity (ITH-index 2-3). Higher ITH-index was not associated with shorter survival or treatment response, suggesting that genetic ITH is not the primary resistance mechanism in digestive NEC/MiNEN. Moving towards targeted treatment strategies, our data indicate that a single biopsy may underestimate ITH. BRAF and KRAS may be favourable targets as they displayed no heterogeneity.

papers.title: Mucosal Small Cell Neuroendocrine Carcinoma of the Gallbladder With Extraregional Lymph Node Metastasis: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Gallbladder small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (SCNEC) is a rare and highly aggressive malignancy, and an optimal treatment strategy has not been established. We report a case of mucosal gallbladder SCNEC with extraregional lymph node metastasis that responded well to chemotherapy. A 69-year-old woman presented with severe epigastric pain and inflammatory findings. Ultrasonography, endoscopic ultrasonography, and computed tomography revealed a 40 mm gallbladder mass and enlarged lymph nodes in the hepatoduodenal ligament. Because inflammation and pain could not be controlled by conservative treatment and endoscopic gallbladder drainage was unsuccessful, emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy was performed. Histopathological examination revealed SCNEC with a Ki-67 index of 80%. Although continuous tumor invasion was limited to the mucosal layer and the tumor was classified as T1a, lymphatic invasion was present. Postoperative positron emission tomography and octreotide scintigraphy revealed metastases in the hepatoduodenal ligament and extraregional perisplenic artery lymph nodes. Further surgical resection was not performed, and chemotherapy with cisplatin and irinotecan was initiated. After six cycles, the hepatoduodenal ligament lymph node decreased from 31 mm to 13 mm, and the perisplenic artery lymph node disappeared, resulting in a partial response. No disease progression was observed during the 12-month postoperative follow-up period. This case suggests that gallbladder SCNEC may have metastatic potential even when the primary tumor is limited to the mucosal layer. Careful systemic staging is important, and platinum-based chemotherapy may be effective for metastatic disease.

papers.title: Peritoneal neuroendocrine carcinoma of unknown primary with markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein: a case report
Biogenic amines as neuroendocrine tumor markers: limitations and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Biogenic amines and their metabolites are central biochemical markers in the diagnosis and management of catecholamine-producing neuroendocrine tumors, including pheochromocytoma, paraganglioma, and neuroblastoma. Despite decades of clinical use, their wider implementation remains limited by substantial physiological variability, pre-analytical influences, and methodological heterogeneity across laboratories. The transition from colorimetric and immunoassay-based techniques to liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry has markedly improved analytical sensitivity and specificity. The multiplexing capacity of modern mass spectrometric platforms has enabled comprehensive quantification of biogenic amine profiles, thereby increasing diagnostic sensitivity in tumor subtypes in which individual biomarkers exhibit limited performance. Increasing attention has been given to dopamine derived metabolites, especially 3-methoxytyramine, which is associated with MYCN-related tumor biology and unfavorable clinical outcomes in neuroblastoma and selected paraganglioma subtypes. However, the analytical complexity of mass spectrometric approaches, together with the absence of full metrological traceability, continues to limit inter-laboratory comparability. In this review, we critically evaluate the analytical evolution of biogenic amine testing, the principal pre-analytical and methodological determinants that influence the interpretation of results, and current efforts to improve harmonization. Particular emphasis is placed on the potential of biogenic amines as prognostic biomarkers and on the need to integrate expanded biogenic amine profiling into clinically robust, comparable diagnostic approaches that may advance precision oncology.

papers.title: Widespread Cutaneous Metastases as the Primary Presentation of an Occult Neuroendocrine Tumour of Unknown Primary
Changes in tumor volume predict overall survival after [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in neuroendocrine neoplasm
papers.abstract: Purpose Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) is a crucial therapy for neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs). Pre-treatment somatostatin receptor (SSTR) PET determines eligibility for PRRT and can prognosticate overall survival (OS). The prognostic value of an end-of-treatment (EOT) SSTR-PET is underexplored. Methods 132 NEN patients who were treated with PRRT and underwent baseline and EOT SSTR-PET/CTs were retrospectively identified. Tumor lesions were semi-automatically annotated and total tumor volume (TTV), SUV max and SUV mean were derived from both PET scans and relative change in PET parameters were calculated. Associations between PET parameters and OS were assessed with Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses. Results Higher baseline TTV and increased TTV at EOT were significantly associated with shorter OS, while baseline and EOT SUV metrics were not independently associated with OS. Conclusion Increased TTV at baseline and EOT SSTR-PET/CT portends shorter OS in NEN and may guide clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Pancreatic hamartoma presenting with sleep-related behavioral abnormalities due to neuroglycopenia: a case report
Intracranial metastasis following intrahepatic remission in primary hepatic small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma: a case report
Multifocal Well-Differentiated Small Intestinal Neuroendocrine Tumor Presenting as Partial Small Bowel Obstruction in an Elderly Female: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Background Small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors (SI-NETs) are rare, slow-growing malignancies that frequently present with nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms, leading to diagnostic delays averaging five to seven years. Despite the existence of blood-based biomarkers including serum chromogranin A and urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA), most patients continue to present with advanced locoregional or metastatic disease. This case illustrates the diagnostic and surgical challenges of SI-NET in an elderly patient and highlights the clinical consequences of delayed biomarker utilization. Case presentation: A 77-year-old White female was referred to a surgical clinic after her primary care physician identified a small bowel mass on imaging ordered for chronic abdominal discomfort and a 20-pound unintentional weight loss. CT imaging demonstrated a solid mesenteric mass with adjacent adenopathy and small bowel tethering, producing the characteristic spoke-wheel sign of mesenteric desmoplasia. Serum chromogranin A and urinary 5-HIAA were not obtained prior to surgical referral. She underwent exploratory laparotomy with open small bowel resection and side-to-side anastomosis. Surgical pathology confirmed multifocal, well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (Grade 1, Ki-67 ~ 1%), staged pT4N1, with lymphovascular and perineural invasion and a positive mesenteric margin. Postoperative Dotatate PET identified a single PET-avid mesenteric lesion, prompting referral to a tertiary hepatobiliary center. A second exploratory laparotomy resected a 1.5 cm mesenteric nodule requiring direct repair of a superior mesenteric artery branch. Final pathology demonstrated fibrosis and chronic inflammation with no residual neuroendocrine tumor. The patient elected active surveillance with annual follow-up. Conclusions This case demonstrates the striking discordance between low tumor grade and advanced locoregional disease extent in SI-NETs and underscores the missed opportunity for earlier detection through routine biomarker screening in symptomatic patients. The PET-positive mesenteric nodule that yielded only fibrosis on re-resection raises important questions about functional imaging specificity in the desmoplastic postoperative mesentery. Clinicians should maintain a low threshold for obtaining serum chromogranin A and urinary 5-HIAA in patients presenting with unexplained weight loss and chronic gastrointestinal symptoms.

papers.title: Methylation profiling reveals epigenetic programs associated with chr18 loss in small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors
Follicular Dendritic Cell Sarcoma Arising in the Aortopulmonary Window: A Case Report of Complete Resection Using Proximal Pulmonary Artery Control
papers.abstract:
Background: Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma is a rare malignant neoplasm, and its occurrence in the aortopulmonary window is exceptionally uncommon. Tumors in this location are technically challenging because of the limited operative space and their close relationship to the aortic arch, left pulmonary artery, left main bronchus, and left recurrent laryngeal nerve. We report a case of follicular dendritic cell sarcoma arising in the aortopulmonary window that was completely resected using a strategy for proximal pulmonary artery control. Case presentation: A 46-year-old man was referred to our institution after an abnormal mediastinal shadow was incidentally detected on chest radiography. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed a 48 × 29 mm well-circumscribed mass in the aortopulmonary window, broadly contacting the aorta, left pulmonary artery, and left main bronchus. Positron emission tomography showed moderate fluorodeoxyglucose uptake without distant metastasis. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration suggested a neuroendocrine tumor but did not establish a definitive diagnosis. Surgical resection was performed through median sternotomy combined with a left anterior second intercostal thoracotomy. Because direct exposure and encirclement of the tumor-adjacent left pulmonary artery were considered hazardous, proximal vascular control was established through the transverse pericardial sinus before tumor manipulation. Division of the ligamentum arteriosum increased pulmonary artery mobility and improved exposure of the operative field. The tumor was completely separated from the left pulmonary artery, aorta, left main bronchus, and recurrent laryngeal nerve without combined organ resection. Histopathological examination showed spindle-shaped tumor cells arranged in whorled and rosette-like patterns. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD21, CD23, D2-40, and somatostatin receptor 2, confirming follicular dendritic cell sarcoma. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remained free of recurrence 3 years after surgery.

Conclusions:

Complete resection of a tumor arising in the aortopulmonary window can be facilitated by secure proximal pulmonary artery control and mobilization of surrounding structures. These technical principles may also be useful for other tumors in this anatomically complex region when direct manipulation of the tumor-adjacent pulmonary artery is considered hazardous.

papers.title: Cyclotron production of [68Ga]GaCl3 using solid target and its clinical adaptation through automated purification and GMP-grade production of [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE
papers.abstract: Background The clinical demand for [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTATATE has expanded substantially over the past decade. This is particularly due to its ability to selectively localize the somatostatin receptor expressing lesions in patients with neuroendocrine tumor. The interest in radiometal-based PET imaging is further privileged due to selective targeting of biological markers overexpressed on the tumor cells, and its ability to integrate molecular imaging and targeted radionuclide therapy within a unified theranostic framework. This growing demand has particularly highlighted the supply shortage and production challenges of metal-based PET radiopharmaceuticals, notably the [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTATATE. The generator-based supply of Ga-68 encounters low activity output issues, transportation or logistical challenges, increasing purchase cost and long procurement times. On other hand the cyclotron-based production is an attractive alternate but currently is restricted to a limited number of specialized facilities. Methods Our work demonstrates a practical and transferable approach to cyclotron-based production of Ga-68 through 68 Zn(p,n) 68 Ga nuclear reaction using the solid target. The work illustrates a complete solid-target-based production workflow including preparation of the target plate(s), cyclotron irradiation, target material dissolution, radionuclide purification, and automation of [ 68 Ga]GaCl 3 and [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTATATE productions using the NEPTIS radiosynthesis module. Results Following the described procedures, we were able to produce 90–110 GBq of [ 68 Ga]GaCl 3 at EOB using an incident proton energy of 12.5 MeV, 40 µA beam current and irradiation time of 2 hrs. The [ 68 Ga]GaCl 3 was obtained in RCY of 51 ± 6 (n.d.c) with > 99% radionuclide purity and molar activity of 137 GBq/µmol. The produced [ 68 Ga]GaCl 3 was subsequently used in radiosynthesis of [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTATATE under GMP conditions in RCY of 54 ± 3 with > 98% purity in all aspects for up to 5 hrs at RT. Conclusion Rather than proposing an entirely new target design or staying dependent on external supply, the work demonstrates a scalable and self-reliant workflow to Ga-68 production and its subsequent use in radiosynthesis of [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-DOTATATE. The work also emphasizes the establishment of regional Ga-68 production platform with possible implementation to production of other emerging radio-metals and thus maximizes the use of cyclotron and existing radio pharmacy infrastructure.

papers.title: Hyperactivation of β-catenin rewires mitochondrial fuel selection in liver cancer cells
papers.abstract:
ABSTRACT

Metabolic state is tightly linked to cell fate, and expression of the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC), which imports pyruvate into mitochondria, is a robust marker of it. The transcriptional regulators that set metabolic state, however, remain poorly defined. In the liver, β-catenin is one of the determinants of metabolic zonation, and activating CTNNB1 mutations are frequent in hepatocellular carcinoma. Here we show that β-catenin regulates metabolic state in liver cancer cells. An unbiased CRISPR screen that uses endogenous MPC1 transcript abundance as the marker identifies CTNNB1 . Activating β-catenin pharmacologically or genetically reduces MPC1 and MPC2 transcript and protein levels, and MPC expression is also low in β-catenin-driven liver tumors in vivo. Beyond the MPC, β-catenin activation impairs assembly of respiratory Complexes III and IV, reduces mitochondrial DNA content and respiratory capacity, elongates mitochondrial networks and remodels the lipidome. Stable isotope tracing shows reduced entry of glucose- and lactate-derived carbon into the TCA cycle alongside increased oxidation of palmitate and oleate. These findings identify β-catenin as a regulator of metabolic state that drives a fuel switch from carbohydrate to fatty acid oxidation in liver cancer cells.

papers.title: Patient characteristics and the safety of stent placement for malignant vena cava syndrome in Japan: a nationwide analysis.
papers.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the overall safety of stent placement for malignant superior or inferior vena cava (SVC/IVC) syndrome by assessing adverse events in a nationwide multicenter population.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination nationwide inpatient database. Patients who underwent stent placement for malignant superior or inferior vena cava (SVC/IVC) syndrome between April 2019 and March 2023 were included. The primary endpoint was the overall incidence of adverse events, which were identified using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision codes. Secondary evaluations included patient characteristics, underlying malignancies, therapeutic interventions, 7-day mortality after stent placement, 30-day in-hospital mortality after admission, and comparisons between the SVC and IVC groups.

Results

This nationwide study included 301 patients from 137 hospitals, of whom 187 underwent SVC stenting, and 114 underwent IVC stenting. Overall, 34 adverse events occurred in 32 patients (10.6%). Red blood cell transfusion was required in 10 patients (3.3%), but no invasive treatment, including embolization, was required. Seven-day mortality after stenting was 5.0%, and 30-day in-hospital mortality after admission was 11.6%. In comparisons between the SVC and IVC groups, respiratory failure was more common after SVC stenting, whereas other adverse events and mortality were comparable between groups. Lung tumors predominated in SVC cases and liver tumors in IVC cases; multiple stents were used more frequently in IVC cases.

Conclusion

Stent placement for malignant vena cava obstruction demonstrated an overall complication rate of 10.6% with no serious adverse events requiring invasive intervention.

papers.title: Long-Term Outcomes and Biomarker Correlates of a Multi-Institutional Phase II Study of Hypofractionated Proton Beam Therapy for Unresectable Primary Liver Tumors.
papers.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate long-term outcomes and determine whether longitudinal plasma profiling provides biological insight into disease progression after proton hypofractionated ablative radiation therapy (HART) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC).

Patients and methods

In this single-arm, multi-institutional phase II trial, 92 patients with localized unresectable HCC or ICC with Child-Pugh class A/B liver function received HART (up to 67.5 GyE in 15 fractions). Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Plasma samples were collected at baseline, days 1, 8, 15, and 1-month after treatment for exploratory correlative analyses.

Results

Among evaluable patients (44 HCC, 39 ICC), median OS was 29.2 months (HCC) and 20.8 months (ICC), with 5-year OS rates of 25.9% and 12.3%, respectively. Median PFS was 13.8 months (HCC) and 8.4 months (ICC). In-field local failure occurred in 2 HCC (4.5%) and 7 ICC (17.9%) patients, whereas out-of-field intrahepatic/distant progression remained the predominant pattern of failure. No grade >3 treatment-related toxicities were observed. Exploratory plasma profiling identified distinct biological signatures associated with progression: HCC was characterized by markers of hypoxia, inflammation, vascular remodeling, stromal activation, and hepatic regeneration, whereas associations in ICC predominantly involved signatures of hypoxia and vascular remodeling.

Conclusions

HART provides durable long-term in-field local control with minimal toxicity, but disease progression remains predominantly out-of-field intrahepatic/distant. Exploratory correlative analyses suggest that biological signatures reflecting vascular remodeling, hypoxia, inflammation, stromal activation, and hepatic reserve are associated with progression despite successful local therapy, informing future translational studies and combination strategies.
