Germline Whole-Gene Deletion of SDHA in a Carotid Body Paraganglioma Identified by Whole-Genome Sequencing and Confirmed by MLPA: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
papers.abstract: Background : Carotid body paragangliomas are frequently associated with germline variants in succinate dehydrogenase ( SDH ) genes. Among these, SDHA variants are particularly challenging to diagnose due to low penetrance and the presence of highly homologous pseudogenes. Standard diagnostic workflows, including whole-exome sequencing and targeted panels, often fail to detect large structural variants, such as whole-gene deletions, leading to potential underdiagnosis. This case is the first to report a germline whole-gene deletion of SDHA identified via whole-genome sequencing (WGS), providing definitive physical evidence of the Knudson two-hit hypothesis through the somatic loss of the remaining allele in the tumor tissue. Case presentation : A 63-year-old female presented with a 2-cm, left carotid body tumor. There was no relevant family history. The tumor was successfully resected, and histopathology confirmed a paraganglioma. While immunohistochemistry showed a loss of both SDHA and SDHB expression, WGS of peripheral blood revealed what is, to our knowledge, the first reported germline whole-gene deletion of the SDHA gene (copy number ≈ 1.1) in the region chr5:210,651–314,171. Notably, this type of large structural variant is potentially elusive to standard genetic analysis workflows. Subsequent WGS of the tumor tissue confirmed biallelic inactivation through the loss of the remaining allele (copy number ≈ 0.86), representing a classic two-hit mechanism. This large-scale deletion of all SDHA exons was further validated using multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA), confirming it as the pathogenic driver. The patient remains under rigorous long-term follow-up given the reported 15% risk of malignancy associated with SDHA variants. Conclusions : This case highlights the clinical utility of WGS in overcoming the inherent limitations of exome-based sequencing for SDHA analysis. When clinical suspicion remains high - specifically in cases with SDHA-negative immunohistochemistry but negative standard genetic testing - WGS or MLPA should be employed to detect hidden structural variants. Accurate molecular diagnosis is essential not only for understanding the mechanism of tumorigenesis but also for tailoring oncological surveillance and genetic counseling for the patient and their family.

papers.title: Delayed diagnosis of MEN1 after kidney transplantation: unrecognized pre-transplant features and implications for clinical practice.
papers.abstract: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1), characterized by multiglandular endocrine tumors such as hyperparathyroidism (HPT), is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations of the MEN1 gene. In patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), abnormalities in calcium-phosphate metabolism may obscure this diagnosis, making the recognition of MEN1 challenging. A 68-year-old man with end-stage renal disease underwent an ABO-compatible living-donor kidney transplantation (KT); however, persistent hypercalcemia prompted further evaluation, which revealed recurrent HPT with bilateral parathyroid enlargement. Pre-transplant imaging revealed an adrenal adenoma and a pancreatic tail lesion. Subsequent pituitary magnetic resonance imaging and genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis of MEN1. A retrospective review of the patient's medical history revealed several pre-transplant findings suggestive of MEN1 that had not been recognized. This case highlights that MEN1 may remain unrecognized in KT candidates owing to the occurrence of metabolic abnormalities also associated with CKD. The early recognition of MEN1 in KT candidates with recurrent or multiglandular hyperparathyroidism may improve pre-transplant risk assessment and enable appropriate long-term oncological surveillance.

papers.title: Primary Extramedullary Plasmacytoma of the Ileum: A Rare Diagnostic Challenge with Clinicopathological Correlation and Review of the Literature
papers.abstract: Background Primary extramedullary plasmacytoma is a rare plasma cell neoplasm arising outside the bone marrow cavity. Primary involvement of the gastrointestinal tract is rare specially isolated small bowel in a middle age patient. Diagnosis is challenging as presentation of disease is variable with non-specific symptoms such as abdominal pain, or gastrointestinal bleeding, and imaging cannot differentiate between these tumor from other non-hematological neoplasms. Diagnosis requires histopathological examination of the tumor with immunohistochemistry, and other workup to rule out systemic disease and bone marrow involvement. Treatment depends on the primary site of disease involvement and the presence of other features of systemic disease. Case presentation We present a rare case of a primary extramedullary plasmacytoma of small intestine in a 40-year-old patient presenting with abdominal pain, and melena and was found to have a 3.5x3 cm ileal ulceroinfiltrative avidly enhancing mass with mesenteric lymphadenopathy, raising a suspicion of ileal neuroendocrine tumor. He underwent segmental ileal resection and was diagnosed as plasmacytoma after histopathological examination along with assimilation of immunohistochemistry. Conclusion Primary extramedullary plasmacytoma of the ileum is a rare entity and should be included in the differential diagnosis of an ileal mass. A definitive diagnosis requires thorough histopathological assessment with immunohistochemistry and a complete systemic work-up to rule out underlying plasma cell myeloma.

papers.title: Butyrate enhances the obesity reduction effect of Semaglutide.
papers.abstract:
Background

Obesity represents a global public health burden with continuously increasing prevalence over recent decades. Combination regimens pairing semaglutide (Sema) with additional therapeutic agents have emerged as a major focus for anti-obesity research.

Methods

In diet-induced obese (DIO) mice, we evaluated whether oxytocin (Oxt, 3 and 5 mg·kg-1), long-acting oxytocin (la‑Oxt), caffeine, or butyrate could potentiate the anti-obesity efficacy of Sema. We further compared hypothalamic neuronal activity and plasma metabolomic profiles following Sema treatment against dietary restriction (DR), an established intervention for weight loss and metabolic improvement.

Results

Whereas Oxt, la‑Oxt, and caffeine did not augment Sema-mediated body weight reduction, butyrate produced significant potentiation of Sema's anti-obesity effects. Either Sema monotherapy or Sema-butyrate co-administration elevated the number of c-Fos-positive cells in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) of the hypothalamus. By contrast, DR decreased PVN c-Fos-positive cell number. Butyrate amplified Sema-elicited activation of PVN neuronal activity. Plasma metabolomics revealed limited overlap between the pharmacological interventions and DR, demonstrating orthogonal metabolic responses.

Conclusions

These findings identify the Sema-butyrate combination as a promising anti-obesity strategy, and demonstrate that Sema and DR exert divergent effects on both hypothalamic neuronal activity and plasma metabolite levels.

papers.title: The contribution of PLCB1 and VDR gene variants to susceptibility of central precocious puberty in Hubei Han Chinese girls: Integrating case-control evidence with meta-analysis.
papers.abstract:
Introduction

Central precocious puberty (CPP) is a prevalent pediatric endocrine disorder resulting from the premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis. PLCB1 acts downstream of the KISS1/GPR54 signaling pathway to mediate gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) secretion, a key event in pubertal initiation. Moreover, VDR is widely expressed in breast tissue, modulates glandular development, and low serum vitamin D levels have been associated with an elevated risk of CPP. This research aimed to investigate the association between genetic variants in the PLCB1 and VDR genes and CPP susceptibility in Hubei Han Chinese girls.

Methods

A total of 384 CPP girls and 422 healthy girls from Hubei province were enrolled in this case-control study, which targeted three PLCB1 gene variants (rs932491, rs2235613, rs708910) and three VDR gene variants (rs731236, rs7975232, rs1544410). A comprehensive meta-analysis integrating this study and existing literature was subsequently conducted.

Results

For the rs708910, the A allele and AA genotype were identified as protective factors against CPP risk. For the rs7975232, the C allele and CC genotype were significantly associated with a reduced risk of CPP. The subsequent meta-analysis confirmed that both rs708910 and rs7975232 were robustly linked to CPP susceptibility in the Chinese population.

Conclusion

The PLCB1 gene rs708910 and VDR gene rs7975232 may represent potential risk-associated variants for CPP in Han Chinese girls. These findings warrant validation in future large-scale, multi-ethnic cohort studies.

papers.title: The PVN-to-MeA Oxytocinergic Pathway Encodes Social Relationship-Dependent Consolation Behavior in Mandarin Voles.
papers.abstract: Consolation behavior is defined as an increase in affiliative contact toward a distressed individual and is associated with the physical and emotional well-being of social species. Allogrooming a distressed individual represents a primary form of consolation behavior and is considered as a complex type of empathy. However, the neural mechanisms underlying allogrooming remain poorly understood. In this study, using adult male and female monogamous mandarin voles (Lasiopodomys mandarinus, approximately three-month-old), we demonstrate that individuals exhibited significantly more allogrooming toward a defeated same-sex littermate than toward a defeated stranger, indicating effects of familiarity on consolation. Social interaction with a defeated cagemate elicited more activity of paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVN) neurons, medial amygdala (MeA) and PVN oxytocin (OT) neurons compared to interaction with a stranger male. Using cholera toxin subunit B (CTB) as a retrograde tracer, we confirmed that PVN OT neurons project to the MeA. Fiber photometry recording revealed that the activity of both PVN OT neurons projecting to MeA and OTR-expressing neurons in the MeA was significantly elevated during allogrooming a defeated cagemate. Furthermore, in both male and female voles, overexpression of oxytocin receptor (OTR) mRNA in the MeA increased allogrooming time toward a defeated stranger, whereas interference of OTR mRNA expression in the MeA significantly reduced allogrooming toward a defeated cagemate. These findings demonstrate that mandarin voles display different levels of allogrooming toward distressed siblings or strangers and reveal a critical role for the PVN-to-MeA oxytocinergic pathway in encoding and modulating allogrooming behavior.

papers.title: Short-term outcomes of mini-thoracotomy, multiportal video-assisted thoracic surgery, and multiportal robot-assisted thoracic surgery for complex segmentectomy.
papers.abstract: This study examined the association of surgical approach with operative and postoperative outcomes as well as margin and nodal outcomes after complex segmentectomy, comparing mini-thoracotomy (MT) with multiportal minimally invasive thoracic surgery (mMITS) and, within mMITS, video-assisted thoracic surgery (mVATS) with multiportal robot-assisted thoracic surgery (mRATS), using propensity score matching (PSM). The study cohort comprised 808 consecutive patients treated with complex segmentectomy for suspected malignant pulmonary tumors from January 2015 through July 2026. Of these, 138 underwent MT and 670 mMITS, including 605 mVATS and 65 mRATS. PSM (1:2) was performed for MT versus mMITS (n = 126 vs. 252) and mVATS versus mRATS (n = 126 vs. 63). We assessed operative outcomes, postoperative complications, pain-related outcomes only for the mVATS-mRATS comparison, and margin and nodal outcomes. Blood loss was lower with mMITS than with MT (5 vs. 20 mL, p < 0.001), and chest tube duration was shorter (p = 0.002). Margin and nodal outcomes did not differ significantly between MT and mMITS. mRATS was associated with less blood loss than mVATS (3 vs. 5 mL, p = 0.006), a shorter duration of regular oral analgesic use (20 vs. 31 days, p = 0.007), and greater hilar and mediastinal lymph node yields (hilar, p = 0.037; mediastinal, p = 0.025). For complex segmentectomy, mMITS was associated with less blood loss and shorter chest tube duration than MT, without significant differences in margin and nodal outcomes. Within mMITS, mRATS was associated with shorter regular oral analgesic use and greater hilar and mediastinal lymph node yields than mVATS.

papers.abstract: Goblet cell adenocarcinoma (GCA) is a rare appendiceal neoplasm that typically metastasizes to the peritoneum and pelvic organs, with no reported gastric involvement. We report a 72-year-old man with multiple comorbidities presenting with recurrent small bowel obstruction. Imaging revealed a cecal and a gastric mass; colonoscopy confirmed poorly differentiated right-sided adenocarcinoma. Surgical resection with intraoperative biopsies identified high-grade appendiceal GCA infiltrating the cecum, mesentery, and gastric wall. Immunohistochemical staining showed cytokeratin 7 negativity and cytokeratin 20 positivity, suggesting an appendiceal origin. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration of the gastric lesion confirmed gastric metastasis, demonstrating identical morphology and immunoprofile, thus expanding the metastatic spectrum of GCA.

papers.title: Robotic resection of cardiac papillary fibroelastoma guided by three-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography: a case report.
papers.abstract: Heart neoplasms are classified as primary or secondary, with primary tumors considered rare. Cardiac papillary fibroelastoma is the second most common benign cardiac tumor. It has distinct morphological features and carries a potential risk of embolization; therefore, surgical excision is generally recommended. The use of three-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography (3D TEE) enables improved characterization of the suspected lesion, provides a detailed anatomical assessment, and assists in intraoperative planning and management. We report the case of a patient diagnosed with a cardiac papillary fibroelastoma of the mitral valve who underwentrobotic-assisted surgery guided by 3D TEE.

papers.title: Association of Prophylactic Abdominal Drain Placement With Short-Term Postoperative Outcomes After Hepatectomy: A Nationwide Inpatient Database Study in Japan.
papers.abstract:
Aim

Although randomized trials have discouraged routine prophylactic abdominal drainage after uncomplicated hepatectomy, these drains are still widely used in clinical practice. This study evaluated the association between prophylactic abdominal drain placement and short-term outcomes after hepatic resection using a nationwide inpatient database.

Methods

We identified patients who underwent initial hepatic resection for liver tumors from the Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination database. Patients were classified into drain and no-drain groups according to whether a prophylactic abdominal drain was placed intraoperatively. In-hospital outcomes were compared using propensity score overlap weighting. Subgroup analyses were performed for intra-abdominal infection and in-hospital mortality.

Results

Among 73 613 eligible patients, 62 934 (85.5%) received prophylactic abdominal drains. After overlap weighting, the incidence of intra-abdominal infection did not differ significantly between the drain and no-drain groups (5.1% vs. 5.5%; risk difference, -0.3%; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.8 to 0.1). Bile leakage, postoperative transfusion, postoperative drainage, and hospitalization costs were also comparable between groups. In contrast, prophylactic drain placement was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (0.5% vs. 1.0%; risk difference, -0.6%; 95% CI, -0.8 to -0.4). Subgroup analyses showed that this association was more evident in patients with low body mass index and those treated at low- or middle-volume hospitals.

Conclusion

Prophylactic abdominal drain placement after hepatic resection was not associated with a lower incidence of intra-abdominal infection.

MicroRNAs and polymorphisms influencing MICA immune modulation.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs that play a central role in post-transcriptional gene regulation. They act mainly by interacting with sequences located in the 3' untranslated regions (3'UTRs) of messenger RNAs (mRNAs), thereby influencing mRNA stability and translation. Through these mechanisms, miRNAs contribute to the fine-tuning of multiple biological pathways, including immune activation, inflammatory signaling, and cellular stress responses. Among the genes involved in immune surveillance, the major histocompatibility complex class I polypeptide-related sequence A (MICA) has emerged as an important target for post-transcriptional regulation due to its role as a ligand for the activating receptor NKG2D (natural killer cell group 2-D), which is expressed in natural killer (NK) cells and cytotoxic T lymphocytes. MICA is highly polymorphic, and several allelic variants differ in sequence composition, structural organization, and expression patterns, potentially influencing miRNA-mRNA interactions. Growing evidence suggests that miRNA-mediated regulation of MICA contributes to immune modulation in cancer, viral infections, and autoimmune disorders, particularly through mechanisms associated with immune evasion and altered NKG2D signaling. In addition, genetic polymorphisms and structural variations within regulatory regions, especially within the 3'UTR, can alter miRNA binding affinity by creating, disrupting, or modifying target sites. This mini review discusses the current understanding of miRNA-mediated regulation of MICA, emphasizing the impact of allelic diversity and regulatory polymorphisms on post-transcriptional control. Furthermore, it highlights current knowledge gaps and future perspectives regarding allele-specific regulation.

Multiply recurrent pituitary apoplexy treated nonsurgically: illustrative case.
papers.abstract:
Background

Pituitary apoplexy is rare clinical entity resulting from hemorrhage or infarction of a pituitary tumor, typically presenting with headaches, endocrinopathy, and variable neurological manifestations. Recurrent apoplexy, particularly multiply recurrent cases, is exceedingly rare and associated with clinical equipoise in many cases.

Observations

The authors report the case of an 85-year-old female who presented with three distinct episodes of pituitary apoplexy over 6 years, each presenting with acute headache in the absence of neurological deficits. Given the patient's age, lack of neurological symptoms, and personal preference, she did not undergo surgical intervention and was treated with only hormone replacement for hypopituitarism after the second episode.

Lessons

This case highlights that nonsurgical management may be successful in carefully selected cases of pituitary apoplexy, although the risk of recurrence is an important consideration that is often overlooked in cases presenting with mild symptoms. The authors suggest that upfront surgery may be considered in younger patients, even in the setting of mild presentations that do not require emergency intervention, to avoid the potential morbidity of recurrent apoplexy. Better predictors of apoplexy recurrence will be helpful to develop increasingly personalized management strategies for these patients. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26461.

MZF1 Inhibits TGFβ-1/SMAD Signaling by Transcriptionally Activating SnoN to Augment Tumorigenic Potential in Colon Cancer.
papers.abstract: Colon cancer progression is associated with transcriptional and signaling abnormalities. MZF1, linked to leukemogenesis, has an unclear role in colon cancer. This study examined its function in colon tumorigenesis and signaling-targeted therapies. Multi-omics (RNA-seq, CUT&Tag) identified MZF1 targets, validated in vitro/in vivo using xenografts and epithelial-specific MZF1 knockout mice. Virtual screening found MZF1 inhibitors. MZF1 activated SnoN transcription, suppressing TGF-β/SMAD signaling. Overexpression enhanced proliferation and colony formation; knockdown reversed these. In vivo, MZF1-overexpressing xenografts grew faster with more Ki67+ cells, while MZF1<sup>-/-</sup> mice had reduced tumor burden. Organoids from MZF1<sup>-/-</sup> mice grew poorly. 10Panx Acetate, an MZF1 inhibitor, disrupted MZF1-SnoN interaction, inhibiting cell and xenograft growth. Our results indicate MZF1 as a key colon cancer regulator via SnoN-mediated TGF-β pathway suppression and suggest 10Panx Acetate for precision therapy. MZF1/SnoN co-expression may predict aggressive disease.

Characterization of therapeutic antibodies targeting lymphatic and vascular resistance factor for the treatment of hypervascularized and highly metastatic cancers.
papers.abstract: Angiogenesis is a major driver of tumor progression and a validated therapeutic target in highly vascularized cancers such as clear cell renal cell carcinoma. However, the clinical benefit of antivascular endothelial growth factor therapies is limited by the emergence of resistance. We identified a vascular endothelial growth factor A splice variant, termed Lymphatic and Vascular Resistance Factor (LVRF), which promotes both angiogenesis and lymphangiogenesis and is upregulated following anti-angiogenic treatment. To therapeutically target this pathway, we generated fully human monoclonal antibodies against LVRF. Lead antibodies displayed high specificity and nanomolar affinity and effectively inhibited LVRF-driven biological activities. Anti-LVRF antibodies reduced renal carcinoma cell invasion, inhibited vascular and lymphatic endothelial responses, and suppressed lymphatic endothelial cell sprouting. In vivo, treatment significantly reduced the growth of bevacizumab-resistant renal carcinoma xenografts, induced regression of blood and lymphatic vessels, and decreased metastatic dissemination in zebrafish models. These findings identify LVRF as a mediator of resistance to anti-angiogenic therapy and support therapeutic targeting of LVRF as a novel strategy for vascularized tumors resistant to current antivascular endothelial growth factor treatments.

papers.title: Tumor-antigen-specific polyclonal antibodies suppress tumor growth and metastasis in heterogeneous solid tumors
Thymic hyperplasia in patients with acromegaly: imaging-based assessment and clinical implications.
papers.abstract:
Objective

We aimed to compare thymus visibility and volume in patients with acromegaly to those of controls, and to evaluate the correlation between growth hormone (GH), insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) levels, and thymus volume.

Subjects and methods

This cross-sectional case-control study included 66 patients with acromegaly who underwent thoracic computed tomography scans. An age- and sex-matched control group of 65 trauma patients without comorbidities was selected. All thoracic computed tomography scans were reassessed to measure thymus volume using imaging software. Comparisons of thymus volume and assessment of correlation with GH and IGF-1 levels were performed.

Results

The acromegaly group (28F/38M) and the control group (27F/38M) had similar sex and age distributions. The thymus was more frequently detectable in the acromegaly group (80.3%) compared to controls (44.6%; p = 0.001). Thymus volume was significantly higher in the acromegaly group (13.1 cm3 [9.7-18.7]) than in the control (10.3 cm3 [4.6-12.3]; p = 0.013). Serum IGF-1 levels were nearly significantly higher in acromegalic patients with a visible thymus compared to those without (visible thymus: 608.5 ng/mL [377.6-921.8]; non-visible thymus: 440.5 ng/mL [201.5-596]; p = 0.054). However, no significant differences were found in GH and IGF-1 upper limit of normal levels. No correlation was found between thymus volume and other parameters.

Conclusion

Patients with acromegaly have larger and more frequently visible thymus glands than controls. When a mass is detected in the anterior mediastinum, acromegaly should be considered, especially before invasive procedures.

papers.title: In Silico Prediction of Bioactive Peptides From <i>Lactococcus lactis</i> SwR14: Evaluation of a Potential Probiotic Candidate.
papers.abstract: Lactic acid bacteria (LABs) are widely recognized for their nutritional and therapeutic potential, primarily due to their ability to produce bioactive peptides during fermentation. In this study, Lactococcus lactis strains, potential probiotics from Sui Wu'u, a traditional fermented meat from Bajawa, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, were evaluated for folate biosynthesis, cholesterol-lowering activity, α-glucosidase inhibition, and antioxidant capacity, and their association with bioactive peptide production in milk was investigated. Among the isolates, SwR14 and SwR16 were able to grow under folate-depleted conditions, indicating folate autotrophy, with SwR14 producing the highest extracellular folate concentration in folate-free medium (12.40 ng/mL). All isolates exhibited moderate in vitro cholesterol reduction (14.28%-20.94%) and α-glucosidase inhibitory activity (25.94%-33.96%), with no significant interstrain differences. Antioxidant activity assessed using DPPH, ABTS, and FRAP assays showed assay-dependent variability, with SwR14 demonstrating the most efficient DPPH radical scavenging activity based on the lowest IC50 value. Peptides from milk fermented by L. lactis SwR14 were then identified via liquid chromatography-high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS/MS) and profiled using the BIOPEP-UWM database, revealing 49 peptide sequences with 47 distinct biological activities. ACE and DPP-IV inhibitory activities were detected in all sequences, whereas α-glucosidase inhibitory and antioxidant activities were predicted in 33 and 31 sequences, respectively, consistent with the in vitro results. Several peptide sequences emerged as promising candidates for antioxidant and α-glucosidase inhibitory activity on the basis of their molecular weight and hydrophobic amino acid composition, suggesting that milk fermentation by L. lactis SwR14 promotes bioactive peptide generation despite its weak proteolytic phenotype. These findings highlight L. lactis SwR14 as a promising functional strain for the development of bioactive peptide-enriched dairy products. Future studies should explore peptide bioactivity mechanisms and validate their efficacy through in vivo studies.

Intensivists' Perspectives and Practices on Palliative Care in the ICU: A Nationwide Survey in Korea.
papers.abstract:
Background

While many countries have made progress in integrating palliative care into intensive care units (ICUs), implementation remains highly context-dependent. In Korea, palliative care integration within ICUs remains limited, and intensivists' perspectives on its role and applicability have not been well studied.

Methods

We conducted a nationwide, cross-sectional online survey of certified intensivists and fellows registered with the Korean Society of Critical Care Medicine between April and May 2024. The questionnaire explored knowledge and confidence in palliative care, current ICU practices, referral patterns, perceived barriers, and preferred strategies for integration.

Results

A total of 241 intensivists responded (response rate, 23.9%). Most agreed that palliative care should be incorporated into ICU care (97.1%) and were willing to make referrals (98.3%). Advance care planning, symptom management, and family decision-making were the most expected domains of support. However, fewer reported involvement in psychological support, end-of-life care, or bereavement services. Referral practices were more frequent in institutions with palliative care teams, while lack of resources, unsupportive institutional culture, and unclear processes were commonly cited barriers. Clinical guidelines, professional education, and reimbursement reform were identified as priority strategies for integration.

Conclusion

Korean intensivists widely recognize the need for palliative care in the ICU but apply it within a limited scope. To strengthen integration, consensus on definitions, clear referral criteria, and supportive institutional and policy frameworks are required.

Advancing Early Breast Cancer Diagnosis and Ki-67 Expression Prediction With Ultrasound Viscoelastography: Based on Peritumoral Assessment.
papers.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most common invasive malignancy in women. Ultrasound viscoelastography may improve non-invasive diagnosis, but the clinical relevance of peritumoral viscoelastic parameters (VPs) and their correlation with Ki-67 remain unclear. This study explores these associations.

Methods

A prospective study enrolled 256 breast masses (156 malignant, 100 benign). Patients underwent conventional ultrasound and viscoelastography. VPs were acquired within masses (A), peritumoral shells (Shell1: 1 mm, Shell2: 2 mm, Shell3: 3 mm), and combined regions (A' = A + Shell). Quantitative metrics included elasticity (V/1 E, V/0 E), dispersion coefficient (V/1 D), viscosity coefficient (V/0 V), and their maximum (Max), minimum (Min), mean(Mean), and standard deviation (SD) values. Diagnostic performance was evaluated by analyzing the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and calculating the area under the curve (AUC), followed by logistic regression. VPs were compared between high/low Ki-67 groups.

Results

The AUCs of peritumoral VPs exceeded those from masses. V/1 D showed higher AUC than V/0 V and elasticity values, with Shell3 V/1 D SD having the highest AUC (0.840). The diagnostic efficacy of the peritumoral viscoelastic model surpassed that of the single elasticity parameter model, with 89.1% sensitivity, 73% specificity, 82.8% accuracy. Key variables included Shell3 V/1 D and Shell3 V/0 E. Shell1 V/0 V Max was significantly higher in high versus low Ki-67 expression groups (p < 0.05).

Conclusion

The viscoelastic model improves diagnostic accuracy by quantifying peritumoral biomechanics, and certain VPs may predict Ki-67 expression. Peritumoral VPs show potential as novel non-invasive imaging biomarkers for early breast cancer evaluation.

papers.title: HECTD1 Directs HIF-1α to Facilitate Intestinal Inflammation and Carcinogenesis via Promoting Th17 Differentiation and Glycolysis.
papers.abstract: Targeting glucose metabolism in Th17 cells may be beneficial for treating inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and colitis-associated cancer (CAC), however, the molecular mechanisms orchestrating Th17 cell metabolism remain unclear. Here, we revealed that HECTD1 regulates IGF2BP3-dependent HIF-1α translation to promote Th17 cell glycolysis and differentiation and that HECTD1 expression correlates with IBD and CAC pathogenesis. T-cell-specific deletion of HECTD1 mitigated the severity of colitis and CAC in murine models. RNA-seq revealed enrichment of Th17 differentiation, glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, and HIF-1 signaling pathways among differentially expressed genes between HECTD1-sufficient and HECTD1-deficient CD4<sup>+</sup> T cells. Consistently, loss of HECTD1 suppressed Th17 cell differentiation both in vitro and in vivo, and suppressed glycolytic metabolism and HIF-1α activity, revealing the mechanism underlying its protective effects against IBD and CAC. Mechanistically, HECTD1 potentiates m<sup>6</sup>A-based HIF-1α translation by mediating IGF2BP3 K63-linked ubiquitination to promote the binding of IGF2BP3 with the translation initiation machinery of Hif1a mRNA. Reciprocally, HIF-1α acts as a key transcription factor that promotes Hectd1 gene expression, establishing a distinct positive feedback loop. Our findings highlight a self-reinforcing feedback mechanism in which HECTD1 and HIF-1α engage in mutual regulation to dictate Th17 cell fate and metabolic reprogramming, providing novel potential IBD and CAC treatments targeting HECTD1.

Matrix metalloproteinase-guided targeting of vesicular stomatitis virus to tumors following systemic administration.
papers.abstract: The lack of tumor-specific targeting by oncolytic viruses (OVs) restricts their therapeutic potential. Here, we report a "cap-linker" strategy to modify the vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) glycoprotein (G protein, VSV-G<sup>IN</sup>). The modified VSV (Pro-VSV<sup>IN</sup>) loses its ability to infect cells until present in the tumor microenvironment, where the linker is cleaved by tumor-enriched matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs). When Pro-VSV<sup>IN</sup> is armed with a single-chain IL-12 (Pro-VSV<sup>IN</sup>-IL-12) and systemically injected into MC38 tumor-bearing mice, Pro-VSV<sup>IN</sup>-IL-12 eradicates established tumors while avoiding systemic toxicity, and elicits long-term anti-tumor immune memory. Systemic administration of Pro-VSV<sup>IN</sup>-IL-12 also markedly inhibits the growth of metastatic cancers in the lung. The efficacy of Pro-VSV<sup>IN</sup>-IL-12 was further improved when combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade. Compared to WT VSV<sup>IN</sup> that carries IL-12, intravenously injected Pro-VSV<sup>IN</sup>-IL-12 leads to strong Th1 immunity, near abolishment of regulatory T cells, and potent CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell activation and clonal expansion in tumors. This preclinical work demonstrates a new tumor-specific targeting strategy of VSV for enhanced immunotherapy safety with superior efficacy.

papers.title: Distinct Clinicogenomic Contexts of BRAF-Altered Gliomas and Glioneuronal Tumors: A Nationwide Real-World Study.
papers.abstract: BRAF alterations occur across diverse gliomas and glioneuronal tumors, but their alteration-specific clinicogenomic contexts in real-world cancer genomic profiling cohorts remain incompletely characterized. We analyzed BRAF-altered brain tumors registered in the Japanese Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics database from June 2019 to March 2026. Operational diagnostic harmonization was performed using available clinicopathological and genomic information. Grade-stratified analyses focused on BRAF p.V600E-positive gliomas and glioneuronal tumors. Among 413 BRAF-altered brain tumors, 344 were classified as gliomas and glioneuronal tumors after harmonization. Within this cohort, the major alteration contexts included BRAF p.V600E-positive tumors (n = 166), KIAA1549::BRAF fusion-positive tumors (n = 60), amplification-only tumors (n = 15), and tumors with other BRAF alterations (n = 109), with overlap in a subset. KIAA1549::BRAF fusion-positive tumors were mainly associated with low-grade glioma contexts, particularly pilocytic astrocytoma. Amplification-only tumors showed marked enrichment of MET alterations, all representing MET amplification, together with frequent EGFR and TP53 co-alterations, supporting a receptor tyrosine kinase-amplified, copy-number-rich context. Among 118 grade-evaluable BRAF p.V600E-positive gliomas and glioneuronal tumors, CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion and TP53/ATRX alterations were enriched in higher-grade groups, and high-grade tumors showed increased tumor mutational burden, although hypermutator phenotypes were rare. BRAF alteration classes define distinct clinicogenomic contexts in gliomas and glioneuronal tumors. These findings highlight both the opportunities and methodological challenges of nationwide real-world cancer genomic profiling datasets in central nervous system tumor research.

Incidence of intra-axial brain metastases in Eastern Finland.
papers.abstract:
Purpose

Brain metastases (BM) incidence and characteristics remain poorly defined due to registry data being often incomplete, recording only primary tumors or unspecified metastases. The objective of this study was to examine BM incidence rates and characteristics confirmed by MRI in North Savo, Finland.

Methods

In this retrospective study, North Savo residents with first MRI diagnosis of BM between 1 January 2004 and 31 December 2023 were identified through the radiology information system, irrespective of primary cancer diagnosis date. Medical and histopathological records were reviewed. Population person-years were estimated by summing annual end-year counts of all North Savo residents obtained from Statistics Finland. Crude incidence rates and age-standardized incidence rates (ASIRs), standardized to the 2013 European Standard population, were calculated. Temporal trends were assessed using age-adjusted Poisson regression.

Results

Among 516 patients, 474 had histopathological verification. Cancers originating from lung and breast tissue accounted for 56.8% of BM cases. Overall crude incidence was 10.22 (95% CI 9.36-11.15) and ASIR was 9.20 (95% CI 8.42-10.04) per 100,000 person years. ASIR increased from 5.8 in 2004-2008 to 11.8 in 2019-2023. Age-adjusted Poisson regression estimated a 24% increase in incidence per five-year period (incidence rate ratio 1.24; 95% CI 1.14-1.34; P < 0.001). Age-specific incidence peaked at 33.1 per 100,000 person years among patients aged 70-74 years.

Conclusions

MRI-confirmed BM incidence increased over 20 years, despite age standardization. Incidence was highest among older adults. These findings provide contemporary population-based epidemiological data of BM incidence.

papers.title: Fibrinogen Alpha Chain (FGA) Associates With Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition, Stemness, and the USP-Catenin Complex in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract:
Background

Colorectal cancer (CRC) progression is heavily driven by epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and the acquisition of cancer stem cell (CSC) properties. Elucidating the specific molecular drivers and dynamic indicators underlying these processes is crucial for advancing CRC management.

Methods

The clinical significance and diagnostic value of fibrinogen alpha chain (FGA) were evaluated using TCGA data, immunohistochemistry (IHC), and paired pre- and postoperative serum samples. The biological functions of FGA were assessed in HCT116 cells through Transwell and 3D spheroid formation assays. Immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry (IP-MS) and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analyses were utilized to uncover the underlying molecular mechanisms.

Results

FGA mRNA and protein are significantly upregulated in CRC tissues, and preliminary data indicate elevated serum FGA in CRC patients. Clinically, aberrant FGA expression correlates with tumor histological type, lymphatic invasion, and poor survival outcomes. In vitro, FGA overexpression is associated with the downregulation of E-cadherin, upregulation of mesenchymal markers (Vimentin, ZEB1, Snail), and increased cell migration and spheroid formation. Mechanistically, IP-MS identified a potential PPI network wherein FGA associates with ubiquitin-specific proteases (USP7, USP10) and the catenin complex (β-catenin, p120-catenin), suggesting a potential role in mediating pro-stemness signaling.

Conclusion

These findings suggest that FGA may contribute to CRC plasticity by modulating EMT and stem-like properties in vitro. Furthermore, its dynamic postoperative reduction warrants further investigation to determine its utility for non-invasive tumor monitoring.

papers.title: Surgical Treatment of Tumor-Induced Osteomalacia With Causative Tumors Affecting the Long Bones.
papers.abstract:
Background

The causative tumor for tumor-induced osteomalacia (TIO) locating in the long bone is hidden and has diverse locations, resulting in great challenges to orthopedists. This study aimed to investigate and summarize the clinical features and surgical outcomes of TIO patients with culprit tumors involving the long bones to enhance clinical understanding and improve orthopedic surgical management of this rare disease.

Methods

A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of TIO patients with causative tumors located in the long bones who underwent surgery by the Orthopedic Bone and Soft Tissue Tumor Sub-specialty Group at our hospital between January 2013 and January 2023. This article described the clinical symptoms, location of causative tumors, tumor sizes, and other clinical features of TIO patients, and analyzed the trend of changes in blood phosphorus levels before and after surgery and pathological results. At the same time, clinical surgical experience and strategies for TIO patients with culprit tumors located in long bones were summarized.

Results

All 49 patients included in the study had been pathologically confirmed and met clinical diagnostic criteria for TIO. All patients experienced bone pain (49/49), often accompanied by limited mobility, fatigue, difficulty turning over, and difficulty sitting up or walking. Importantly, 65.3% (32/49) experienced height loss during disease progression. A total of 65 operations were performed on these 49 patients, with culprit tumors located in the humerus (five cases), femur (33 cases), tibia (seven cases), fibula (three cases), and foot (one case). Twenty-nine cases involved skeletal lesions, seven cases affecting the periosteum (outside-in), while 13 showed both bone and soft tissue involvement. Following the final orthopedic procedure, serum phosphorus levels increased in 45 patients, and the median follow-up duration was 45 months (interquartile range, 28-61 months; range, 2-215 months). Nine patients showed no remission after the first orthopedic surgery, and five experienced recurrence. One patient was diagnosed with a malignant culprit tumor.

Conclusion

Surgical planning for TIO with long bone involvement should account for the anatomical location and extent of the causative tumor. Currently, no standardized surgical strategy exists for this rare condition. Recurrence, non-remission, or malignant transformation remains possible due to incomplete resection or local relapse. Based on the single center experience of this case series, we summarized the surgical classification and feasible surgical strategies for TIO's orthopedic surgery with causative tumors located in the long bones. The actual clinical application effect of this classification system needs further clinical data verification.

Domain-aligned self-supervision: CT-specialized DINOv3 enhances PET/CT tumor segmentation.
papers.abstract: Objective.This study investigates how domain-aligned self-supervised pretraining influences downstream PET/CT tumor segmentation, with a focus on disentangling the roles of domain proximity and pretraining dataset scale.Approach.We compared nnU-Net segmentation models initialized from random weights or from DINOv3 encoders pretrained on natural images, x-ray mammography, CT, or PET, using datasets of different sizes. To disentangle the effects of pretraining domain and dataset size, CT-DINOv3 encoders were pretrained using different numbers of 2D CT slices, including subsets matched in size to the pretraining datasets from other domains. Models were evaluated on two PET/CT benchmarks, autoPET (whole-body, FDG/prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)) and HECKTOR (head-and-neck primary tumors and metastatic lymph nodes), using five-fold cross-validation with frozen encoders.Main results.CT-pretrained models achieved the highest Dice scores for lymph nodes, FDG lesions, and PSMA lesions. For primary tumors, PET pretraining produced the highest observed Dice score, followed by CT pretraining, suggesting the potential benefit of in-domain representations when PET data are sufficient. Notably, PET pretraining exceeded size-matched CT pretraining for PSMA but remained below models pretrained on larger CT datasets for both PSMA and FDG targets. In contrast, natural-image pretraining did not outperform from-scratch training despite its much larger pretraining scale, indicating that scale alone is insufficient when domain proximity is low. Across comparisons, strong transfer reflected the combination of domain proximity and sufficient pretraining scale, especially for CT-based models with broad data availability.Significance.These results demonstrate that both domain proximity and dataset scale jointly determine the effectiveness of self-supervised pretraining. While higher domain alignment improves performance at comparable scale, sufficient data is required to realize this benefit. CT-based pretraining provides a favorable balance between domain relevance and data availability, leading to robust performance across tasks. This study provides practical guidance for selecting pretraining strategies in PET/CT segmentation.

papers.title: Perivascular spaces are associated with T cell trafficking and may have prognostic relevance in brain metastases.
papers.abstract:
Background

Perivascular structures, in particular, perivascular spaces (PVS) are emerging key immune modulators in the tumor microenvironment. However, their relationship with immune infiltration, vascular remodeling, and clinical outcomes in brain metastases is unclear.

Methods

In this retrospective two-center study, we analyzed 56 brain metastases. Perivascular spaces were graded on preoperatively T2-weighted MRI in the basal ganglia and centrum semiovale. Tumor immune infiltration, vascular features, and immune cell phenotypes were assessed by immunohistochemistry and spectral flow cytometry and correlated with clinical outcome.

Results

Here we show that high PVS burden in the centrum semiovale region, but not in the basal ganglia, were significantly associated with improved overall survival. High PVS are linked to increased presence of tumor-infiltrating cytotoxic T cells-most of which exhibited an activated/exhausted phenotype, indicated by PD-1- and Fas-positivity-was likewise prognostically favorable. Moreover, these cells showed elevated expression of the migration marker CXCR3, as well as Granzyme B/IFNγ consistent with effector polarization. High PVS were additionally associated with a higher M1/M2-like macrophage ratio, which showed similar prognostic relevance as high vascular density, suggesting enhanced blood supply and immune cell recruitment.

Conclusion

These findings could establish PVS as a non-invasive imaging marker of anti-tumor immunity and prognosis in patients with brain metastasis, underscoring their potential as biomarkers for immune activity and therapeutic monitoring.

papers.title: Dysregulated AKT signaling reprograms osteosarcoma to drive selective reliance on EP300.
papers.abstract: Cancers depend on transcriptional control to maintain the malignant cell state. EP300 and CBP are paralogous master epigenetic enzymes that control normal and malignant transcription. Using a cancer-wide integrative chemical-genetic analysis, we demonstrate enhanced dependency on EP300, compared with CBP, in cell lines from most cancer lineages, including lethal osteosarcoma (OS). Using a selective EP300 degrader (JQAD1), we identify that a genetically defined subgroup of OS with dysregulation of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway is genetically and chemically sensitive to loss of EP300. Activated AKT promotes sensitivity to JQAD1, driven by relocalization of EP300, CBP and H3K27ac to genetic subtype-enriched dependency loci. AKT inhibition combines with JQAD1 to synergistically suppress the growth of AKT-dysregulated OS cells in vitro and in orthotopic xenografts. These observations extend across >850 cancer cell lines, where synergy is predicted by elevated protein synthetic rates. These findings reveal determinants of EP300 degrader function in OS and provide a foundation for co-targeting EP300 and AKT in cancers with enhanced protein translation.

papers.title: PRAME Augments K63-Linked Ubiquitination and Stabilization of METTL3 to Promote Lung Adenocarcinoma Metastasis.
papers.abstract: Metastasis is the primary cause of mortality in cancer including lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Preferentially expressed antigen of melanoma (PRAME), a cancer-testis antigen, displays context-dependent functions across malignancies, but its biological role in LUAD metastasis has not been clearly defined. Here, we demonstrate that the significantly upregulated PRAME in metastatic LUAD directly interacts with the m6A methyltransferase METTL3 and promotes its K63-linked non-proteolytic ubiquitination. This modification occurs at lysine 235 of METTL3, increases its protein stability and facilitates METTL3 interaction with METTL14 and WTAP. Consequently, m6A modification of TGFB2 mRNA and activation of the TGF-β signaling pathway are enhanced, which is essential for PRAME-driven pro-metastatic effects both in vitro and in vivo. Clinically, PRAME expression positively correlates with METTL3 protein abundance and TGF-β pathway activation, and is robustly associated with poor clinical outcomes. Taken together, our findings identify K63-linked ubiquitination as a previously unrecognized post-translational modification of METTL3 and underscore the importance of the PRAME/METTL3/TGF-β axis in LUAD metastasis, providing mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets for this malignancy.

papers.title: Tubocapsenolide A Overcomes Oxaliplatin Resistance in Colorectal Cancer by Targeting PLK1 to Impair CEP55-ESCRT-Associated Vesicular Damage Clearance.
papers.abstract: Oxaliplatin (L-OHP) is a first-line chemotherapeutic agent for advanced colorectal cancer (CRC) and postoperative adjuvant therapy. However, acquired L-OHP resistance remains a clinical obstacle. Here, we identify Tubocapsenolide A (TA), a natural withanolide isolated from Tubocapsicum anomalum, as a promising antitumor agent that suppresses CRC growth and sensitizes L-OHP-resistant CRC to L-OHP. Using a PROTAC-based target deconvolution strategy, we identify PLK1 as a direct molecular target of TA. PLK1 is elevated in L-OHP-resistant CRC and is associated with reduced patient sensitivity to L-OHP. Mechanistically, elevated PLK1 promotes CEP55 Ser436 phosphorylation and facilitates ESCRT recruitment to nuclear and mitochondrial budding sites. This process facilitates the clearance of L-OHP-induced damaged components through nuclear budding and TOM20<sup>-</sup>/PDH<sup>+</sup> mitochondrial-derived vesicles, thereby contributing to organelle homeostasis and cell survival. By inhibiting PLK1, TA interferes with this vesicle-associated damage clearance process, leading to intracellular accumulation of damaged components. This damage accumulation is accompanied by nucleolar stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, ultimately contributing to cell death. Collectively, our findings identify a previously unappreciated role of the PLK1-CEP55-ESCRT axis in vesicle-associated damage clearance during L-OHP resistance and support this axis as a potential therapeutic target. TA represents a promising lead compound for overcoming L-OHP resistance in CRC.

Oncogenic mutations in non-small cell lung cancer: from molecular mechanisms to clinical practice.
papers.abstract: Targeted therapy has revolutionized the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients harboring oncogenic alterations, and next-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) significantly increase blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, leading to improved disease control and survival benefits. However, several issues remain to be addressed, including the selection of more appropriate and individualized agents, the emergence of TKI resistance, and the challenging management of central nervous system (CNS) progression. In this review, we comprehensively summarize the efficacy and safety of TKIs and targeted specific antibodies in advanced or metastatic patients with common or rare mutations, providing guidance in selecting the optimal agent. We further explore the mechanisms underlying drug resistance and regimens aimed at overcoming resistance. In nonmetastatic resectable or unresectable NSCLC, we discuss the therapeutic potential of targeted agents and current issues requiring further research. In addition, we distinguish current and potential therapeutic strategies for patients with baseline brain metastasis (BM) and those without baseline BM who subsequently develop brain progression, leading to more effective and personalized treatment. Finally, we provide perspectives on challenges and future directions in the identification and treatment of oncogenic alterations, particularly in the context of co-mutations and the heterogeneous nature of metastases, and emphasize the clinical importance of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted genetic testing and biomarker development.

papers.title: New and emerging pharmacological treatment options for acromegaly: a 2026 update.
papers.abstract:
Introduction

Acromegaly is associated with significant morbidity, impaired quality of life (QoL), and increased mortality when uncontrolled. While current treatments achieve biochemical control in many patients, a substantial proportion remain uncontrolled or experience persistent treatment-related burdens, highlighting a need for safer, more effective, and convenient therapeutic alternatives.

Areas covered

This narrative review examines current treatment modalities, the growing role of precision medicine and biomarker-guided algorithms, and newly approved or emerging pharmacological options. A comprehensive literature search was performed in Pubmed database for articles in English, including the following terms: 'acromegaly AND new treatments,' acromegaly AND new drugs," 'acromegaly AND CAM2029,' 'acromegaly AND paltusotine,' 'acromegaly AND debio4126,' 'acromegaly AND CAM4071,' 'acromegaly AND MAR002,' 'acromegaly AND HTL0030310,' 'acromegaly AND Hu-13H02m,' 'acromegaly AND biomarkers,' 'acromegaly AND precision medicine,' 'acromegaly AND personalized treatment.' This review highlights innovations such as long-acting subcutaneous octreotide depots (CAM2029), oral selective somatostatin receptor type 2 agonists (paltusotine), extended-interval formulations (Debio 4126), subcutaneous pasireotide depots (CAM4071), allosteric growth hormone receptor antagonists (MAR002), and direct growth hormone-neutralizing antibodies.

Expert opinion

Integrating personalized medicine approaches with novel pharmacological agents offering greater convenience and distinct mechanisms of action holds significant promise for overcoming current treatment limitations, optimize biochemical control, and enhance patient well-being.

papers.title: Clinicopathological Characteristics and Recurrence Patterns of Olfactory Neuroblastoma: A 15-Year Tertiary Center Case Series.
papers.abstract:
Objectives

Olfactory neuroblastoma (ONB) is a rare malignant tumor of the sinonasal tract with heterogeneous clinical behavior and recurrence potential. Due to its low incidence, prognostic factors and optimal treatment strategies remain incompletely defined. The objective of this study was to describe the clinicopathological characteristics, treatment approaches, and recurrence patterns of ONB over a 15-year period at a tertiary referral center.

Methods

A retrospective case series and literature review were performed. Medical records of nine patients with histologically confirmed ONB treated between 2007 and 2022 were reviewed. Demographic characteristics, presenting symptoms, imaging findings, Hyams histologic grade, treatment modalities, and follow-up outcomes were analyzed. Diagnosis in every case rested on characteristic morphology together with a full neuroendocrine immunohistochemical panel, and Hyams grade was assigned on the definitive resection specimen. Variables that were not uniformly documented across the 15-year archive-clinical stage, surgical margin status and the anatomical compartment of recurrence-were deliberately not imputed and are reported as unavailable.

Results

Patients ranged in age from 18 to 61 years (mean 41.3 ± 12.4 years; median 42 years), with a male predominance (6/9, 66.7%). The most common presenting symptoms were nasal congestion, headache, and nasal mass. All patients underwent surgical resection with curative intent, predominantly through endoscopic endonasal approaches, followed by adjuvant chemoradiotherapy. Within a uniform, protocol-defined posttreatment observation window of 3 years (median follow-up 36 months), tumor recurrence occurred in 4 of 9 patients (44.4%), and 5 of 9 patients (55.6%) remained free of documented recurrence. Recurrence was observed across different Hyams grades, including grade I tumors, without a statistically significant association between histologic grade, age, or gender and recurrence.

Conclusions

ONB demonstrates variable clinical presentation and recurrence patterns, even following multimodal treatment. Histologic grade alone may not reliably predict recurrence in small cohorts. Recurrence despite low-grade histology and uniformly administered chemoradiotherapy supports grade-, stage-, and margin-adapted rather than uniform adjuvant strategies, and structured surveillance continued well beyond 5 years.

papers.title: Cancer metastasis: biological mechanisms, therapeutic bottlenecks, and emerging interventions.
papers.abstract: Metastatic cancer remains a major clinical challenge, which is driven by the continuous adaptation of disseminated tumor cells to diverse tissue environments and therapeutic pressures. Although current treatments, including conventional therapies, small-molecule drugs, antibody-drug conjugates, and immunotherapies, have improved clinical outcomes in selected patients, they rarely achieve durable disease control, largely because each stage of the metastatic cascade presents distinct therapeutic bottlenecks. This review examines these bottlenecks and identifies therapeutic vulnerabilities that can be targeted at each metastatic stage. Cross-stage adaptive programs, encompassing genetic, epigenetic, metabolic, immune, and microenvironmental alterations, are linked to the specific modes of therapeutic failure they drive, thereby connecting underlying mechanisms with their corresponding clinical consequences. Emerging therapeutic strategies are discussed in the context of the metastatic stage, and general design principles for combination regimens are proposed. We also highlight the potential of liquid biopsy-guided dynamic treatment adjustment and advanced preclinical models to inform patient selection, treatment timing, and the design of therapies aimed at overcoming resistance. By integrating metastatic biology, mechanisms of therapeutic failure, and emerging interventions, this review provides a framework for understanding and targeting the bottlenecks that limit durable disease control in metastatic cancer.

Neuropathic Pain Comorbid Cognitive Impairment and Vitamin D: A Narrative Review From Mechanisms to Clinical Management.
papers.abstract: Neuropathic pain (NP) is not merely simple persistent pain but a complex pathological condition mediated by dysregulation across multiple systems, including the neuro-immune-endocrine axis. As a high-intensity endogenous stressor, persistent pain signals can deplete cognitive resources and trigger neuroinflammation and central sensitization, leading to cognitive impairment (CI) characterized by attention deficits and impaired working memory. Currently, mainstream pharmacological treatments for NP carry risks of addiction and may exacerbate CI. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop synergistic intervention strategies that address both pain management and cognitive protection. Given that NP and CI share multiple pathological pathways, identifying interventions capable of simultaneously targeting multiple mechanisms has become a research hotspot. Vitamin D, a secosteroid hormone with both neuroprotective and immunoregulatory functions, is closely associated with an increased risk of NP and CI when deficient. Existing evidence suggests that Vitamin D may regulate the shared pathological mechanisms of these two diseases through multiple pathways, thus serving as a potential adjunctive strategy worthy of further investigation to alleviate the intertwined vicious cycle between NP and CI. This paper systematically reviews the shared pathological mechanisms between NP and CI, summarizes the latest research progress, and explores the multi-target mechanisms of Vitamin D in intervening in NP-CI comorbidity, aiming to promote the application of this safe and cost-effective nutritional strategy in dietary supplementations for NP-CI comorbidity.

Dietary context and ethanol-related injury in preclinical models: A contemporary systematic review of predominantly obesogenic diets and liver outcomes.
papers.abstract: Diet composition is an important food-derived exposure that may influence alcohol-related tissue injury. However, evidence on how specific dietary contexts modify ethanol-induced injury and its underlying biological mechanisms in controlled preclinical models remains fragmented. This systematic review examined whether defined dietary patterns modify ethanol-related injury in controlled mammalian studies. Following PRISMA 2020, PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published from January 2021 to January 15, 2026. Eligible studies were controlled in vivo mammalian experiments comparing ethanol exposure under defined dietary patterns. Evidence was narratively synthesized by diet type, organ system, and mechanism; random-effects meta-analyses and prespecified interaction analyses were conducted when sufficiently comparable data were available. Twenty-seven studies met the inclusion criteria (24 mouse and three rat studies); 18 used male-only animals, most examined high-fat or Western-type diets, and liver outcomes predominated. Evidence for non-obesogenic diets was limited to one ketogenic-diet study. In acute high-fat-diet models, adding ethanol increased serum ALT (SMD 2.31, 95% CI 1.46-3.16), AST (SMD 1.18, 95% CI 0.54-1.81), and hepatic triglycerides (SMD 2.06, 95% CI 0.96-3.17). Acute interaction analysis identified dietary effect modification only for ALT (MD 74.56, 95% CI 59.03-90.10), while chronic analyses showed a negative interaction for hepatic triglycerides (MD -0.048, 95% CI -0.092 to -0.004; P = 0.03). Extrahepatic, microbiome, and multi-omics findings were sparse and heterogeneous. High-fat and Western-type diets generally exacerbated ethanol-induced hepatic injury, whereas evidence for other dietary patterns remains limited.

trials.title: Real World Positioning of Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors (TKIs) Within Systemic Treatment Strategies for Advanced Neuroendocrine Tumors (NETs)
trials.conds: Well-Differentiated Neuroendocrine Tumors (NETs)
trials.brief:
Well differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are rare and heterogeneous malignancies that frequently evolve toward advanced or metastatic disease, requiring long-term systemic treatment strategies delivered over multiple lines. Their management is complex and influenced by tumor-related factors-including primary site and grade-as well as disease burden, functional status, patient comorbidities, and access to available therapeutic options. As a result, real-world treatment pathways in advanced NETs are highly diverse.

In recent years, the systemic treatment landscape of advanced NETs has expanded beyond somatostatin analogues (SSA), peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT), and chemotherapy to include targeted therapies. Among these, multitarget tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) targeting tumor angiogenesis have progressively been incorporated into clinical practice. Their use varies according to tumor subtype, disease dynamics, prior treatments, and patient-related considerations, reflecting the absence of standardized sequencing algorithms.

In routine clinical practice, the choice and sequencing of TKIs are driven by individualized clinical decision-making rather than predefined treatment pathways. Their positioning within systemic treatment strategies is influenced by anticipated benefit, tolerability, prior toxicities, and practical constraints such as regulatory indications, access, and reimbursement conditions, which differ by tumor origin. Consequently, the real-world positioning of TKIs within treatment sequences remains insufficiently characterized at a national level.

"SEQUENCE-NET" is an ambispective observational study designed to prospectively document how TKIs are integrated into systemic treatment strategies for advanced pancreatic and extra-pancreatic NETs in routine clinical practice within the ENDOCAN-RENATEN network.

trials.brief:
Background:

Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is the deadliest form of lung cancer. Extrapulmonary neuroendocrine cancer (EPNEC) is a similar type of cancer that develops anywhere other than the lungs. EPNEC is also deadly. B7-H3 is a protein often found in SCLC and EPNEC tumor cells. Researchers can modify a person s own T cells, or immune cells, to target B7-H3. When these modified T cells are returned to the body-a treatment called B7-H3 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy-they may help kill cancer cells.

Objective:

To test B7-H3 CAR T cell therapy in people with SCLC or EPNEC.

Eligibility:

People aged 18 years and older with SCLC or EPNEC that either did not respond or returned after treatment.

Design:

Participants will be screened. They will have blood tests and tests of their heart function. They will have imaging scans.

Participants will undergo apheresis: Blood will be taken from the body through a needle. The blood will pass through a machine that separates out the T cells. The remaining blood will be returned to the body through a different needle. The collected T cells will be altered to make them attack cells with B7-H3.

Participants will be in the hospital for at least 15 days. They will receive chemotherapy drugs to prepare their body for the treatment. These drugs will be given through a tube attached to a needle inserted into a vein.

The modified T cells will be infused through a vein. Participants will remain in the hospital until they are well enough to go home.

Follow-up visits will continue for 15 years....

trials.brief:
Background:

High-grade neuroendocrine carcinomas (HGNEC) are cancers that develop in different parts of the body, including the digestive tract, genitals, neck, and head. One drug (belinostat), combined with 2 other drugs (etoposide and cisplatin), is approved to treat HGNEC. But some people may have a gene variant that affects how quickly their body gets rid of the drug; these people may do better with different dosages of belinostat.

Objective:

To test higher or lower doses of belinostat based on gene variants in people with HGNEC.

Eligibility:

People aged 18 years and older with HGNEC.

Design:

Participants will be screened. They will have a physical exam with blood tests. Some blood will be used for genetic testing. They will have imaging scans and a test of their heart function. Samples of tumor tissue may be collected.

All 3 study drugs (belinostat, etoposide, cisplatin) are given through a tube attached to a needle inserted into a vein. Treatment will be given in 21-day cycles.

For cycles 1 through 6: Participants will come to the clinic for the first 4 days. They will be given all 3 drugs. Imaging scans and other tests will be repeated. Each visit will last 4 to 8 hours.

After cycle 6: Participants may continue treatment with belinostat alone. They will come to the clinic for the first 3 days of each cycle. They may continue treatment for up to 5 years if the drug is helping them.

Participants will have a follow-up visit 30 days after their last dose of belinostat. Then they will receive follow-up visits by phone or email every 3 to 6 months.

trials.brief: This phase I trial tests the safety, side effects, and best dose of sunitinib malate in combination with lutetium Lu 177 dotatate in treating patients with pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. Sunitinib malate is in a class of medications called kinase inhibitors and a form of targeted therapy that blocks the action of abnormal proteins called VEGFRs that signal tumor cells to multiply. This helps stop or slow the spread of tumor cells. Radioactive drugs, such as lutetium Lu 177 dotatate, may carry radiation directly to tumor cells and not harm normal cells. It is also a form of targeted therapy because it works by attaching itself to specific molecules (receptors) on the surface of tumor cells, known as somatostatin receptors, so that radiation can be delivered directly to the tumor cells and kill them. Giving sunitinib malate and lutetium Lu 177 dotatate in combination may be safer and more effective in treating pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors than giving either drug alone.

Temozolomide and capecitabine are considered chemotherapy drugs. Temozolomide is in a class of medications called alkylating agents. It damages the cell's deoxyribonucleic acid and may kill cancer cells. Capecitabine is in a class of medications called antimetabolites. It is taken up by cancer cells and breaks down into fluorouracil, a substance that kills cancer cells. Lutetium Lu 177-dotate is a radioactive drug. It binds to a protein called somatostatin receptor, which is found on some neuroendocrine tumor cells. Lutetium Lu 177-dotatate, builds up in these cells and gives off radiation that may kill them. It is a type of radioconjugate and a type of somatostatin analog. trials.title: Cardiovascular Complications After Adrenalectomy for Pheochromocytoma and Non-secreting Tumors
trials.conds: Pheochromocytoma; Cardiovascular Complication; Adrenal Incidentaloma
trials.brief:
Pheochromocytoma is an adrenomedullary chromaffin cell tumour that releases catecholamines. Adverse cardiovascular events are considered the main cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with pheochromocytoma. Consequently, preoperative medical preparations using alpha-blockers or other antihypertensive drugs and the control of hemodynamic instability during adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma are recommended by guidelines to prevent vasoconstriction, perioperative cardiovascular complications, and the risk of death. However, the definition of a catecholamine-induced hypertensive crisis in patients with pheochromocytoma has only recently been validated by an international consortium as the occurrence of systolic/diastolic blood pressure \>180/120 mmHg1. Limitations of published studies include small sample sizes, and single institution analysis. Some studies have reported substantial variability in the management of pheochromocytomas, with the use of routine preoperative medical preparation varying from 49% to 100%, whereas others have questioned the utility of this preparation for postoperative cardiovascular complications. The aim of this study was to evaluate pan-European practices in terms of specific preoperative medical preparation before surgery and to identify risk factors for postoperative cardiovascular complications 30 days after adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma and non-secreting tumors (indication for surgery = " excluding malignancy ").

The EUROCRINE® registry offers a valuable opportunity to assess clinical practices for preoperative medical preparation and the morbidity linked to adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma and non-secreting tumors. This prospective study aims to refine surgical protocols and inform updates to existing guidelines, thereby advancing the management of adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma.

trials.brief:
Background:

The NCI Surgery Branch has developed an experimental therapy that involves taking white blood cells from patients' tumors, growing them in the laboratory in large numbers, and then giving the cells back to the patient. These cells are called Tumor Infiltrating Lymphocytes, or TIL and we have given this type of treatment to over 200 patients with melanoma. Researchers want to know if TIL shrink s tumors in people with digestive tract, urothelial, breast, or ovarian/endometrial cancers. In this study, we are selecting a specific subset of white blood cells from the tumor that we think are the most effective in fighting tumors and will use only these cells in making the tumor fighting cells.

Objective:

The purpose of this study is to see if these specifically selected tumor fighting cells can cause digestive tract, urothelial, breast, or ovarian/endometrial tumors to shrink and to see if this treatment is safe.

Eligibility:

\- Adults age 18-72 with upper or lower gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary, genitourinary, breast, ovarian/endometrial cancer, or glioblastoma refractory to standard chemotherapy.

Design:

Work up stage: Patients will be seen as an outpatient at the NIH clinical Center and undergo a history and physical examination, scans, x-rays, lab tests, and other tests as needed.

Surgery: If the patients meet all of the requirements for the study they will undergo surgery to remove a tumor that can be used to grow the TIL product.

Leukapheresis: Patients may undergo leukapheresis to obtain additional white blood cells. (Leukapheresis is a common procedure, which removes only the white blood cells from the patient.)

Treatment: Once their cells have grown, the patients will be admitted to the hospital for the conditioning chemotherapy, the TIL cells and aldesleukin. They will stay in the hospital for about 4 weeks for the treatment.

Follow up: Patients will return to the clinic for a physical exam, review of side effects, lab tests, and scans about every 1-3 months for the first year, and then every 6 months to 1 year as long as their tumors are shrinking. Follow up visits will take up to 2 days.

trials.title: Tissue Procurement and Natural History Study of Neuroendocrine Neoplasms (NENs) Including Adrenocortical Carcinoma (ACC)
trials.conds: Neuroendocrine Tumors; Carcinoma, Neuroendocrine
trials.brief:
Background:

Neuroendocrine neoplasm (NENs)are rare cancers arising from the neuroendocrine cells and can affect almost any part of the body. They vary from low grade neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) to high grade neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs). These tumors often occur in the gastrointestinal tract, pancreas, lungs, adrenal medulla (pheochromocytomas) or adrenal cortex (adrenocortical cancer) and other areas of the body mentioned below:

* Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NET): stomach, duodenum, pancreas, colon, appendix, etc.
* Liver and gallbladder
* Adrenal tumors
* Pituitary gland
* Thyroid gland: medullary thyroid carcinoma
* Parathyroid tumors
* Pulmonary neuroendocrine tumors: typical and atypical carcinoid, small cell lung cancer (SCLC), large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC)
* Extrapulmonary small cell cancer
* Peripheral nervous system tumors: paraganglioma, neuroblastoma)
* Breast and genitourinary tract

Their rates are rising in the United States and worldwide. Researchers want to learn more about NENs through this natural history study.

Objective:

To study the natural history of people with NENs and obtain samples from them to learn more about the disease. The clinical management of all NETs is not standardized, with only a few FDA-approved therapies and we would like to learn which combination therapeutic approach should be used, how long treatment should be continued, and in what subgroup of NENs a particular treatment option should be used.

Eligibility:

People aged 18 and older who have or are suspected to have NENs or ACC.

Design:

Participants will be screened with a medical history.

Participants will have a physical exam. Their symptoms and their ability to perform their normal activities will be reviewed. They will have blood and urine tests.

Participants will receive recommendations for managing their disease and potential treatment options. They will be able to ask as many questions as they would like.

Participants may provide saliva and blood, a for research. They will give tumor samples from a previous surgery or biopsy.

Participants may have optional biopsies. During biopsies, cancer tissue will be obtained using a needle and syringe. Tissue will be taken from the liver, lung, or a lymph node. Participants may have an imaging scan or ultrasound to help locate the tumor or area to be biopsied. They will receive local anesthesia and may be sedated.

Participants will complete a questionnaire about their family medical history.

Participants will have follow-up visits every 12 months. They will have physical exams and give samples. If their health changes, they may have extra visits. If they cannot visit NIH, they (or their doctor) will be contacted by phone or email.

Participants will take part in the study for all their life.

trials.title: Evaluating the Addition of the Immunotherapy Drug Atezolizumab to Standard Chemotherapy Treatment for Advanced or Metastatic Neuroendocrine Carcinomas That Originate Outside the Lung
trials.conds: Advanced Extrapulmonary Neuroendocrine Carcinoma; Metastatic Extrapulmonary Neuroendocrine Carcinoma; Recurrent Extrapulmonary Neuroendocrine Carcinoma; Unresectable Extrapulmonary Neuroendocrine Carcinoma
trials.brief: This phase II/III trial compares the effect of immunotherapy with atezolizumab in combination with standard chemotherapy with a platinum drug (cisplatin or carboplatin) and etoposide versus standard therapy alone for the treatment of poorly differentiated extrapulmonary (originated outside the lung) neuroendocrine cancer that may have spread from where it first started to nearby tissue, lymph nodes, or distant parts of the body (advanced) or that has spread from where it first started (primary site) to other places in the body (metastatic). The other aim of this trial is to compare using atezolizumab just at the beginning of treatment versus continuing it beyond the initial treatment. Immunotherapy with monoclonal antibodies, such as atezolizumab, may help the body's immune system attack the cancer, and may interfere with the ability of tumor cells to grow and spread. Cisplatin and carboplatin are in a class of medications known as platinum-containing compounds that work by killing, stopping or slowing the growth of cancer cells. Etoposide is in a class of medications known as podophyllotoxin derivatives. It blocks a certain enzyme needed for cell division and DNA repair, and it may kill cancer cells. Giving atezolizumab in combination with a platinum drug (cisplatin or carboplatin) and etoposide may work better in treating patients with poorly differentiated extrapulmonary neuroendocrine cancer compared to standard therapy with a platinum drug (cisplatin or carboplatin) and etoposide alone.

trials.conds: Gastrointestinal Neuroendocrine Carcinoma; Adjuvant Treatment; Resection
trials.brief: Patients with pathologically-confirmed gastrointestinal neuroendocrine carcinoma will be enrolled, to explore the efficacy and safety of oxaliplatin-based doublet chemotherapy in the adjuvant treatment of gastrointestinal neuroendocrine carcinoma. For patients after radical resection, adjuvant chemotherapy is recommended. XELOX, SOX or FOLFOX regimens can be selected based on the patient's physical status. Single-agent chemotherapy alone is not recommended.

trials.title: Cabozantinib in High Grade Neuroendocrine Neoplasms

trials.interventions: Cabozantinib; Blood for plasma biomarkers; Tissue biopsy
trials.brief: High grade neuroendocrine neoplasm patients are treated with platinum doublets such as carboplatin and etoposide mimicking the current guidelines for small cell lung cancer (SCLC). Unfortunately, recurrences are common and most patients with metastatic disease succumb to it within a year. There is no extensive literature or consensus on second- or third-line options (which include FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, capecitabine and temozolomide, taxanes or immunotherapy) and there is urgent need for better regimens.
